note: Visual audit of the 141 quadruped-routed mammals AFTER waves 4-6. Each judged by an agent that opened the portrait. headUnique answers Nick's standing complaint directly.

rows.readsAs: A pale dun pony or a small horse with a plumed tail — the leg length, level barrel and long blunt face all read equine, not canid.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on two of three. (a) 'Large pointed erect ears' are absent — there is one small dark rounded lobe at the top-rear of the skull, the identical ear part used on the Jaguar, Kinkajou, Leopard and Lion. (b) The muzzle is a broad blunt wedge, not a slender fox-like snout; it is wider at the tip than at the stop. Only the tail passes, and it reads as a horse's plume rather than a bushy brush — the white tip is correct for a fox, but the jackal's tip is BLACK, so even the pass is the wrong species' cue. HEAD: fully generic — identical cranium dome, identical single round white eye with a black pupil set high and far forward, identical dark nose dot; swap it with the Kinkajou head and nobody could tell. SEAMS: hard elliptical boundary around the haunch oval where it sits on the torso, and a visible chevron line where the neck wedge overlaps the shoulder; both fore and hind legs are capsules that terminate in a hard rim against the barrel rather than merging into it. COAT: floating — the barrel carries flat polygonal facets plus horizontal banded striation that reads as planking/woodgrain, running straight across the form instead of wrapping the round solid, and the lighter shoulder/haunch patches have hard edges instead of a form shadow.
rows.fix: Replace the shared ear lobe with a tall triangular erect ear (height ~0.45 of skull length, base wide, tip sharp) with a dark rear face and lit inner cup. Narrow the muzzle: taper it to a point, drop the tip below the eye line, add a shallow stop. Blacken the tail tip. Kill the horizontal striation on the barrel and drive coat value from the body normal so the flank darkens toward the belly and the ventral silhouette edge. Dissolve the haunch and shoulder ellipses into gradients with no closed outline, and blend the neck-to-shoulder join over ~8-10 px instead of butting two shapes.

rows.readsAs: A spotted yellow dog or a hyena — leggy, narrow-chested, splattered with ink.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on all three. (a) 'Stocky muscular build on short legs' — the legs are long, thin and straight, and the chest is shallow; body-to-leg ratio is the same as the Jackal's and the Kinkajou's. (b) 'Rosettes with spots inside them' — the markings are solid black splatter clusters at flat uniform opacity with no ring structure and no central spot; several read as inkblots or paw prints. (c) 'Massive broad blocky jaw' — the jaw is the same narrow wedge muzzle worn by every other profile animal in this batch; there is no mandible mass, no cheek, no widened zygomatic. HEAD: fully generic and swappable with the Leopard's and the Jackal's. SEAMS: same closed-ellipse haunch, same hard rim where each leg capsule meets the torso, same neck/shoulder overlap line. COAT: floating — the spots sit at constant size and constant opacity across the whole flank, do not compress or foreshorten toward the silhouette edge, and are unaffected by the body's shading, so they read as stickers on a lit shape rather than pigment in fur.
rows.fix: Rebuild the marking as a true rosette: a broken ring of 4-6 dark petals with a mid-tone interior and one or two small dark centre spots, then scale the ring down and crowd it toward the spine and the limbs. Multiply rosette opacity by the surface shading so they darken in the belly shadow and compress near the silhouette. Shorten the legs by ~20% and thicken them, deepen the chest, and drop the belly line. Give the skull a genuinely blocky jaw: widen the muzzle to at least the cranium width, square the chin, add a heavy cheek mass below the eye.

rows.readsAs: A small tan dog or a young deer — nothing about it suggests an arboreal procyonid.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on all three. (a) 'Long prehensile tail thick at the base' — the tail is a thin even-width curl no thicker at the root than at the tip and shorter than the torso; nothing indicates grasp. (b) 'Round teddy-bear face with huge dark eyes' — the face is the same long wedge muzzle as the Jackal's, and despite eyes:prominent in the row the eye rendered is a single small round bead the same size as the Jaguar's. This is the single clearest case in the batch of the owner's complaint: the head is not merely similar to its neighbours, it is the wrong head entirely. (c) 'Golden-brown woolly fur' — the coat is flat tan with the same horizontal barrel striation as the Jackal, no wool, no pile, no soft silhouette. SEAMS: closed haunch ellipse, hard leg-to-torso rims, neck overlap line. COAT: floating, same faceted planking as the rest of the profile set.
rows.fix: Swap in a short-faced skull: cranium dominant, muzzle no longer than a third of head length, forehead round, small round ears set LOW and to the side of the skull. Enlarge the eye to roughly 2x the current diameter, make the iris dark and fill most of the aperture, and set both eyes forward-facing. Thicken the tail root to near limb thickness, run it longer than the body, and curl the distal third into a grip. Replace the flat fill with a woolly coat — short overlapping clumped strokes that soften the silhouette — and let it darken along the belly.

rows.readsAs: A koala. This one is recognisable at a glance and is the only picture in the batch that names its own species.
rows.defect: All three mustReads pass: the huge round fluffy ears are there and correctly sized, the large spoon-shaped black nose dominates the face, there is no tail and the animal is astride a vertical trunk. The head is genuinely unique in this batch — frontal, ear-dominant, tiny beady eyes — and could not be swapped with anything else here. What holds it back: (a) the coat does not lie on the body — it is a corona of straight white needle-like spikes projecting OUTSIDE the silhouette on the ears, cheeks, shoulders and flanks, reading as porcupine quills or frost rather than dense grey pile, and none of those strands are shaded by the form underneath. (b) The body beneath is an undifferentiated blob — no shoulder, no haunch, no limb articulation; the arms are vague pale grey smudges. (c) It is not actually gripping: no paws, no digits, no claws close on the trunk, so it reads as pasted in front of the trunk rather than clinging to it, and the trunk passes behind with no contact shadow or fur compression. (d) Coat hue is lavender-purple rather than the ash grey the species reads by. (e) Both eyes sit high and wide with white sclera showing, which googles the expression.
rows.fix: Replace the outward spikes with short dense clumped fur strokes that stay inside or barely break the silhouette, and shade each clump by the body form so the flanks go darker than the chest. Desaturate the purple toward neutral ash grey with a warm cream chest. Build actual forelimbs: two arms wrapping the trunk with visible dark curved claws over the near edge of the bark, plus a contact shadow on the trunk and fur pressed flat where it meets. Shrink the sclera so the eyes read as small dark beads.

rows.readsAs: A stilt-legged antelope or a hybrid horse-antelope with a zebra-striped neck and a burnt patch on its shoulder.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on two of three. (a) 'Enormous rounded satellite-dish ears' are entirely ABSENT — there is no ear anywhere on the skull; the single most distinctive feature of the animal after the horns is missing. (b) 'Six to ten thin white vertical stripes on the flank' — the stripes rendered are DARK BROWN, not white, and they are in the wrong two places: horizontal banding across the NECK (which reads as zebra) and a hard-edged dark radial starburst on the shoulder that reads as a palm frond, a scorch mark or a paint splatter rather than flank striping. The flank proper is bare. (c) The horns pass only weakly — they are two wavy ribbons that undulate in the picture plane; a corkscrew needs the spiral to twist AROUND the horn axis with the ridge crossing the silhouette, and none of that reads here. HEAD: generic. Cover the horns and it is the same wedge muzzle, same single round white bead eye, same cranium as the Jackal. The horns are props sitting on the standard skull, not a kudu skull. SEAMS: the shoulder starburst has a hard clipped edge that ignores the body form entirely, the haunch is again a closed ellipse, and the leg capsules meet the torso at visible rims. COAT: floating on both counts above.
rows.fix: Add the ears: two large rounded paddles set wide and low behind the eye, each nearly as long as the face, with a pale inner cup. Move the stripes to the flank, run them VERTICAL from spine to belly, make them thin and PALE against the grey-fawn coat, and curve each one to follow the barrel's cross-section. Delete the shoulder starburst and the neck banding. Rebuild the horns as a swept helix — two to two-and-a-half turns, keel visible where it crosses the silhouette, tips diverging — and add a throat mane/dewlap fringe. Narrow and lengthen the face and set the eye further back.

rows.readsAs: A spotted yellow dog — and specifically the same spotted yellow dog as the Jaguar two rows up.
rows.defect: Indistinguishable from the Jaguar in this same batch: same silhouette, same leg length and stance, same tawny fill, same head, same splatter markings. That alone is a blocker, and it defeats the reference note, which exists precisely to separate these two. mustRead FAILS on all three. (a) 'Long thick tail nearly as long as the body' — the tail is a short thin upward curl roughly a third of body length, thinner than a leg. (b) 'Hollow ring rosettes with empty centres' — the marks are solid filled black clusters with no ring and no open centre, identical in construction to the Jaguar's, so the one feature that distinguishes the two species has been rendered the same way on both. (c) 'Low-slung slender body' — the body is carried high on long straight legs with a shallow chest; there is no low-slung line. HEAD: fully generic; interchangeable with the Jaguar, Jackal and Kinkajou. SEAMS: closed haunch ellipse, hard leg-to-torso rims, neck/shoulder overlap line. COAT: floating — spots at constant opacity and constant scale, unshaded by the body, not compressed toward the silhouette edge.
rows.fix: Make the rosette hollow: a broken ring of dark petals over an unmodified coat centre, explicitly NO centre spot, and hold that contrast against the Jaguar's filled version so the two are readable side by side. Run the tail to at least 0.9 of body length, thicken it to near limb diameter, and let it trail low with a lazy curve. Drop the body: shorten the legs, deepen and lower the chest, put the shoulder blade above the spine line. Then differentiate the two cats structurally as well — leopard skull narrower and smaller relative to the body, jaguar's markedly heavier.

rows.readsAs: A lion — but only because of the mane. Mask the mane and it is the Jackal.
rows.defect: The mustReads technically pass: mane present and large, a dark club at the tail tip, plain tawny coat, back roughly level. But the mane is doing all of the work, and it is an appliqué — a scalloped radial fan pasted over the shoulder with a hard closed outline against the torso, sitting in front of the body rather than growing from the neck; you can trace an unbroken seam where the fan's edge crosses the shoulder and the throat. HEAD: generic. Underneath the mane it is the same cranium dome, same single small dark ear lobe, same large round white eye with the pupil set high and forward, same narrow wedge muzzle used on every other profile animal in this batch. A lion's head must read as broad, flat-topped and short-faced with a heavy muzzle; this one is a jackal's head with a collar. SEAMS: the closed haunch ellipse and hard leg-to-torso rims are present as on the rest of the set. COAT: the barrel shows the same flat polygonal facets and horizontal banded striation as the Jackal — it reads as planking, not as short fur on a muscled solid. The tail tuft is a smooth rounded blob with a hard edge rather than a hair tuft.
rows.fix: Grow the mane out of the neck: strand clumps rooted at the nape and throat, irregular outer edge, individual locks overlapping the shoulder with no closed boundary, and darker where it tucks under the jaw. Rebuild the skull broad and short — widen the cranium, flatten the top, shorten and deepen the muzzle, move the eye back and set it lower, and use the small low rounded ear rather than the shared lobe. Remove the horizontal striation from the barrel and shade the coat off the body normal. Break the tail tuft into hair strands with a ragged edge.

rows.readsAs: A dark grey ram or sheep — short-coupled woolly body on four thin hoofed sticks, with a Roman-nosed head and a big round ear disc. Nobody would say 'bear'.
rows.defect: Not one mustRead lands. No tan muzzle (the whole face is one flat charcoal mask, muzzle included). Rump is NOT higher than the shoulders — the topline is flat, with the neck/withers as the highest point, i.e. the opposite of the note. Ears are not tall and rounded, they are a single dark filled circle stamped flat on the skull. Short curved claws are absent entirely: the feet are dark HOOF caps, which is a category error for a bear and contradicts the claim of a per-family foot type. HEAD is the batch's generic head — rounded cranium, downward-hooked snout with a dark nose bead, one white-ringed eye with a black pupil at a fixed spot; swap it onto the Brown Bear or Bull and no one would notice. SEAM: a hard-edged diagonal boundary runs down from the withers to the chest where the darker neck/shoulder plate overlaps the pale torso — the neck is laid on top of the body, not grown from it. COAT: the pale flank is two soft ellipse blobs (shoulder, haunch) plus a dark hip disc that sit over the silhouette rather than being shaded by it; the fine hatching is a uniform overlay that ignores the belly curve.
rows.fix: Give it a genuine plantigrade bear foot — broad flat sole, five short curved claws — and kill the hoof for the whole ursid family. Rebuild the skull as a straight-profile bear head: long straight bridge, a distinct TAN muzzle wedge separated in value from the black mask, and tall rounded ears set wide and low on the cranium, drawn as an outlined ear with an inner bowl rather than a filled disc. Raise the sacrum so the hindquarters read as the high point and drop the withers. Dissolve the neck/shoulder overlap into a single continuous torso silhouette with the value change gradient-blended across it, and multiply the coat hatching by the body's own form shading so it wraps the barrel instead of tiling it.

rows.readsAs: A spotted fawn or a young deer — long hoofed legs, dappled tan coat, small deer-like head. Reads as a cervid, not a cat, at any distance.
rows.defect: Missing mustReads: no cheek ruff at all — the jawline is a smooth taper with nothing framing it; the small dark shapes on the crown are generic pointed ear caps, not black tufts rising off an ear tip. The tail requirement is the only one half-met: there is a dark rounded lump at the rump that can be read as a stub, but it reads more as another coat spot than as a tail. Fatal category error: the animal stands on four thin HOOFED stilts — a felid must have short, thick, digitigrade legs on padded paws, and the leg length here is deer proportion, not cat. The spotting is deer-fawn dapple (scattered round blobs across back and flank) rather than bobcat's broken bars and rosettes on the limbs. HEAD is the batch-generic head at a smaller scale — same rounded cranium, same hooked muzzle with nose bead, same single ringed eye; there is no short broad cat skull, no wide-set forward eyes, no blunt short muzzle. SEAM: hard line where the neck plate meets the shoulder, same overlap artifact as the rest of the batch. COAT: spots float — they are uniform opaque dots at the same value everywhere, including on the shadowed underbelly and inside the leg shadow, so they clearly are not being shaded by the surface they sit on.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a felid rig: halve the leg length, thicken them, and put it on four padded digitigrade paws with visible toe pads. Rebuild the skull short and broad — wide zygomatic cheeks, blunt muzzle less than a third of head length, two forward-facing eyes visible in profile, and a flared ruff of side whiskers breaking the jaw silhouette. Draw the ears as triangles with an outlined tip and a discrete black tuft spike above it. Give the tail a defined short cylinder with a black tip clearly separated from the coat, not a blob. Convert the dapple to broken bars/rosettes and multiply spot opacity by the underlying form shading so the belly and inner legs go dark with the body.

rows.readsAs: A striped antelope — kudu or bushbuck. The only picture in the batch a stranger would name to the right family.
rows.defect: Coat colour and horns are right, the stripes are wrong in the way that matters. mustRead calls for ten or more vertical WHITE stripes; the render has roughly seven DARK brown stripes, and on the shoulder they have merged into one solid dark slab that reads as a saddle blanket or a shadow rather than as striping. The white chevron between the eyes is absent — the face carries only a thin dark line and the generic eye ring. The horns are pale and spiralled, which is correct in character, but they sweep UP and FORWARD from the poll rather than being heavily backswept over the neck. SEAM: the horn bases sit on top of a dark ear/poll patch with a hard edge, and the same shoulder/neck overlap boundary present batch-wide is visible here running from withers to brisket. COAT: the stripes are flat opaque shapes that do not wrap — they stay full-strength as they cross onto the shaded underside of the barrel and terminate in straight cut edges at the belly rather than curving around the ribcage. HEAD is genuinely the most differentiated in the batch: elongated antelope muzzle, higher-set eye, real horn structure — this one could not be swapped for the Bull's without notice.
rows.fix: Invert the stripe value to white/cream and raise the count to 11-13 thin stripes, spaced so none touch; the slab on the shoulder must be broken back into discrete stripes. Curve each stripe along the barrel's cross-section and multiply it by the body's form shading so it darkens under the belly. Add the white facial chevron as a distinct V between the eyes and white cheek spots. Rake the horns back over the shoulders and blend the horn base into the skull with a short pedicle rather than butting it against the ear patch. Blend the neck/shoulder value break.

rows.readsAs: A tan sheep or a capybara on stilts. Same animal as the Black Bear with the palette changed.
rows.defect: The single diagnostic mustRead — the muscular shoulder hump making the front the tallest point — is entirely absent; the topline is flat-to-slightly-domed at MID-back, and the shoulder is no higher than the hip. The face is convex and sheep-like, the exact opposite of the required dished concave profile with a broad forehead, and there is no forehead mass at all. Long straight pale digging claws are absent: the feet are dark HOOF caps, wrong family and wrong order. HEAD is the batch-generic head — identical construction to the Black Bear (rounded cranium, hooked snout, dark nose bead, one white-ringed eye, one filled dark ear disc); place the two side by side and only the hue differs, which is the owner's complaint reproduced verbatim inside a single batch. SEAM: a hard-edged plate boundary where the darker neck/shoulder mass overlaps the pale torso, visible as a continuous line from withers to chest; the head also butts the neck with a value step rather than a transition. COAT: two large soft ellipses (shoulder ball, haunch ball) and a dark hip patch sit over the flank as separate decals; the hatching runs at one uniform density across belly, flank and back, so it does not describe the barrel.
rows.fix: Build the hump as actual TOPLINE geometry over the scapulae so the profile peaks at the withers and slopes down to a lower rump — it must change the silhouette, not be a shading trick. Rebuild the skull with a concave bridge, heavy brow and broad domed forehead, small deep-set eye, and a short blunt muzzle, so it cannot be confused with the Black Bear's straight profile. Replace hooves with plantigrade paws carrying long straight pale claws. Merge the neck plate into the torso as one silhouette with a soft value gradient. Drive the coat hatching and the shoulder/haunch masses off the body's normal so they read as anatomy under fur rather than blobs on top of it.

rows.readsAs: A grey mouflon or a shaggy goat with curled ram horns. Nothing about it says buffalo.
rows.defect: The defining mustRead is missing: the horns are NOT fused into a helmet boss across the forehead — they are two separate pale rams-horn curls springing from the poll with clear daylight between them and the skull, and their downward-then-forward curl is mouflon geometry, not Cape buffalo. Massive shoulders and thick neck are absent — the withers sit no higher than the hips, the neck is the same slim tube used on the Bull and Camel, and the belly actually sags LOWER than the chest, giving a pot-bellied goat read instead of a front-heavy bovid. Large fringed drooping ears hanging below the horns are absent; there is one small dark ear patch tucked behind the horn base and no fringe. HEAD is the batch-generic head with horns bolted on — same cranium, same hooked muzzle, same nose bead, same single ringed eye as the Bull, whose head this could be swapped with undetected. SEAM: a hard line along the back where the shoulder plate meets the barrel, plus a visible straight-edged boundary where the pale neck meets the darker torso. COAT: the flank is two overlapping pale ellipses with a dark saddle decal above them; the value change does not follow the ribcage and the hatch density is constant regardless of form.
rows.fix: Replace the horns with the real thing: a heavy keratin boss meeting in the middle of the forehead as one continuous rugose mass, then dropping outward and down before hooking up at the tips — the boss must occupy the whole forehead and read as fused. Hang large drooping fringed ears BELOW the horn line, outside the head silhouette. Rebuild the mass distribution: deep chest, high withers, thick short neck, and a topline that falls from shoulder to rump. Give the skull a broad flat forehead and a wide square muzzle distinct from the Bull's. Fuse the neck and shoulder into one silhouette and shade the coat off the barrel's form.

rows.readsAs: A tan goat or a small ox calf with short pale horns. Reads as the same animal as the Buffalo in a warmer palette.
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads absent. No massive humped neck and shoulder mass — the neck is a slim tube of the same diameter as the Camel's, and the withers are level with the hips, so the animal has no front-heavy bull mass whatsoever. No heavy pendulous dewlap — the throat line is a clean straight taper from jaw to brisket with nothing hanging. The horns are the one hit: short, pale, curving forward, correct in character, though they are stuck onto the dark poll patch with a hard edge rather than emerging from a pedicle. HEAD is the batch-generic head — cranium, hooked muzzle, dark nose bead and single white-ringed eye all identical to the Buffalo and the Brown Bear; swap it with the Buffalo's, remove the horns, and no viewer could tell. Feet are the same dark hoof cap used on the bears and the bobcat, so 'each family has its own foot type' is not visible here either. SEAM: the shoulder/neck plate boundary shows as a hard diagonal from withers to chest, and there is a second visible straight edge where the pale barrel meets the darker rump. COAT: the flank is built from two soft ellipse masses plus a floating dark hip patch; the uniform hatching crosses belly and back at the same strength and does not curve around the body.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front end: a crest of muscle over the neck and withers making the shoulder the tallest point, a neck at least twice its current diameter, and a deep brisket. Add a pendulous dewlap as a real silhouette feature — a scalloped fold running from jaw to chest that breaks the throat line. Broaden and square the skull with a wide flat forehead, set the eyes wider and lower, and shorten the muzzle so it cannot be swapped with the Buffalo. Blend the horn bases into the skull. Remove all hard plate boundaries at neck, shoulder and rump; light the coat off the body's own form.

rows.readsAs: A camel — the best read in the batch. A stranger would name it correctly.
rows.defect: Hump present, long high-held neck present, so two of three mustReads land. The third does not: the legs are neither very long nor knobbly-kneed — leg mass is roughly 40% of total height against the note's 'roughly half', and the limbs are smooth tapered tubes with no carpal knob, no stifle, no chestnut pads, ending in the same generic dark hoof cap used on the bears and the bobcat rather than a splayed two-toed camel foot pad. SEAM — the worst in the batch: the hump is an ELLIPSE PASTED ON TOP of the back. There is a hard, unblended contour where its underside crosses the topline and a visible value step between hump and torso, so it reads as a separate object balanced on the animal rather than a rise in the spine. A second seam runs from the withers down the front of the shoulder where the neck plate overlaps the barrel. HEAD is the batch-generic head with a dark eye patch added — the same rounded cranium, same downward-hooked muzzle and same white-ringed eye as the Brown Bear and the Bull; there is no split lip, no long low-set nostril, no camel's narrow deep jaw or heavy brow, so the eye patch is the only thing carrying the identity. COAT: the flank is two large pale ellipse balloons (shoulder and haunch) with soft edges sitting over the barrel; they read as inflated bladders rather than muscle under skin, and the hatching does not thin or darken as it wraps to the belly.
rows.fix: Make the hump part of the topline — one continuous back contour that rises out of the withers and falls to the sacrum, with no independent outline and no value step; if a hump silhouette is needed, it should be a deformation of the torso mesh, not a stacked shape. Lengthen the legs to about half total height and articulate them: pronounced knee/carpal knobs, angled hocks, and a broad splayed two-toed foot pad instead of a hoof. Rebuild the skull as camelid — narrow, deep-jawed, with a distinctly split upper lip, a long slit nostril and a heavy brow shelf above the eye, so the identity survives without the patch. Blend the neck into the shoulder, and drive the shoulder/haunch masses and coat shading off the body's form so they stop reading as balloons.

rows.readsAs: A grey elephant with an enormous black dinner-plate ear pasted over its shoulder — the ear reads African, or at a glance like a fan/shield stuck on a tapir.
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL: 'small triangular ears'. The ear is a huge dark rounded ellipse roughly 40% of the whole body area, covering the neck, shoulder and foreleg. It is a flat, uniformly-filled shape with a hard unbroken outline — a decal lying over the body, not a membrane growing off the skull, and it takes no light from the body it covers. The eye is stranded on the ear's upper edge instead of on the cheek, so the eye/ear relationship is nonsense. 'Twin-domed forehead with a dip between' does not read either: the cranium above the ear is one smooth single dome. Trunk and arched convex back are correct and are the only reason the picture says elephant.
rows.fix: Shrink the ear to ~1/3 its current area, make it a triangle with the point down at the jaw and the long edge along the skull, and give it its own inner shading + a soft folded leading edge so it curves off the head. Move the eye forward onto the cheek ahead of the ear root. Split the forehead into two domes with a shallow median dip, and expose the foreleg the ear is currently hiding.

rows.readsAs: A smooth tan two-humped camel toy — clean silhouette, but shaved.
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL: 'shaggy hanging hair on the neck, chest and hump crowns' is entirely absent — the whole animal is smooth flat tan with no hair anywhere, so the winter-Bactrian read is gone. The two humps are present but sit as two separate outlined lumps ON the topline with a visible boundary at each base, rather than rising out of the back. SEAMS: a hard-edged pale rectangle spans the midsection (straight top edge and a vertical right edge across the barrel), and the two haunch spheres show their own circular boundaries where they overlap it — the torso reads as three stacked primitives, not one solid. Coat is a flat fill, not shaded by the form. HEAD: the rounded wedge muzzle, high-set cartoon eye and small dark ear are the same head as the Bison and the Banteng in this batch — swap them and nobody would know.
rows.fix: Add a hanging mane along the underside of the neck, a chest bib and a shaggy crown on each hump, drawn as strands that hang WITH gravity off the silhouette edge. Fuse the humps into the topline with a continuous curve. Kill the rectangular midsection panel and the haunch circle edges — one torso mass with shoulder and haunch as bulges in a single outline. Give the head a camelid signature: split upper lip, downturned nose, heavy brow over the eye, small backswept ear.

rows.readsAs: A small pale striped goat or a bleached hyena cub — not a badger.
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL on two of three. 'Broad flattened low-slung body': the animal is narrow, short in the barrel and stands on long clear-of-ground legs — belly clearance is roughly a full leg length. Rendered aspect looks closer to 1.6 than the specified 2.4. 'Long straight digging foreclaws': absent — the feet are blunt pale cylinder ends with no claw geometry at all. 'White stripe running back over the face' has become a dark banded eye-mask instead of a longitudinal crown stripe, so it reads raccoon/lemur. The flank carries long dark brush-strokes like tiger stripes, which no badger has, and they are drawn as straight strokes over the flank rather than curving with the barrel — floating pattern, not coat on form. SEAMS: every leg is a pale tube with a hard-edged join at the shoulder and hip. HEAD: a small rounded blob differentiated only by a painted mask; the underlying skull is the same as the Beaver's.
rows.fix: Drop the belly to near ground level, widen the barrel, shorten the legs to stubs. Replace flank stripes with a plain grizzled grey coat. Run ONE white stripe from the nose over the crown between two black cheek bands. Add long pale straight foreclaws projecting past the forefoot. Wedge the skull — flat low cranium, tapering conical snout, tiny ear set far back.

rows.readsAs: A brown cow with a big white horseshoe hung on its cheek.
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL: 'white rump patch' — the rump is solid brown, no patch. 'White lower legs' is at best marginal; the lower legs are only slightly lighter tan, not the sharp white stockings that define the species. The horns are the worst read: instead of two crescents sweeping up and out from a bald forehead plate, a single thick white C-ring sits low on the cheek beside the muzzle, looking like an object hanging off the face; there is no forehead plate joining them. The white muzzle band is present and correct. SEAMS: same rectangular midsection panel as the Camel with a straight top edge across the barrel, plus visible circular haunch boundaries overlapping it; the head is a separate blob with a soft but traceable join at the neck. HEAD: apart from the misplaced horn ring, this is the Camel/Bison head — same rounded muzzle, same high cartoon eye, same small dark ear.
rows.fix: Move the horns to the top of the skull, origin at the outer poll, sweeping up-out-then-in as two separate smooth crescents, and join their bases with a pale bald boss. Add the hard-edged white rump patch and four clean white stockings from the knee/hock down. Remove the torso panel edge. Give the bovine skull a straight flat profile, a broad squared muzzle and eyes set wide on the sides of the head, so it cannot be the camel.

rows.readsAs: A mustard-yellow haystack or hedgehog body standing on four brown wooden planks.
rows.defect: BLOCKING SEAM: the legs are literal flat dark-brown rectangles — parallel vertical sides, hard corners, a different flat tone from the body, butted into the underside with a visible straight join. Nothing about them grows from the animal; they read as furniture legs. mustRead FAIL: 'muscular shoulder hump over the forelegs' — the topline is a plain oval whose highest and heaviest point is at the MIDDLE/REAR; the shoulder end is the low end, exactly backwards. Also FAIL: no stub tail is visible at all. 'Flat-footed plantigrade paws' is only half there — the feet are dark blobs with a few white claw ticks, no long sole. The fur is a fringe of straight spikes radiating outward from the back and rump edge only, standing off the silhouette like a halo instead of lying along the body; the body interior is a smooth ungroomed gradient, so the coat is floating, not mapped. HEAD: small rounded snout with a cartoon dot eye and one small ear — it would pass as a dog or the Beaver's head enlarged.
rows.fix: Rebuild the limbs as tapering masses with shoulder/upper-arm and hip/thigh volumes that swell out of the torso outline with no join line, ending in long flat plantigrade feet. Raise the topline into a distinct hump directly above the forelegs and slope down to lower hips. Add the stub tail. Run the fur as short directional strokes across the whole body following its curvature, with the shaggier break at the hump. Broaden and dish the skull, widen the muzzle base, and set the small round ears high and wide.

rows.readsAs: A river otter with a beaver paddle glued to its back.
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL: 'big orange chisel incisors' — there are no teeth of any kind, the mouth is a plain closed line, and the incisors are the single most identifying feature of the animal. Partial FAIL on 'stocky humped body': the torso is a long straight-topped tube with no arch, and it is far too slender — this is a mustelid body, not a rodent's. The paddle tail is well drawn and cross-hatched but attaches high on the flank with a hard-edged root seam, so it reads as attached rather than continuous with the rump. SEAM: a hard tonal line runs the whole length of the body where the pale belly panel meets the darker back, and the torso is filled with regular horizontal contour striping that looks like wood grain rather than fur following the form. HEAD: a small rounded blob with a dark patch, a cartoon eye and a blunt muzzle — this is the Badger's head with the mask removed.
rows.fix: Add two large orange chisel incisors below the muzzle, visible in profile. Arch the topline into a rounded rump-heavy hump, thicken the barrel, keep the legs short. Blend the tail root into the rump mass with the scales fading in rather than starting at a hard edge. Replace the horizontal grain with fur direction that wraps the barrel, and soften the belly/back boundary into a gradient. Give the skull the beaver signature: blunt squared muzzle, small round ears set right on top of a flat head, tiny eye high and far back.

rows.readsAs: A scruffy pale alpaca or a shaggy pony — nothing about it says bison.
rows.defect: Fails ALL THREE mustReads, and lands exactly on the failure mode the reference note warns about. (1) 'Huge muscular shoulder hump': absent — the topline is a level uniform barrel like a cow. (2) 'Massive low-slung shaggy head with beard': the head is small (reads ~0.18, not the specified 0.27), carried HIGH on an upright raised neck, with no beard, no chin hair and no horns. (3) 'Narrow tapering hindquarters': reversed — the hindquarters are the bulkiest part of the animal. SEAM: a hard straight diagonal line crosses the shoulder from the withers down to the chest, cutting the torso into two panels; the haunch sphere edge is also visible. The shag is a ring of straw-colored spikes projecting from the belly, chest and neck edge, sitting outside the silhouette like a fringe with a clean smooth body behind it — coat floating over the form, not on it. HEAD: rounded muzzle, high-set white cartoon eye, small dark ear — identical construction to the Bactrian Camel and the Banteng; this is the clearest instance of the owner's complaint in the batch.
rows.fix: Rebuild the topline front-heavy: peak the mass directly over the forelegs into a tall hump, then slope steeply down to small hips. Drop the head low, below the line of the back, on a short thick neck, and scale it up to the specified headFrac. Add the beard hanging off the chin, a dark woolly cape over head/hump/forelegs contrasting with short bare hindquarters, and short black upcurved horns. Remove the diagonal shoulder seam and the haunch circle. Give the skull a heavy broad forehead with the eyes pushed low and forward of the horn bases so it can never be the camel's head.

rows.readsAs: A pale toy antelope — closest real read is a pronghorn or an impala figurine. Nobody would say "gazelle" specifically.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS: (a) no dark band along the flank — the whole body is one uniform tan with no tan/white boundary anywhere, so the species' single most diagnostic marking is absent; (b) horns are not ringed — they are smooth pale tubes with no annulation, and the curve is a plain outward hook rather than a lyre S. Only "fine legs / long neck" partially reads, and the legs are thick tapered cylinders, not delicate. HEAD: identical construction to Gerenuk, Goat and Giraffe in this batch — same rounded cranium, same rectangular box muzzle jutting forward with the same little mouth notch, same single oversized white eye ring. Swap it with the Gerenuk head and no one could tell. SEAMS: two hard-edged pale ellipses are pasted onto the flank as shoulder and haunch — you can trace their outlines as discrete discs sitting on top of the torso, not as bulges in it. A separate dark circular disc floats at the hip with a hard edge, unattached to any tail or marking. COAT: horizontal hatching runs in flat straight lines across the torso panel and does not bend around the barrel or the shoulder mass — it floats over the form rather than wrapping it.
rows.fix: Add the flank band as a real value break (dark chocolate stripe running shoulder-to-haunch with the white belly below it and tan above) and follow the body's curvature. Cut ring grooves into the horns and give them the double curve — back, then up and forward at the tips. Kill the pasted shoulder/haunch ellipses: build the bulges from the torso solid's own shading so no edge exists. Delete the dark hip disc. Re-project the coat hatching along the body's cross-section so it curves with the barrel. Give the gazelle its own skull: short, fine, tapering to a narrow black nose, eye set high and far back on the cheek.

rows.readsAs: A llama or a guanaco. The long straight neck on a short body with no ear presence points at camelid, not antelope.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS: (a) "huge ears" are entirely absent — I see no ear on the head at all, and the gerenuk's oversized ears are half its recognizability; (b) the head is not a tiny wedge — headFrac reads far larger than 0.15 and the skull is the same rounded-cranium-plus-box-muzzle as the Gazelle; (c) not reared upright, which the row lists as the characteristic pose. The neck IS elongated, which is the one thing that lands. HEAD: this is the Gazelle's head at slightly smaller scale — same horns, same muzzle box, same eye. Directly swappable with entry 1; that is the owner's complaint proven in a single pair. SEAMS: same two pasted pale ellipses on the flank with hard visible outlines, same floating dark hip disc, and the neck meets the torso at an abrupt narrowing rather than flowing into a chest. COAT: flat horizontal hatching on the torso panel that ignores the body's roundness; the neck is untextured, so coat and body read as separate layers.
rows.fix: Give it enormous ears — leaf-shaped, nearly as long as the face, set wide. Shrink the skull to a true narrow wedge (a third of the current mass) so the neck dominates. Make the horns short, thick and hooked forward at the tips — nothing like the Gazelle's. Lengthen the neck further and taper it so it grows out of a real chest instead of plugging into the torso. Remove the pasted haunch discs and the hip disc; sculpt those masses in shading. Consider the reared browsing pose the row calls for.

rows.readsAs: A scruffy grey stray dog or a small hyena with a bottlebrush tail. Not remotely an anteater.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on two of three: (a) NO tubular snout — the head is a short rounded blob with a stubby blunt muzzle; the anteater's whole silhouette identity is a straight tapered tube half the length of the body and it simply is not there; (b) NO black-and-white diagonal shoulder wedge — the body is uniform grey-tan with no marking of any kind. The eye is also large and prominent when the row calls for small, which further pushes the read toward dog. The tail is bristly and does read as a fan, but it is a thin scraggly broom rather than an enormous body-wide flag, and it hangs behind rather than plumes over the back. OFF-BODY ARTIFACT: a hard-edged pale white sphere sits at the tail base, half overlapping the rump and half floating in empty space — clearly a stray primitive, not anatomy. HEAD: generic small-carnivore head; place it on the Giant Otter and nobody notices. SEAMS: a hard vertical boundary runs where the darker neck/shoulder mass meets the pale torso panel, and the same boundary repeats at the rear — the torso reads as a lighter rectangle laid between two darker end-caps. Front legs are plain cylinders butted into the body; the knuckle-walking note is not expressed at all. COAT: horizontal hatch lines run dead straight across the torso and stop at the panel edges instead of continuing around the form.
rows.fix: Rebuild the skull as the defining feature: a long straight cone, no forehead stop, tiny pin-hole mouth at the tip, and a small dark eye placed far back near the ear. Add the black wedge — a broad white-edged black band running diagonally from the throat up across the shoulder. Make the tail a huge banner of long hair, wider than the torso is deep. Delete the white sphere at the tail base. Blend the neck/shoulder into the torso so no vertical seam exists, and curl the forefeet under to knuckles with the claws visible inside.

rows.readsAs: A dachshund. Long low body, four short legs, thin round tail, dog head.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on two of three: (a) the tail is round, thin and tapering with a curl at the tip — exactly the river-otter/rat tail the note explicitly warns against; there is no width, no flattening, no rudder; (b) NO cream throat bib — the throat is the same dark brown as the head, and the bib is the one marking that separates this species from every other otter. The head is broad-ish and has a visible ear, but no whiskers are drawn. SEAMS — the worst in the batch: a hard, almost straight vertical line separates the dark neck/chest from the pale torso panel, and a matching hard line separates the panel from the dark rear. The pale coat is a rectangle stuck between two dark blocks; you can read the panel's four corners. The legs are dark cylinders butted onto the pale panel with an abrupt tonal step at the join. HEAD: generic mustelid-ish blob — same rounded cranium, same short muzzle, same big white eye ring as the Giant Anteater. Fully swappable with it. COAT: hatching is a flat horizontal weave that neither wraps the barrel nor darkens toward the silhouette edge; it sits on top of the body like wallpaper.
rows.fix: Replace the tail with a broad dorsoventrally flattened paddle — wide at the base, widening again before the tip, edged like a rudder. Add the cream bib as an irregular pale blotch across the throat and upper chest (its shape is individual — make it read as a patch, not a stripe). Dissolve the two vertical seams: the pale flank must fade into the dark dorsal tone across a gradient, not meet it at a line. Flatten and widen the skull, add long white whiskers and set the ears as small round buttons low on the sides. Add webbed feet.

rows.readsAs: A giraffe. Immediately and unambiguously, at any size.
rows.defect: All three mustReads land: neck is enormously long, two dark skin-covered ossicones sit on the crown, and the back does slope from high shoulders down to the hips. Portrait aspect is correct. This is the only head in the batch a stranger could name — the ossicones plus the reticulated pattern running up the neck make it unswappable. Remaining faults are real but not shipping-fatal: (1) the muzzle is the same rectangular box primitive used on Gazelle, Gerenuk and Goat — the giraffe reads only because of the ossicones and the pattern, not because the skull was drawn for it; the face should be long, narrow and slightly convex with a heavy soft upper lip. (2) The torso is visibly faceted — there are straight polygon creases across the shoulder and a hard diagonal edge on the chest where flat planes meet, so the body reads as low-poly rather than as a solid. (3) The reticulation is painted onto a flat plane: the patch grid keeps the same scale and orientation right up to the silhouette edge instead of compressing and turning as the body rounds away, so the coat sits slightly above the form. (4) The patch field stops with a straight horizontal cut at the top of each leg. (5) The tail is a bare thin line with a tuft, thinner than any drawn line elsewhere on the animal.
rows.fix: Replace the box muzzle with a purpose-built giraffe skull — long narrow face, slight bulge over the nasals, prominent lips, eye large and dark with lashes, set high and wide. Smooth the shoulder and chest facets into a continuous surface. Warp the reticulation with the body's curvature so patches foreshorten and shrink toward the silhouette, and let them break up gradually down the legs rather than ending on a straight line. Thicken the tail and give the tuft weight.

rows.readsAs: A pale sheep or a young llama. Nothing in the picture says goat.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on all three: (a) "backward-sweeping horns" are two barely-visible dark nubs on the crown — no sweep, no length, no curve; (b) NO chin beard at all; (c) NO upright tail — there is no tail on the animal, and the dark circle at the rump is the same floating hip disc that appears on the Gazelle and Gerenuk, not a tail. The note's own distinguishers are inverted: the coat reads soft and woolly and the face is short and blunt, so the render lands on "sheep" precisely where the row says to avoid it. HEAD: strip the nubs off and this is the Gazelle's head — identical rounded cranium, identical box muzzle, identical eye. Fully swappable within the batch. SEAMS: the two pasted pale ellipses on the flank read as discrete discs with traceable outlines; the hard-edged dark hip disc floats over the rump; the legs meet the belly at an abrupt tonal step. COAT: flat horizontal hatching across the torso panel, unbent by the barrel, and it stops dead at the panel boundary while the neck and legs carry no texture — coat and body are two layers, not one.
rows.fix: Give it real horns: thick, ridged, sweeping back over the neck in a long arc. Add the chin beard as a distinct hanging tuft. Add the short tail pointing UP over the rump — that plus the beard is what kills the sheep read. Flatten the coat (short, lying hair, not wool) and narrow/straighten the face profile with a Roman-nosed muzzle and horizontal-slit pupils. Delete the hip disc and the pasted haunch ellipses; build those masses from the torso's own shading.

rows.readsAs: A brown pig, or a capybara. The straight forward-jutting snout, flat back and small dark feet all point at suid, not ursid.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on all three: (a) NO shoulder hump — the topline is flat, and if anything the rump sits as high as the withers, i.e. the exact black-bear silhouette the note tells us to avoid; (b) NO dished concave face — the profile is a straight rectangular muzzle tube stuck onto a round cranium, convex if anything; (c) NO long pale front claws and NO grizzled fur — the feet are small dark blunt blobs that read as cloven hooves, and the coat is a single flat brown with no silver-tipped guard hairs. OFF-BODY ARTIFACT: a hard-edged dark ring/disc sits on top of the skull, overlapping the crown and the ear — the same stray primitive that lands on the hip of the Gazelle, Gerenuk and Goat, here mis-placed onto the head. SEAMS: a hard curved boundary separates the dark shoulder/neck mass from the pale torso panel, and a second one separates the panel from the dark haunch — the pale flank is a stuck-on patch, not a lit surface. Legs are cylinders butted into the belly with a visible tonal step. HEAD: apart from the stray disc, this is the same cranium-plus-box-muzzle used on the Otter and the Anteater, and the body construction is shared with the Goat. COAT: horizontal hatch lines run straight across the torso and do not wrap the barrel or darken toward the silhouette.
rows.fix: Build the hump — a distinct muscular mass over the withers that is the highest point of the animal, with the back falling away to a lower rump. Rebuild the skull: broad, with a concave dip between the brow and the nose, small close-set eyes, small round ears set wide and low. Replace the feet with plantigrade paws and add the long pale front claws. Add grizzling — pale tips scattered through the dark undercoat, denser over the hump and shoulders. Delete the disc on the skull. Dissolve the two torso seams into gradients so shoulder, flank and haunch are one continuous surface.

rows.readsAs: A pale grey capybara with a spiky mane — a rodent, not a pig relative
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL: there are no tusks of any kind. The muzzle is a bare pink oval disc with two nostril dots and a thin curved mouth line, nothing protruding from the jaw. Second: the bristle mane is drawn as loose straight strands that leave the silhouette entirely — a dozen spikes hang in empty space below the belly line and off the chest, unattached to any surface, so the coat floats rather than lying on the form. Third seam: at 3x there is a hard rectangular stair-step notch on the throat where the skull block meets the neck, and a straight vertical crease down the shoulder — head and neck are stuck on, not grown. The head is a byte-for-byte relative of the Pig's in this same batch: identical rounded blunt skull, identical pink nose disc with two dots, identical white-ring bead eye, identical mouth line.
rows.fix: Add two short straight tusks emerging from the upper jaw and pointing STRAIGHT DOWN past the lower lip, dark ivory, visible in profile — this is the whole identity of the species. Clip every bristle to the body silhouette and root it in the coat (bristles should read as a raised crest along the spine and a slight fringe on the cheek, never as free-floating strands over the background). Kill the throat notch by carrying the neck taper into the jaw as one continuous solid. Differentiate the skull from the Pig: peccary has a longer wedge head with a flatter forehead and the eye set high and far back near the ear, not a round dome with a centred eye.

rows.readsAs: A pink capybara or a hairless tapir-piglet
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL: no curly corkscrew tail. At the rump there is only a flat dark maroon oval smudge — it reads as a bruise or a shadow blob, not a tail at all. Body also fails 'deep barrel on very short legs': the torso is a shallow slab and the legs are long straight sticks with the same clearance as the Pronghorn's. Ear is a dark brown heart-shaped blob pasted flat over the skull that OVERLAPS the eye, sitting in front of it in z-order — clearly an appliqué. Same throat stair-step notch as the Peccary where head meets neck, plus a hard inverted-V crease under the belly where the shoulder lens and haunch lens meet. The snout disc is the one thing that reads correctly. Head is interchangeable with the Peccary's — same skull, same nose disc, same eye bead.
rows.fix: Draw a real corkscrew: a thin tail rising off the rump and spiralling into 1.5–2 visible loops, silhouetted against the background. Drop the belly line and shorten the legs by roughly a third so the barrel nearly grazes the ground. Move the ear behind and above the eye and let it fold forward with a shaded inner cup that shares the body's light direction. Merge the shoulder and haunch masses into a continuous barrel so the belly V-crease disappears. Give the pig a dished forehead and a long straight snout bridge so its profile is not the Peccary's dome.

rows.readsAs: A white plastic toy lamb or a white ferret on stilts
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL twice. (1) No huge furred paws — every leg ends in the exact same small dark two-toed HOOF used on the Pig, Possum, Quoll and Raccoon in this batch. A bear with hooves is a category error. (2) No sloping shoulders on a long body: the torso is a smooth featureless loaf, the topline is flat, and the shoulder is a soft airbrushed grey ellipse floating on the surface with its own visible edge rather than a mass under the skin. The neck is short, not long. Coat FAIL: there is zero fur — the surface is a glossy airbrushed white gradient with specular highlights that reads as vinyl or porcelain. Seams: a hard faceted crease line runs across the neck into the chest, the same stair-step notch appears behind the jaw, and the shoulder/haunch ellipses have soft but distinct boundaries that do not follow the body's curvature. The ear is a flat two-tone grey coin stuck on the skull like a sticker.
rows.fix: Replace the hooves with broad, heavily furred plantigrade paws — wide oval pads noticeably wider than the leg, with fur spilling over the toe line and short dark claws. Lengthen the neck and drop the head so the profile is the polar bear's low-slung, Roman-nosed wedge with no shoulder hump. Add fur: directional strokes over the whole coat that follow the body's contour and darken in the shadow terminator, with a longer guard-hair fringe on the belly and haunch. Blend the shoulder/haunch into the torso with form shading rather than pasted ellipses. Set the ear into the skull with a shaded cup instead of a flat disc.

rows.readsAs: A pale beige goat kid or a smooth-coated cat
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL on all three. (1) The tail is a thin, smooth, tapered, fur-coloured curve with no scale texture, no pink flesh tone and no rat-like appearance — it reads as a cat's tail. (2) The face is not white-and-pointed with a pink nose: the muzzle is the same beige as the body with a small dark-brown nose dot, and the skull is a rounded wedge, not the opossum's long narrow triangle. (3) The coat is not grizzled or shaggy — it is a flat smooth cream airbrush with faint horizontal banding and no guard hairs, and the ears are the Pig's dark heart-shaped blob rather than thin bare pink ears. Seams: a hard angular facet line runs from the withers down the front of the shoulder, and the shoulder and haunch are two grey airbrushed lenses with visible edges meeting in a crease at the belly. Head is generic small-mammal — swap it with the Polar Bear's or the Quoll's and only the colour would change.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as bare skin: pink-grey at the base fading to off-white at the tip, with a visible ring-scale texture and no fur. Repaint the face white from the nose to above the eyes and give it a distinct PINK nose button; lengthen and narrow the skull into a true triangle with a long thin rostrum. Replace the coat with grizzled shaggy fur — long overlapping pale-tipped guard hairs over a dark undercoat, silhouette broken and irregular rather than smooth. Ears become two thin, bare, dark rounded flaps with translucent edges. Dissolve the shoulder facet line and the belly crease into continuous form shading.

rows.readsAs: A tan mule deer fawn with small antlers
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL on the markings, which are the species' signature. (1) No white throat bands — the throat is a single flat tan with no banding of any kind. (2) No white rump patch — worse, the rump carries a DARK brown blob, the exact inverse of what a pronghorn has. (3) The horns are cream/bone-coloured forked shapes that read as small deer ANTLERS, not the pronghorn's black, forward-hooked horn with one short prong; there are two tines of near-equal length and both curve backwards. Body is a chunky angular slab, not slim and deep-chested; there is a hard polygonal shoulder patch with a crisp straight edge on the neck-shoulder junction and a bright hairline running along the whole topline where the back solid is capped. The head is a generic deer muzzle with the same white-ring bead eye used on all seven.
rows.fix: Paint two crisp white bands across the throat and a large white rump patch, and remove the dark rump blob. Recolour the horns near-black and rebuild the shape: a single upright blade that hooks FORWARD at the tip with one short prong jutting forward from the front edge at mid-height — asymmetric, not a symmetric fork. Narrow the barrel and deepen the chest so the ribcage is the widest point and the flank tucks up. Remove the hard-edged shoulder polygon and the bright topline hairline. Give the head the pronghorn's very large dark eye set high on a narrow tapering muzzle so it does not read as a fawn.

rows.readsAs: An Appaloosa pony foal
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL: the spots stop at the base of the tail. The tail is a bushy banded brown-and-cream brush with a white tip and NOT ONE spot on it — the reference note calls the tail spots out as the distinguishing feature and they are absent. Snout FAIL: the muzzle is a short blunt brown block with a dark nose dot, not a pointed pink snout. Posture FAIL: the animal stands square and tall on straight vertical legs with high belly clearance — the opposite of a low slinking body. The spot pattern itself is coarse and blotchy, several spots merged into irregular ink-stains that read as Appaloosa roaning rather than discrete round quoll spots. Seam: a bright pale blue-white hairline runs along the top of the back at the withers, a hard cap on the body solid, and the head is joined by the same stair-step notch behind the jaw. The ear is the same flat dark disc used on the Polar Bear and the Raccoon.
rows.fix: Scatter round white spots along the length of the tail as well as the back and flanks, and shrink and separate the body spots so each is a discrete crisp dot rather than a merged blotch. Rebuild the muzzle as a long, fine, tapering point ending in a PINK nose. Drop the whole body: shorten the legs, lower the chest and belly toward the ground and let the spine curve so the animal reads as slinking. Remove the white rim line at the withers and set the ears into the skull as upright rounded flaps with shaded inner cups.

rows.readsAs: A pale grey sheep or a lemur-faced goat
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL: no hunched arched back. The topline is flat with a slight dip at mid-back and the shoulder sits at least as high as the rump — the defining raccoon hump is simply not there. Feet FAIL for the family: all four legs end in the same small dark two-toed hoof used on the Pig and the Polar Bear, when a raccoon's identity lives in its long-fingered hand-like paws. The ringed tail does read correctly and the eye patch is present, though it renders as a soft dark oval around the single visible eye — a panda-style patch rather than a black band running across the face. Seams: a bright white hairline runs the entire length of the topline where the body solid is capped, the shoulder and haunch are two grey airbrushed lenses with a hard inverted-V crease meeting them at the belly, and there is a straight crease where the neck column meets the chest. The coat is horizontal banding painted flat across the silhouette; it does not wrap the barrel or darken under the belly, so it floats.
rows.fix: Arch the spine: raise the rump above the shoulder and let the back curve up over the hips so the animal reads as hunched. Replace the hooves with five-toed hand-paws — dark, splayed, long-fingered, front pair noticeably dexterous. Extend the mask into a black band that crosses the muzzle bridge and reaches both eyes, bordered above and below by white. Remove the white topline hairline and the belly V-crease; blend the shoulder and haunch into the barrel with directional fur that curves around the form and darkens on the underside.

rows.readsAs: A generic tan antelope, or more precisely a pronghorn — and at a glance, the exact same picture as the Impala two rows down.
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads fail. (1) The face is NOT extremely long and narrow — at 3x zoom it is a short blunt wedge, roughly the same length-to-depth ratio as the Impala's and shorter than the Horse's; nothing about it says 'hartebeest'. (2) The back does not slope steeply down to the hindquarters — the topline is level and the croup blob actually sits slightly HIGHER than the withers, the opposite of the required line. (3) The horns are a pale symmetrical U with smooth tips; there is no bracket kink and no bony pedestal — the brown lump between them reads as a single ear, not a pedestal. SEAMS: a hard straight bright line runs the whole topline where the back panel butts the neck panel; the barrel is a trapezoidal facet with visible straight edges; shoulder and haunch are two pasted ovals of a different tan that read as bolted-on spheres, giving a 'two balloons' underline rather than a barrel. The near foreleg meets the chest with a visible step. The coat pinstriping runs straight along the body and does not wrap the shoulder or haunch masses, so it sits over the form rather than on it. TWIN: near-identical to Impala in body, horn, ear, eye and muzzle.
rows.fix: Lengthen and narrow the hartebeest skull to roughly double the Impala's face length and taper it to a narrow muzzle; drop the croup ~15% below the withers and run one continuous curve from the poll over a high shoulder down to the hips so the slope reads in silhouette. Replace the U-horn with a short backward-angled bracket set on an explicit raised bony boss between the eyes, and give it real ringing. Kill the topline highlight stroke and the barrel facet — the shoulder and haunch must be modelled as swellings of one torso solid with the coat texture flowing over them, not as separate ovals composited on top.

rows.readsAs: A dachshund. Long low pink-grey body, stumpy legs, a doggy smile — nobody would say hippo.
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail. The muzzle is a rounded balloon that is NARROWER than the skull, not the huge squared muzzle wider than the skull; and there are no nostrils anywhere — the required ears/eyes/nostrils-in-a-line on top of the head is absent. What sits on the face instead is one googly white-ringed eye plus two overlapping brown discs like a Mickey Mouse silhouette. The mouth is a floating brushstroke crescent that does not attach to any jaw line, and there is a second unattached crescent above it. SEAMS (blocker): at 3x the head/jowl is a hard-edged polygon with straight cut edges butted against the shoulder, with a notch of background actually visible in the gap; a bright hard 1-2px line runs the entire length of the topline; the tail is a dark circle stamped on the rump with a hard round edge. COAT: horizontal pinstripes run dead straight the full length of the body, crossing shoulder, barrel and haunch at the same angle and spacing with no deflection around any mass — it is a decal, not a surface.
rows.fix: Rebuild the skull as a hippo: a squared box muzzle visibly wider than the braincase, with the eyes, tiny round ears and two nostril bosses raised on the TOP plane in one line, and a wide straight lip line with tusk hints at the corner. Weld the head into the neck as one continuous solid — the polygon plate and the background notch must go. Delete the topline highlight stroke. Bend the coat pinstripes to follow the barrel's cross-section so they compress over the shoulder and haunch. Replace the stamped tail disc with a short flat paddle tail growing out of the rump.

rows.readsAs: A hornless fawn with a duck's snout, or a small dinosaur — the head does not read as equine at all.
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail outright. (1) There is NO mane — no crest, no hair along the neck at all — and the neck is a straight thick cylinder, not arched. (2) There are no ears on the head whatsoever. The tail is high-docked and bushy, which passes, but it renders as a stiff bristle broom with hard individual straight strands and an odd pale oval at its base, not flowing hair. Single hoof per leg passes, but the legs are featureless tapering cylinders with no knee, hock or fetlock. HEAD: at 3x it is a bulbous cranium with a long flat duckbill snout, a slit mouth line and an oversized brown disc eye with a white googly ring — this is the same head as the Hyena's with the ears removed. SEAMS: a bright hard straight line runs the entire topline from croup to withers; a hard-edged tan wedge sits at the shoulder top; the cheek has a straight facet cut; shoulder and haunch are two large pasted ovals of different value that make the body read as two balloons with a sag between them.
rows.fix: Give the horse an equine skull: straight or slightly dished profile, deep jowl and jaw at the cheek, a squared muzzle with visible nostril and lip, an eye set high and to the SIDE of the head at the widest point, and two mobile pricked ears. Add the crest mane as a raised ridge of hair growing out of the neck's top edge and arch the neck. Convert the tail from straight bristles to flowing curved strands and remove the pale disc at the dock. Delete the topline highlight and merge shoulder/haunch into one continuous torso with articulated knees, hocks and fetlocks above the hooves.

rows.readsAs: An Appaloosa pony. Spotted, hoofed, level-backed — a stranger would say 'spotted horse', not hyena.
rows.defect: It is the SAME RENDER AS THE HORSE with spots and ears added — identical silhouette, identical neck, identical two-balloon torso, identical brush tail with the pale disc at the dock, identical leg cylinders, identical HOOVES. A carnivore on hooves is a blocker by itself. All three mustReads fail: (1) the back does not slope down from high shoulders — the topline is level and the croup sits as high as the withers, so the defining skeletal slope is simply absent; (2) the ears are pointed ovals set fox-like on top of the skull, not the large rounded dish ears; (3) there is no thick neck and no jaw mass at all — the muzzle is the horse's thin tapering duckbill, the exact opposite of massive bone-crushing jaws. Spots are also painted onto the face and neck, where a spotted hyena is plain. SEAMS: same hard topline highlight and same hard shoulder wedge as the Horse; the ears are flat hard-edged shapes stuck on top of the cranium.
rows.fix: Fork the body off the horse rig entirely: raise the withers well above the croup and run a steep continuous descent to the hips, shorten the hind limbs relative to the fore, and replace hooves with four-toed digitigrade paws. Rebuild the head with carnivore mass — short deep muzzle, huge sagittal-crested cranium, wide zygomatic arches, visible jaw depth — and set two large round dish ears low-wide on the skull. Clear the spots from the face and neck and coarsen the mane into a bristling dorsal crest. The tail should be a short bushy black brush, not the horse's docked broom.

rows.readsAs: A very small lamb. Cream fleece body, brown cap on the head, long thin legs — nothing rodent-like.
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail. (1) There are NO whiskers at all — not one — and the whiskers are named in the row. (2) The legs are neither stubby nor is the body guinea-pig round: at 5x the legs are long slim ungulate cylinders with a clear gap of daylight under a belly held high, and the torso is the same shoulder-plus-haunch ungulate solid used by the Ibex and Hartebeest, only smaller. Ears are barely present — an ambiguous bump, not small rounded ears. The blunt muzzle is the one thing that passes. SEAM (blocker): the head is a dark-brown blob composited onto a cream body with an abrupt straight-cut colour boundary at the neck and a hard notch at the top-left of the skull — the head is stuck on, not grown out. The eye is the same oversized brown-disc-plus-white-googly-ring used on the Horse, Hyena, Hartebeest and Impala. TWIN: strip the horns and shag off the Ibex and you have this animal.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a true hyrax: one continuous rounded loaf of a body with no waist and no visible shoulder/haunch separation, belly nearly touching the ground, and four short thick legs with rubbery padded feet. Weld the head into the shoulder with a colour gradient rather than a cut edge, and shorten the neck to nothing. Add long radiating whiskers from the muzzle pad and two small round ears set low on the sides of the head. Shrink the eye and drop the googly white ring — a small dark bead reads far better at this size.

rows.readsAs: A shaggy bighorn ram, or a scruffy sheep — not an ibex.
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads fail. (1) The horn is a thick pale C-curl that sweeps FORWARD and DOWN around the face, ending in front of the eye — that is a bighorn ram's curl, not the ibex's massive backward-arcing scimitar, and it carries no knobbed ridges at all, just a smooth tube. It is also far too small to read as 'massive'. (2) There is NO beard under the chin — I looked at 3x and the chin is bare; what fringe exists is the same generic bristle as the rest of the coat, and it is on the throat and belly, not hanging from the chin. Stocky body passes. COAT (major): the shaggy fur is a ring of separate hard-edged black bristles projecting OUTSIDE the silhouette along the back, belly and neck like pins in a cushion — it floats around the body, it does not lie on it, and it does not thin or thicken with the form. The torso underneath carries a hard crosshatch grid that reads as basket weave rather than hair. SEAMS: a hard straight bright streak crosses the shoulder, and the rump tail is a dark stamped disc with a hard edge. The skull under the horns is the same rounded blob as the Hyrax's.
rows.fix: Replace the horn with the real thing: a long, heavy, backward-arcing scimitar reaching past the shoulder, thick at the base and tapering, with a clear row of transverse knobs on its front face. Add a distinct dark chin beard hanging as its own mass below the jaw. Rework the coat so hair strands are shorter, denser, and shaded BY the body — clumped and directional, thickening at the throat and flank and following the torso's curvature, with only a slight ragged break at the silhouette edge rather than free-floating spikes. Remove the crosshatch grid and the shoulder highlight streak, and grow the tail out of the rump instead of stamping a disc.

rows.readsAs: A pronghorn — and side by side, the same picture as the Hartebeest in slot 1.
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. (1) The horns are a plain pale symmetrical U with no ringing whatsoever and no lyre S-curve; in profile they rise straight and hook in, which is the wrong shape. (2) There is no white rump and there are no vertical black stripes on the rump — the hindquarters are the same flat tan as the rest of the body, so the single most identifiable impala marking is entirely absent. (3) The legs are the same medium tapering cylinders used on the Hartebeest and Hyrax, not extremely fine, and there is no black tuft above the hind hoof. TWIN (blocker): head, ear lump, googly eye position, muzzle wedge, mouth line, nostril dash, horn colour and body silhouette are all shared with the Hartebeest — the two renders are separable only by a small difference in horn tip curl. SEAMS: a hard straight line crosses the shoulder where the neck panel meets the barrel, and shoulder and haunch are again pasted ovals with the coat pinstripes running straight through them unaffected.
rows.fix: Give the impala its markings first — a white rump patch with two crisp vertical black stripes plus a black tail line, white belly, white throat and eye ring, and a black tuft on the hind cannon above the hoof. Rebuild the horn as a slender lyre: out, back, then up and inward at the tips, with heavy transverse ringing on the lower two thirds. Thin the legs to roughly two thirds their current diameter. Then separate the head from the Hartebeest's: the impala's face is short and delicate with a small dark muzzle and long narrow ears, while the hartebeest's must be long and narrow — right now they share one asset and must not. Remove the shoulder seam line and let the coat wrap the shoulder and haunch.

rows.readsAs: A tan dog or young hyena with scattered black paw-print-sized spots. Nobody would say cat, let alone clouded leopard.
rows.defect: THREE mustReads fail. (1) Tail is a short thin tapering hook roughly one-fifth of head+body length — the row's whole point is that the tail EQUALS head+body, and this is the exact error the note warns against. (2) The markings are small round blackish dot-clusters, not large cloud-shaped blotches with dark edges and a paler fill; there is no cloud, no edge/fill split, no rosette logic — they read as a Dalmatian's spots. (3) Legs are long and slim, not very short and stout; the animal stands tall like a hound when it should be a low slung, heavy-limbed climber. HEAD: identical construction to Cougar, Coati and Colugo — same rounded cranium, same flat brown circular ear disc in the same spot, same white-ringed cartoon eye, same short tapered muzzle with a round dark nose, same single mouth stroke. At 4x it is the Cougar head at 90% scale. SEAMS: a bright hairline runs straight along the topline where the neck slab meets the back, and a hard-edged wedge facet sits at the shoulder — the neck is laid over the torso, not grown from it. COAT: the spots are flat opaque blobs at full strength on the shaded underbelly as well as the lit back, and several stop dead on the neck/shoulder panel boundary — the pattern is floating on top rather than being shaded by the form.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail at full head+body length and give it real mass (a clouded leopard's tail is nearly as thick as its forearm). Replace the dot field with 6-10 large irregular cloud shapes, each a dark rim enclosing a mid-tone fill, sized ~1/4 of the torso depth, and rotate them to follow the barrel. Halve the leg length and thicken the forearm/thigh. Give the skull its own profile: broad short face, the longest canines relative to skull of any cat, small low-set rounded ears well back on a wide cranium, and a cat's forward-set eye — not the shared muzzle module. Multiply the coat pattern by the body's own shading pass so spots darken in the belly shadow, and let the spots cross the neck-shoulder join instead of terminating at it.

rows.readsAs: A small brown-and-tan dog, or a meerkat that has been put on all fours. No trace of a coati.
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. (1) The snout is the shared short tapered muzzle with a round nose tipped slightly DOWN — the defining long, mobile, up-tilted pig-like proboscis is simply not there. (2) The tail is a thick brown hook curving backwards and DOWN, roughly horizontal; the mustRead flagpole — a thin tail held bolt upright — is absent, and the banding is one vague dark smear, not faint rings. (3) The body is a normal-proportioned quadruped on mid-length legs with blunt cylinder feet ending in a dark colour band; it is neither long nor low, and there is no plantigrade sole meeting the ground. HEAD: the same module as Cougar, Clouded Leopard and Colugo — round cranium, brown disc ear, white-ringed eye, tapered muzzle. Swap it with the Cougar's and nobody would notice. SEAMS: the worst in the batch. A hard-edged pale trapezoid panel sits across the midsection with sharp straight diagonal boundaries at both the shoulder and the haunch, and a bright horizontal hairline crosses the topline at the neck join. The torso reads as three flat plates butted together. COAT: flat colour fills bounded by those plate edges; the tone changes on the seam line rather than with the curve of the barrel, so the coat is following the geometry of the panels, not the volume.
rows.fix: Build a real snout: extend the muzzle to roughly 1.5x the cranium length, taper it, and kink the last third UPWARD past the nose plane so the nostril points forward-up. Re-rig the tail to vertical, thin it to about half its current diameter, lengthen it to body length, and lay 6-8 soft alternating rings along it. Lengthen and lower the torso, shorten the legs, and give the foot a flat plantigrade sole with visible long claws. Dissolve the three torso plates into one continuous surface with a single gradient wrap; the shoulder and haunch should be swellings in that surface, not panels with borders. Kill the topline hairline where neck meets back.

rows.readsAs: A miniature giraffe, or a goat wearing giraffe hide. It is not recognisable as a gliding mammal of any kind.
rows.defect: The most complete failure in the batch — every mustRead is missing and the posture is wrong. (1) NO gliding membrane anywhere. The row calls for the most complete patagium of any mammal, enclosing neck, fingers, toes and the whole tail; the render has bare cylindrical legs, a bare thin tail and open air between all of them. This alone kills the species. (2) The eyes are not prominent — it uses the same ordinary small white-ringed eye as the Cougar and Coati, when the reference explicitly specifies huge round forward-facing eyes and that is the single most memorable thing about a colugo's face. (3) The camouflage is a hard-edged reticulated polygon net — a giraffe pattern — not soft mottled lichen blotching; the cells are regular, outlined in cream, and geometric where colugo camouflage is irregular and blurred. Posture is specified as flying and the render is a standing quadruped with all four feet planted and a cast ground shadow. HEAD: the shared module again — round cranium, brown disc ear, tapered muzzle, standard eye. Indistinguishable from Coati's. SEAMS: the reticulated pattern stops on a sharp straight vertical line where the torso panel abuts the plain neck, exposing the panel boundary; there is also a hard facet edge at the shoulder. COAT: the net pattern is drawn at uniform scale and uniform cream-line weight straight across the barrel with no foreshortening toward the silhouette edges — it is wallpaper laid over the shape.
rows.fix: This one needs re-authoring, not patching. Put it in the gliding pose the row asks for: limbs splayed, seen from front or three-quarter, and draw the patagium as one continuous translucent kite from the side of the neck out past the fingertips, down the flank, around the ankles and enclosing the tail to its tip — the tail must be INSIDE the membrane, which is what separates it from a flying squirrel. Enlarge the eyes to at least 2x current diameter, move them forward and parallel on the face, and give them a dark iris ring. Replace the reticulated net with soft, irregular, low-contrast grey-green lichen mottling of at least three overlapping scales. If the pipeline cannot yet do a non-quadruped rig, it is still better to ship a clinging-to-a-trunk pose with the membrane visible than a standing goat.
