rows.readsAs: A plain tan dog, or a lioness with no mane. The body is credible as a big cat but nothing narrows it to a cougar.
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads fail. (1) The tail is a short, thin, upward-curled hook about a third of body length with NO black tip — the row specifies a very long, heavy, black-tipped tail, and the heavy black tip is the one field mark that separates a cougar from every other plain tan cat. (2) There are no black muzzle bars; the face has a plain round nose and one grey mouth stroke on an unmarked cream muzzle. The plain unmarked tawny coat (3) is correctly delivered, and the plainness does read. The note's topline is also wrong: shoulders and hindquarters sit at the same height, so the cougar's characteristic hindquarters-higher stance is gone. HEAD: at 4x it is the same shared module as Clouded Leopard, Coati and Colugo — same rounded cranium, same flat brown circular ear disc, same white-ringed eye, same tapered muzzle. This is the owner's complaint in its purest form: the Clouded Leopard and the Cougar have literally the same head at different scales. SEAMS: a hard pale hairline runs the full length of the topline where the neck meets the back, and the shoulder is a darker wedge with a straight-cut diagonal edge; a matching hard edge sits at the haunch. Three flat plates again. The ear is a flat brown disc with a crisp outline stuck onto the skull rather than a shape emerging from it. COAT: the tan surface carries a faint diagonal hatch that runs at the same angle and density across shoulder, barrel and flank without wrapping, so it does not describe the volume; the shoulder and haunch masses are soft airbrushed smudges sitting underneath the hard panel edges rather than being those masses.
rows.fix: Triple the tail length, thicken it to a heavy rope of near-uniform diameter, drop it into the low J-curve a cougar carries, and put a solid black 15% tip on it — that tip alone will do most of the identification work. Add the black muzzle bars flanking a pink-grey nose and the white chin/upper-lip patch. Raise the pelvis above the withers so the topline slopes down toward the shoulder. Remove the topline hairline and the two straight panel edges — one continuous torso surface with the shoulder blade and thigh as swellings in it. Rebuild the head to a cat skull: short broad face, wide-set eyes on the front plane, small rounded ears set wide on the skull top rather than a disc pasted on the side.

rows.readsAs: A giraffe, or an okapi. Every stranger shown this unlabelled says giraffe. It is not a cow.
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads fail outright and the coat is the wrong species. (1) No udder and no heavy sagging barrel — the belly line is straight and tucked, the topline is level and slim, the whole silhouette is an athletic browsing ungulate, not a dairy animal. (2) No throat dewlap; the underside of the neck runs as a clean straight edge from jaw to chest with no hanging fold at all. (3) Only this one lands: the ears are large, sideways-set and paired, and the tail does end in a distinct grey tuft. But the coat is a brown-on-cream RETICULATED GIRAFFE pattern — hard-edged polygons separated by cream channels — which is a giraffe's exact field mark and is not any cattle marking; and the muzzle is a long narrow taper, not a bovine's broad square muzzle. There are no horns or poll boss. HEAD: it IS different from the other six — the only long-muzzled, paired-tall-eared skull in the batch, so a swap would be noticed. But it is unique as a giraffe head, not a cow head, so it solves the sameness problem by drawing the wrong animal. SEAMS: a hard straight diagonal line where the neck plate overlaps the shoulder, with the reticulated patches terminating abruptly on it, plus hard panel edges at shoulder and haunch on the torso. The neck is a separate flat plate laid over the body. COAT: the polygon cells hold the same size, same cream line weight and same contrast from spine to belly and right up to the silhouette edge — no foreshortening, no shading from the body under it. Fully floating.
rows.fix: Replace the reticulated net with cattle marking: large soft-edged irregular patches, high contrast (black or deep red on white), that break across the shoulder and hip rather than tiling. Rebuild the body mass: sag the belly into a deep barrel, drop the ribcage, add the udder between the hind legs, and add hip bones standing proud at the rump. Hang a real dewlap — a soft triangular fold from the jaw down the throat to the brisket. Broaden and square the muzzle, shorten the face, widen the forehead and add horns or a visible poll. Merge the neck plate into the shoulder with a continuous surface and let the patches cross that join.

rows.readsAs: A pale sandy dog or jackal — the closest read in the batch, though the raised brushy tail pulls it slightly toward a scruffy pony.
rows.defect: Best canid form here, but one mustRead fails and the construction is exposed. (1) The narrow pointed muzzle reads — correct. (2) The large erect triangular ears read — correct, and they are the only true triangular ears in the batch. (3) FAILS: the bushy tail is carried HIGH, angled up and back above the topline. The row and the note both specify it hangs LOW, and tail carriage is the single cue that separates coyote from wolf and from dog at distance — carried up like this it actively reads as the wrong animal. SEAMS: clearly visible even at 1x. A darker trapezoid panel with a sharp straight diagonal border sits at the shoulder and another at the haunch, a hard pale line runs along the topline, and the front leg's top simply abuts the belly line on a hard boundary rather than emerging from the chest. The feet are plain cylinder stumps ended with a dark colour band — no paw, no toes, no digitigrade foot, so the promised per-family foot type is not visible. COAT: the tan carries a fine diagonal hatch drawn at one angle and one density across the entire flank; it does not wrap or compress toward the silhouette, and the shoulder/haunch masses are soft airbrushed grey blobs sitting UNDER the hard-edged panels rather than being formed by them — so the muscle reads as a smudge and the panel reads as a plate. There is no coyote colour architecture at all: no dark saddle over the back, no rufous on the ears and legs, no cream throat and belly.
rows.fix: Drop the tail to hang below the topline at roughly 30-40 degrees off vertical and keep the brush. Dissolve the two trapezoid panels and the topline hairline into a single continuous torso surface — the shoulder and haunch should be the only tonal events, modelled as swellings with soft terminators. Build a digitigrade paw: four visible toes, the metacarpals lifted, weight on the pads. Add the coyote's colour map — grizzled dark saddle, rusty ears and outer legs, pale cream throat, chest and belly, black tail tip. Make the hatch follow the body's cross-section direction so it curves around the barrel.

rows.readsAs: A spotted deer — fallow or axis. This one is identifiable, and is the strongest render in the batch.
rows.defect: Two mustReads land, one is doubtful, and the construction is visibly seamed. (1) Branched sweeping antlers — YES, genuinely branched with multiple forward tines, well drawn, and they carry the whole identification. (2) Slender legs and a long thin neck — YES, both read. (3) DOUBTFUL: the large upright cupped ears are effectively missing. All I can find is one small dark shape tucked at the antler base; there is no big upright cupped ear in silhouette, and on a deer the ear should be roughly as long as the face and clearly visible against the sky. SEAMS: a bright hairline runs the length of the topline at the neck-to-back join, and hard-edged darker tan trapezoids with straight vertical boundaries sit at both the shoulder and the rump — the black spots even stop dead on those boundaries in places, which advertises the seam. Worse, the tail is a hard-edged solid brown CIRCLE pasted flat on the rump with a crisp outline and no shading — a pure off-body artifact, not a tail, and no white-tail flash. The legs meet the belly at a straight cut. COAT: the spots are flat opaque black blobs held at identical density and identical value on the sunlit back and in the belly shadow alike, with no size falloff toward the silhouette edge — so the pattern floats. They are also too black and too dense; a fallow or axis deer's spots are small, pale cream and arranged in rows along the flank. HEAD: subtract the antlers and the skull underneath is the shared module — same round cranium, same white-ringed eye, same tapered muzzle as the Coyote. A stranger would notice a swap only because the hardware came off with it; the skull itself is not carrying any deer identity.
rows.fix: Add the ears as real geometry — two large upright cupped ovals, face-length, angled outward and clearly clear of the antler bases, with a paler inner surface. Delete the pasted brown disc and build a proper tail: a short flat flag lying against the rump, white on the underside. Erase the two rump/shoulder trapezoid borders and the topline hairline; carry the spot field continuously across those joins. Recolour the spots to pale cream, shrink them, arrange them in horizontal rows along the flank, fade them out on the belly and neck, and multiply them by the body shading so they darken in shadow. Give the skull deer character independent of the antlers: longer straight nasal bridge, a large dark lateral eye set high and far back, and a black nose pad on a white muzzle band.

rows.readsAs: a small pale lamb or piglet standing on four stubby cone legs
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. No spade forepaws — the forelimbs are the same tapering cones as the hindlimbs, planted mid-torso rather than beside the head. No pink pointed fleshy snout — the muzzle is a broad grey-brown ungulate taper ending in a dark oval nose dot. Not neckless and not cylindrical: there is a defined neck, a shoulder step and a sheep-like scalloped belly. The reference says eyes: hidden, but a large white cartoon eyeball with a dark pupil sits on the cheek, plus a dark round ear disc — mole has neither. SEAM: a dead-straight hard bright line runs the full length of the topline from rump to shoulder with a crisp cut at each end; it is inside the silhouette along the neck/back join, not a rim light. The dark rump patch is a hard-edged decal with no coat texture crossing it. Head is the batch's generic template — dome cranium + dark ear circle + white eye + tapering muzzle + nose dot — swap it with Mongoose or Mountain Tapir and nobody would see the change. Aspect reads ~2.0, short of the 2.6 called for.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a fossorial body plan, not an ungulate one: one continuous cylinder from nose tip to tail with no shoulder step and no neck taper. Replace the forelimbs with broad outward-turned pink spade paws set at the extreme front, palms facing out, claws visible, wider than they are long. Retract the hindlimbs to near-stubs. Delete the eye and the ear disc entirely; leave a faint dark velvet crease where the eye would be. Retip the muzzle in pink with a star-lobed or at minimum pointed fleshy nose extending past the jaw. Kill the straight topline highlight — replace with a soft broad falloff that follows the cylinder. Stretch to 2.6 aspect.

rows.readsAs: a pale tan foal or whippet with a bottlebrush tail
rows.defect: mustRead 1 fails outright: this is not a long low body on short legs. The legs are long straight tubes taking roughly half the standing height and the belly clears the ground by more than the torso's own depth — a mongoose's belly nearly drags. mustRead 3 fails: the tail is a black bristle brush of separate straight spikes, not a thick tail tapering to a point; it also terminates in a blunt pale stub. mustRead 2 partially fails — the snout tapers but the ears are absent (I can find only a faint notch on the skull crown; no small round ear is drawn). FEET: the legs end in open-ended elliptical tube cuts with a visible darker inner ellipse — they read as hollow pipes, no foot or paw at all. SEAM: same hard straight bright line along the entire topline as the Mole, plus hard V-shaped crease lines at the belly where each leg cylinder cuts into the torso. Head is the shared template — dome + brown cap patch + white eye + taper — interchangeable with Mole and Mountain Tapir.
rows.fix: Drop the leg length to roughly one third of what is drawn and thicken them so the belly rides just above the ground line; that single change buys most of the mongoose read. Give the legs actual plantigrade feet with five short toes and claws, closing off the open tube ends. Rebuild the tail as one solid mass, thick at the base where it grows out of the rump and tapering continuously to a point, with the bristle handled as coat texture on that solid rather than as free-floating spikes. Add two small round ears set low and wide on the skull. Remove the topline seam line and the leg-junction creases.

rows.readsAs: a moose — this one is legible without a label
rows.defect: Strongest render in the batch: the long overhanging muzzle with the bulbous nose, the palmate antlers and the very long legs all land, and the head could not be swapped with anything else here. Remaining faults. (1) The bell under the throat is at best hinted — there is a pale curved band under the jaw but it reads as a lighting seam, not as a hanging pendulous dewlap with its own silhouette. (2) SEAM: a thin razor-edged pure-white sliver runs along the neck-to-back junction, starting and stopping abruptly inside the body; it is a join highlight, not form shading. (3) The eye is a white outline ring with a dark centre — it reads as a metal grommet punched into the skull, and the near antler's palm crosses directly over it and over the ear, so the two most expressive features of the head are occluded by a prop. (4) The dark brown patches on the shoulder cap, the hip and the rump have hard vector edges with no coat strokes crossing them — stuck-on decals rather than coat markings. (5) The humped shoulder reads as a lumpy bulge with a saddle dip behind it rather than a withers rising into the neck. (6) Antlers are flat horizontal paddles with straight comb tines and no thickness or beam.
rows.fix: Add a genuine bell: a distinct pendulous flap of skin hanging below the throat line, breaking the silhouette, with its own shadow where it meets the jaw. Delete the white join sliver and let the neck read as a continuous surface into the shoulder. Move the antler beams up and back so they clear the eye and the ear, and give each antler a short round beam before the palm flares. Replace the ring eye with a solid dark almond eye set low and forward on the long skull. Feather the brown patches — let coat strokes cross the boundary and vary the edge so they sit in the fur. Reshape the shoulder so the hump is the highest point of the topline and slopes continuously into the neck instead of dipping first.

rows.readsAs: a white pony or a shaggy white sheep with tan horns
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads fail. Horns: they are pale tan and sweep forward in a long shallow curve — the reference calls for SHORT, only slightly curved, BLACK dagger horns. As drawn they read chamois or young ibex, and the colour is the same beige used for the Nilgai and Musk Ox horns, so it carries no species information. Pantaloons: absent — the legs are smooth flat white tubes with no shag at all from the elbow down, which is the single most recognisable mountain goat feature after the horns. Beard: not present as a distinct hanging tuft; there is undifferentiated shag under the jaw. COAT: the white hair is a spray of straight thin quills radiating outward from the silhouette edge and streaking straight across the body, ignoring the barrel's curvature and unshaded by it — it floats over the form rather than lying on it, and it reads closer to porcupine or thistle than to a deep winter coat. The grey circle on the rump is a hard-edged decal. The muzzle is a long horse-like taper with a drawn mouth line, not the goat's short blunt Roman muzzle; the grey ring around the eye reads as a badger mask. Swap this head onto the Nilgai and only the colour would give it away.
rows.fix: Recolour the horns to glossy black, shorten them to roughly half their drawn length, and stand them nearly upright with only a slight backward hook so they read as daggers. Add pantaloons: extend the coat mass down the outside of each leg to below the knee and hock as a defined shaggy silhouette, leaving only the lower cannon bare. Add a separate wedge beard hanging under the chin. Rebuild the coat so the strands follow the barrel's curve and are shaded by it — darker where the body turns away, brighter on the shoulder and hip crest — and confine the outward strand tips to the silhouette edge instead of firing them across the body interior. Shorten and blunt the muzzle and remove the grey eye ring.

rows.readsAs: a grey donkey or a scruffy grey goat
rows.defect: The defining mustRead is missing: there is no prehensile snout. The muzzle is the batch's standard tapering wedge ending in a rounded tip with a small dark oval nose — no mobile fleshy proboscis, no overhang past the lower jaw, no downward curl. Without it this cannot read as a tapir at all. White-rimmed lips also absent — the lip is a single drawn grey line with no pale rim. Coat is grey-brown with streaky strokes rather than the thick black wool called for, and the strokes stick out as stiff separate spikes above the back and around the throat and belly, which reads as bristle or quill rather than wool; they cross the body interior without being shaded by it. The back is close to flat, not the stocky high arch. The ear is drawn as two overlapping brown circles that read as a doubled or duplicated shape. Hard-edged dark blob on the hip; a hard diagonal edge behind the head where the neck plate overlaps the shoulder; the same bright hard line along the topline as the Mole and Mongoose. Head is the shared template — dome cranium, dark ear disc, big white cartoon eye, tapering muzzle — indistinguishable from the Mole's and Mongoose's.
rows.fix: Build the proboscis as the first move: a short thick flexible trunk growing out of the front of the skull, overhanging the lower jaw and curving down, with the nostrils at its tip — it must break the muzzle silhouette, not sit inside it. Add a clear white rim to the upper and lower lips and a white ear fringe. Darken the coat toward black and rebuild the texture as clumped soft wool that follows and is shaded by the barrel, removing every straight spike that projects across or beyond the body. Raise the mid-back into a pronounced arch and thicken the neck into a low crest. Fix the doubled ear to a single shape. Remove the topline highlight line and the neck-plate edge.

rows.readsAs: a beige shaggy sheep wearing a cream monocle
rows.defect: Both signature mustReads fail. Horns: instead of a broad helmet-like boss meeting across the forehead then hooking down and out, two cream tubes form a large closed RING that loops down across the middle of the face — it reads as a handlebar moustache or a monocle laid over the muzzle, and it completely occludes the eye, which I cannot find at all. There is no boss: no fused horn plate across the forehead, and the horn bases sit as thin separate stalks. Curtain of hair: the qiviut does not hang. The belly line is high and the four legs are bare pale tubes clear from hoof to elbow — the hair stops well above the knee, so the low-slung curtain silhouette that defines this animal is absent. COAT: the strands are straight stick-like straws scattered across the body at many angles and projecting beyond the silhouette in all directions, sitting on top of a smooth blob and unshaded by it — thatch, not a hanging pelage. SEAM: a hard bright white line runs along the back/neck join with a razor edge. The pale saddle patch is right in principle but its boundary is a hard vector edge with no hair crossing it. The skull under the horn prop is the same generic dome-plus-taper as the rest of the batch; only the (incorrect) horn accessory distinguishes it.
rows.fix: Rebuild the horns from the boss outward: a single wide fused helmet plate covering the whole forehead between the ears, from which the horns drop steeply down along the cheeks, then hook sharply UP and OUT to points clear of the face. They must never cross in front of the muzzle and must never cover the eye — put a small dark eye visible below the boss edge. Drop the coat curtain to just above the hooves on all four sides so the silhouette becomes a hair skirt with only the lower cannon and hoof showing; the belly line should be near the ground. Re-author the hair as long parallel vertical hanks that hang with gravity and are shaded by the body behind them, not as scattered straws at random angles. Soften the saddle boundary with hair crossing it, and delete the white back seam. Carry the head lower than the shoulder hump.

rows.readsAs: a grey antelope or a young grey horse — the family reads, the species does not
rows.defect: Two mustRead sub-features fail. The horns are tan crescents curving up and forward in a banana arc; the reference calls for SHORT STRAIGHT forward-pointing horns, and the beige colour is shared with the Mountain Goat and Musk Ox so it carries no identity. The throat beard tuft is entirely absent — the throat is smooth grey with nothing hanging from it. Coat is neutral grey, not slate blue-grey; there is no blue cast to make the bull read. What works: the topline does slope down from high shoulders, and the build is right. Remaining faults. The shoulder cap and hip cap are flat grey patches with hard vector edges pasted on a lighter body — decals, and they are the same two shapes in the same two places as on the Moose, which is why the two animals share a silhouette language. The belly is a row of scalloped bulges with visible boundaries between them, so the torso reads as three overlapping spheres rather than one solid barrel. The tail is a plain grey tube ending in a dark oval blob — a pinned-on lollipop, not a tuft growing out of the rump. There is a hard diagonal edge where the neck meets the shoulder and a light band along the back that terminates in a straight cut. HEAD: dome cranium, dark ear disc, big white cartoon eye, long horse taper with a drawn mouth line and a nose notch — the identical construction used on the Mountain Goat and the Mountain Tapir. Recolour the Mountain Goat's head grey and it would pass as this animal.
rows.fix: Straighten the horns: short, near-straight, angled forward, and recoloured dark so they stop matching the other two horned animals in the batch. Add the throat beard as a distinct dark tuft hanging from the mid-neck and breaking the throat silhouette. Push the coat toward slate blue-grey and add the white throat patch and white fetlock socks that separate a nilgai bull from any generic antelope. Merge the belly scallops into one continuous barrel volume. Feather the shoulder and hip caps into the coat and vary their shapes so they are not the Moose's caps recoloured. Rebuild the tail so it grows thick out of the rump and carries a black tuft rather than a detached oval. Remove the neck-to-shoulder edge and the truncated back band.

rows.readsAs: A tan fawn or a fennec-eared jackal pup — nothing about it says cat
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS: the ear tufts do not exist. The ears are two oversized rounded rabbit/bat lobes with a brown rim and a lighter inner cup; there is not one black hair trailing off either tip. The head is the batch's shared rounded-skull template with a short blunt snout and a nose dot — it is the Cheetah/Civet skull with bigger ears bolted on, so headUnique is false; a caracal skull is a short deep wedge with a high flat forehead and the eyes set forward, none of which is present. Hard lines are visible: a straight diagonal crease runs from the withers down the shoulder, the topline is a flat plank with a hard straight upper edge, and a lighter tan panel at the tail root ends in straight cut edges against the rump. The front leg reads as a separate cylinder overlapping the chest with a visible vertical boundary rather than growing out of it. The coat is uniform flat tan with two airbrushed dark ovals standing in for shoulder and haunch — those ovals are shadow decals, they do not describe muscle, so the coat is floating. Long powerful hind legs do not read; fore and hind legs are the same length and the same cone.
rows.fix: Draw the tufts as actual geometry: 2-3 black hairs, ~35% of ear height, springing from the tip and continuing the ear's line. Halve the ear width and make them narrow triangles set close together. Replace the shared skull with a short deep felid wedge — forehead above the eye, muzzle length under 25% of skull length, forward-facing eyes with a visible cheek ruff. Kill the topline plank and the shoulder crease; blend the shoulder/haunch as value on the coat, not as a pasted oval. Lengthen and angle the hind limb so the hock sits above and behind the stifle.

rows.readsAs: A reindeer — this one lands as the right animal
rows.defect: The antlers read and the neck ruff reads, so a stranger names it correctly. Two mustRead gaps remain: there is no forward brow shovel — both beams are the same flat ribbon with evenly spaced tines, no palmated plate over the face — and the hooves are narrow dark points, not wide splayed snowshoe pads. Artifacts: the shaggy fringe is scattered over the ENTIRE silhouette, not just the neck, and dozens of dark spikes are drawn INSIDE the body — crossing the mid-flank and hanging between the legs — so the animal looks impaled with straw rather than furred. A flat brown disc sits on the rump with a hard circular edge, a second smaller brown blob at the withers, both clearly pasted rather than grown. A hard pale straight line runs the length of the topline (the same seam highlight that appears on Chamois and Cheetah). The antler beams meet the skull as squared-off sticks with no basal pedicle blending.
rows.fix: Add a palmated brow shovel on the near beam sweeping forward over the nose. Widen and round the hoof into two splayed pads. Confine the fringe to the throat/neck and clip every hair to the outside of the silhouette — no strokes inside the body mask. Delete the rump and withers discs. Remove the straight topline highlight and let the back edge be a soft form turn. Thicken the antler base into a pedicle that swells out of the skull.

rows.readsAs: A pale small dog or goat with a brown fern frond stuck to its ribs — and it is so dark on the dark ground it barely reads at all
rows.defect: Exposure blocker first: this card renders 2-3 stops darker than every other image in the batch, the silhouette nearly dissolves into the background, and I had to lift it 3.2x to judge it. mustRead FAILS on the pupil: the eye is a tiny white ring with a round black dot, no vertical slit at any zoom, and whiskers are two faint strokes that disappear at full size. The tabby marking is not tabby — it is a single large feather/fern frond, a central rib with barbs radiating off both sides, laid flat on the flank; it does not wrap the barrel, does not compress toward the silhouette edge, and terminates in a hard straight cut at the shoulder. That is a coat floating over the body, plainly. A large flat lavender-grey trapezoid covers the hindquarter and tail root with a hard straight edge against the flank — a pasted hip plate, a seam. The head is the shared rounded skull; the dark cap meets the pale neck along a hard line. Proportions read canine: long straight legs, deep chest, level back, none of the cat's low crouching topline.
rows.fix: Raise the base value of the whole coat by 25-30% so it separates from the ground. Replace the frond with real tabby: vertical bands that run over the ribs and bend with the barrel, plus a spine stripe. Draw a vertical slit pupil at least 3px wide and 8px tall, and put 5-6 white whiskers with visible arc. Delete the grey hip trapezoid and blend the haunch into the flank. Shorten the legs, drop the chest, and give the head a real cat dome with high triangular ears and a visible whisker pad.

rows.readsAs: A giraffe or an okapi — not a cow, not even close
rows.defect: The coat is textbook reticulated giraffe: orange-brown polygonal plates separated by pale seams, and they are on the face as well as the body. mustRead FAILS twice more on the head: the muzzle is a long narrow tapering snout with a rounded tip, not a broad blunt bovine muzzle, and the horns are two pale tan prongs pointing UP and slightly forward from the crown, not sideways-set. The patch field is a flat 2D mesh — cell size is uniform from spine to belly with no foreshortening at the silhouette edge — so the coat is unambiguously floating over the body, and it is clipped by hard straight diagonal boundaries at the shoulder and rump where the patches simply stop and pale grey begins. The tail is a blocker on its own: the tuft is a dark grey egg-shaped blob detached from the tail tip, floating in empty space, and the tail root is a flat lavender pentagon slab pasted over the hip with hard straight edges. Faceted polygon lines are visible across the belly and shoulders. Body colour is a cold lavender-white that reads plastic. Credit where due: the level back and the cloven hooves are right.
rows.fix: Delete the reticulated patch generator for bovines entirely — use broad soft-edged Holstein blotches or a plain solid coat that follows the barrel. Rebuild the skull: short broad box muzzle, wide flat nose plane, heavy jaw. Re-aim the horns outward and sideways from the poll with a slight upward curl. Re-attach the tail tuft to the tail tip and make it a hair switch, not an egg. Remove the pentagon tail-root plate and let the tail emerge from the rump. Warm the coat off lavender.

rows.readsAs: A generic tan goat or a young deer
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads FAIL outright. The horns are two pale tan prongs rising nearly straight up with only a faint forward lean — there is no sharp backward hook at the tips, which is the single feature that identifies a chamois. There is no black-and-white facial mask: the face is plain warm brown with a slightly darker crown, no white cheek, no dark eye-to-muzzle stripe. What remains is the shared ungulate skull with a long horse-like tapered muzzle — swap this head with the Caribou's (antlers off) or the Cattle's and nobody in the room would notice, so headUnique is false; the chamois face is short and blunt, not this long snout. Artifacts: a flat brown disc with a hard circular edge sits on the rump and a matching brown patch on the shoulder, both pasted rather than grown out of the coat. A hard pale straight line runs along the topline. The torso is a smooth balloon with two airbrushed shadow ovals for haunch and shoulder — no muscle, coat sitting on nothing. The legs are slim, which is right, and the cloven hooves are correct.
rows.fix: Rebuild the horns: slim black spikes rising vertically then hooking through a tight 90-degree backward curl at the top third. Paint the mask as real geometry — white muzzle and cheek, a hard black band from the horn base through the eye to the nose, black chin. Shorten the muzzle by about a third and deepen the jaw. Delete the rump and shoulder discs. Remove the topline seam line and replace the two shadow ovals with form shading that turns with the barrel.

rows.readsAs: A Dalmatian, or an appaloosa-spotted lurcher
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on the tear stripes: below the eye there are only two or three tiny dark dashes, indistinguishable in size and shape from the surrounding spot field — there is no continuous black line running eye to mouth. mustRead FAILS on the body: this is a thick barrel with a deep belly and moderate legs, not a greyhound — no whippet waist, no deep narrow chest, no tuck-up. Spots are solid and round in places, which is right, but across the shoulder and upper flank they have merged into large irregular amoeba blobs, which reads Dalmatian rather than cheetah, and the legs are left completely unspotted plain cream. The head is the batch's shared rounded skull with a snub muzzle and a big brown nose dot; the ear is a flat brown circle pasted on the side of the skull with a hard circular edge, reading like a bear-ear sticker. This head is interchangeable with the Civet's — headUnique is false. Seams: a hard straight grey highlight line runs the length of the spine, the rump carries a flat unspotted tan trapezoid with straight edges where the tail attaches, and the front leg meets the chest along a visible vertical edge.
rows.fix: Draw the tear stripe as one continuous black band from the inner eye corner down to the mouth line, at least 3x the width of a spot, and exclude the spot generator from that region. Re-proportion the body: raise the chest depth, cut the waist in hard, lengthen the legs by roughly 20%, arch the back. Cap spot size and enforce minimum spacing so none merge; carry the spots down the legs and onto the tail. Replace the circular ear decal with a small ear that grows from the skull with a shaded base. Remove the spine highlight line and the rump trapezoid.

rows.readsAs: A smaller, shorter-tailed copy of the Cheetah in the same batch
rows.defect: This is the Cheetah picture at a different scale — same cream coat, same black blotch generator, same rounded skull, same brown circular disc ear, same white-ringed round eye, same leg cones. That duplication alone is a blocker. mustRead FAILS on the muzzle, which the reference row calls out explicitly: it is short, rounded and blunt, not long and pointed. mustRead FAILS on the mask: there is a single large round black blob sitting behind and below the eye, which is just an oversized spot from the same generator — no band runs THROUGH the eye, and there is no second band or contrasting white to make it read as a mask. mustRead FAILS on the build: the body is leggy and stands tall like the ungulates in this batch, not low and elongated on short legs. The tail is the one partial win — it does carry two or three dark bands — but it is a short thick club held low, not the long ringed tail. headUnique is false and it is the worst case in the batch. Seams: hard straight highlight along the spine, and a visible edge where the pale foreleg column meets the chest.
rows.fix: Fork the viverrid head off the felid template: extend the muzzle to roughly 40% of skull length and taper it to a point, add a small pointed nose, set the eyes further forward, and swap the disc ear for a small rounded ear that grows out of the skull. Paint the mask deliberately — a dark band across the eye onto the muzzle plus a pale brow spot, excluded from the spot generator. Shorten the legs by about a third and stretch the torso so the back is long and low. Lengthen the tail to at least body length with 6-8 even dark rings. Coarsen the spots into longitudinal rows so it stops reading as cheetah stippling.

rows.readsAs: a tan hyena-ish dog flecked with black mould spatter
rows.defect: mustRead 'two black stripes on each cheek' is entirely absent — the face is plain tan. The rosettes are not chain rosettes in streaks: they are randomly clustered black flyspeck blobs, dense on the shoulder, sparse mid-flank, absent on haunch and legs, so they read as splatter, not a coat pattern. HEAD IS GENERIC: identical construction to Otter, Pampas Fox and Pangolin in this same batch — same round skull blob, same single big white-ringed eye at the same spot, same tapering wedge muzzle with a small dark oval nose, same thin drawn mouth line, same single dark ear patch on top. Only the colour differs; the ear is a flat brown disc stuck dead-centre on the crown with a hard edge, and there is an angular notch/step in the silhouette where the skull meets the neck. SEAMS: a hard straight horizontal rule runs the full length of the back separating a lighter dorsal band from the flank, and the haunch cap is a darker tan panel with a crisp vertical boundary against the flank. Nothing about the build says housecat — the leg length and depth of chest read dog.
rows.fix: Add the two black malar stripes per cheek and the dark ear-back with white ocellus. Rebuild the pattern as elongated chain rosettes (dark rings with a tawny centre) organised into horizontal streaks along the flank, continuing onto haunch and upper leg. Kill the dorsal rule and the haunch-cap edge — grade both across the form. Give the cat family its own skull: short blunt muzzle, high rounded cranium, forward-set eye, two erect triangular ears set wide at the corners of the skull, not one disc on the crown.

rows.readsAs: a scorched zebra-donkey with a palm frond burnt into its side
rows.defect: The striping fails its mustRead twice over. Position: the stripes cover the neck, face, shoulder and mid-flank while the HINDQUARTERS AND UPPER LEGS — the only place an okapi is striped — are plain. Form: on the torso they are not horizontal white bands but a ragged dark fan with spiky feathered edges, reading as a palm leaf or a burn scar laid over the body. A hard-edged dark RECTANGLE with crisp straight corners sits on the upper flank as an obvious geometric artifact. The body is mid-tan, not the deep chocolate called for, so there is no dark-body/white-stripe contrast at all. Coat clearly floats: the bands cut straight across the head and muzzle silhouette without bending to the form. A bright rim-light stroke along the top of the back overshoots the silhouette. Tail is a thin tube plugged into the rump with a hard join.
rows.fix: Invert the pattern placement — chocolate body and neck, crisp white horizontal stripes confined to rump, thigh and upper foreleg, fading out before the hock. Delete the fan/frond brush and the rectangle primitive. Deepen the body colour to chocolate with reddish rump. Wrap stripe geometry around the barrel so they curve with the haunch. Clip the rim light to the silhouette. Head is genuinely species-specific (ossicones plus long giraffid muzzle) — keep it, but take the stripes off the face and give it the dark mask with pale cheeks.

rows.readsAs: a cream antelope with rapier horns wearing a skull mask
rows.defect: Horns are correct and excellent — long, straight, ridged, swept back — and the blocky cream body with slender legs and split hooves is right. Two failures. (1) mustRead 'bold black LEG markings' is missing entirely: the legs are plain cream top to hoof, no black knee blazes or garters. (2) The facial mask has collapsed into two large solid black discs on the cheek with the actual eye — a tiny white ring — squeezed BETWEEN and above them, half-buried under the horn base, so the face reads as a three-eyed skull rather than an oryx blaze. The same two-black-disc motif is used on the Panda in this batch, which makes the face-marking system read as generic. The tail tassel is a grey ellipse DETACHED from the tail shaft with a visible gap. Shoulder and haunch are soft airbrushed grey ovals sitting on the surface like balloons rather than muscle, and there is a crisp diagonal facet edge at the top of the rear flank.
rows.fix: Add the black leg markings: dark garter above the knee on all four, black stripe down the foreleg front. Replace the two discs with the real oryx mask — a dark blaze down the nose bridge, a dark band through the eye, a dark cheek patch — and put the eye INSIDE the eye band, clear of the horn base. Reattach the tail tassel to the shaft. Convert the airbrushed ovals into shading that follows the shoulder blade and femur, and grade out the flank facet.

rows.readsAs: a pale dachshund-weasel with a rope for a tail
rows.defect: mustRead 'thick tapering muscular tail' FAILS — the tail is a thin uniform rope about a fifth the body's depth, with no muscular base and no taper. mustRead 'broad whiskered muzzle' FAILS — the muzzle is a narrow pointed wedge with a small nose dot and no whiskers at all. HEAD IS GENERIC: the same skull, eye, nose and mouth-line construction as Ocelot, Pampas Fox and Pangolin; recolour it tan and it is the Pangolin's head exactly. SEAMS: the tail root plugs into a darker brown collar at the rump with a crisp vertical hard edge — an obviously stuck-on part; the dark head meets the pale chest along a crisp line with a straight-edged pale wedge abutting it; a rim-light line along the back terminates abruptly mid-body. COAT FLOATS: the torso is covered in straight horizontal hatch strokes that run dead level from end to end and never bend around the barrel or the shoulder. Shoulder and hip are flat airbrushed grey circles. Feet split into two detached pebble blobs.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as a thick muscular cone rooted continuously in the rump — full body depth at the base, tapering to a point over roughly 60% of body length — and delete the collar. Broaden and blunt the muzzle, add a pale whisker pad with visible whiskers, and shrink the ears to flush nubs. Bend the fur hatching along the barrel's cross-section. Blend the head/neck colour transition over 8–10px instead of an edge. Merge the toe blobs into one webbed foot.

rows.readsAs: a small pale pony or donkey with a bottle-brush stuck on the rump
rows.defect: Nothing here reads canid. mustRead 'pointed narrow muzzle with large triangular ears' FAILS on both halves — the muzzle is a broad blunt tapering wedge with a blobby nose, and the ears are two SMALL rounded lobes fused into a heart shape on the crown, not large erect triangles set wide. mustRead 'long bushy dark-tipped tail carried low' FAILS — the tail is carried raised and curled UP over the rump and its tip is a PALE round blob, not dark. mustRead 'grizzled grey back with tawny legs' FAILS — back and legs are the same flat pale cream with no grizzle and no tawny. HEAD IS GENERIC: strip the ears and it is the Ocelot/Otter/Pangolin head — same skull, same single ringed eye, same nose blob, same mouth line, same rear notch. Legs are long and slender ending in blunt two-toe hoof nubs, ungulate not paw. The tail bristles are individual straight strokes, many of which fly off into empty space as detached spikes clear of the tail mass — off-body artifacts. Shoulder and haunch are the same airbrushed grey ovals as the Oryx, and a hard diagonal polygon facet cuts the shoulder.
rows.fix: Give the canid family a real skull: long narrow tapering snout, flat forehead, and two large separate erect triangular ears at the outer corners of the head. Drop the tail to hang below the hock, thicken it, and darken the distal third to near-black. Repaint the coat grizzled grey-black over the back and shoulders with tawny/rufous on legs and muzzle sides. Replace hoof nubs with four-toed digitigrade paws. Contain the bristle strokes inside the tail silhouette and grade out the shoulder facet.

rows.readsAs: a Holstein cow, or a harlequin great dane, with a rat's face
rows.defect: The black markings are two enormous solid TRIANGLES — one on the shoulder, one on the haunch — with razor-straight edges and a scalloped arc cutting their base. They are flat cut-out shapes lying over the body with no shading from the form whatsoever, the clearest case of a floating coat in the batch. mustRead 'black shoulder band joining black forelegs' FAILS: the triangle stops at that arc and the forelegs below are WHITE. mustRead 'very round head' FAILS: the head is an elongated rat-like wedge with a long pointed muzzle and a long straight grey mouth line. mustRead 'black teardrop eye patches' FAILS in form — they are two large solid black CIRCLES on the cheek with the eye, a tiny white ring, wedged BETWEEN them; the same motif as the Oryx face in this batch. Per the note, the ears should be black and round: the ear is a large GREY disc with a pink centre. The tail should be white and visible: it is a grey oval blob stuck on the rump with a hard edge. SEAMS everywhere: a crisp dark arc where the belly mass meets the legs, a hard vertical seam at the front of the torso where the neck plate meets the shoulder, a hatched grey neck panel with a hard boundary against the white body, and flat polygonal facets on the cheek and crown. Feet are grey capsules split into two detached pebbles.
rows.fix: Redraw the markings as anatomical bands with soft edges that shade with the body: a black saddle band across the shoulders that continues DOWN into fully black forelegs, black hindlegs, black ears, white head/neck/back/rump, white stub tail. Round the skull hard — short blunt muzzle, wide cheeks, high forehead — and make the eye patches vertical teardrops that CONTAIN the eye. Recolour ears black. Remove the neck plate seam and the belly arc.

rows.readsAs: a tan dog with two artichoke fans glued to its back
rows.defect: mustRead 'overlapping keratin scales like a pinecone' FAILS — there is no scale field. The back carries two large radiating FANS of big flat petal shapes, one on the shoulder and one on the haunch, meeting in a hard V-notch, reading as an artichoke or a folded paper fan; no small overlapping imbricated plates, no pinecone tiling, and the flanks below the fans are bare. mustRead 'thick tapering tail as long as the body' FAILS badly — the tail is a thin curl roughly a quarter of body length. HEAD IS GENERIC: it is the Otter's head recoloured — identical skull blob, identical single white-ringed eye in the same position, identical nose blob and drawn mouth line, identical dark ear patch on the crown; and a pangolin should have no visible ear patch at all. OFF-BODY ARTIFACT: the pale rim-light stroke along the top of the back overshoots the silhouette and floats detached in the background above the shoulder. SEAM: the scale field terminates against the neck along a crisp straight diagonal cut with a bright pale line, so the armour reads as a decal ending rather than as plating that thins out. Legs are plain tubes with blunt paw ends — no enlarged digging foreclaws.
rows.fix: Replace the two fans with a continuous field of small overlapping teardrop scales, rows running across the body and shrinking toward the head and limbs, each scale shaded by the surface normal so the field curves over the barrel. Extend the tail to full body length, thicken it at the root and scale it too. Give it its own skull: tiny, smooth, conical, no ear patch, eye reduced to a dark bead set low and far forward. Clip the rim light to the silhouette. Feather the scale field into the bare neck and belly skin instead of cutting it. Add long curved foreclaws.

rows.readsAs: A sandy cartoon anteater-pony: a straight-backed tan body on peg legs, a long down-curved snout tube, and a straw feather-duster where the tail should be. Nobody would say 'wild dog'.
rows.defect: THREE mustReads fail. (1) White feet absent — all four feet are dark tan blunt pegs that read as hooves, not paws; no toes, no pads (verified at 5x crop). (2) Ears are not erect pointed triangles — they are two rounded dark petal shapes meeting in a heart on the crown, no points, set too far back. (3) The tail is not a bushy straight brush — it is a straw broom of loose dark bristles radiating well OUTSIDE the tail silhouette from a tan cone with a white tip; an off-body artifact, not fur. The 'lean wolfish frame' also fails: the torso is the batch's shared straight-topped slab sitting on two belly spheres, no chest, no waist tuck. SEAMS: a dead-straight back edge with a bright hard rim line ending in a sharp corner; hard-edged orange facet patches at shoulder and haunch; a V-notch crease at mid-belly where the two spheres meet; each leg caps onto the belly sphere with a visible overlap edge. COAT: floating — the concentric ring texture runs across the torso ignoring the shoulder and haunch volumes, and the ginger patches are flat decals with hard boundaries.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a canid, not an ungulate on the ungulate rig: paw feet with toes and white socks; sharp isoceles ears with real points; a canid skull with a stop, a cheek mass and a jaw instead of a stuck-on snout tube; replace the bristle-fan tail with a solid tapered brush shaded by the body light. Kill the flat-slab topline — give the back a withers rise and a loin dip — and dissolve the belly-sphere V-notch into one continuous underline.

rows.readsAs: The Dingo again, one shade more orange. Same anteater snout, same googly eye, same broom tail.
rows.defect: It is functionally the same picture as Dingo — 79.3% silhouette IoU, the highest pair in the batch, and the head is pixel-for-pixel the same construction. mustRead 'plumed tail carried above the back' FAILS: the tail is the same straw-bristle broom and it hangs at/below the topline, never above it. Black nose reads (a small dot) and the ears are erect, but they are the Dingo's rounded petals, not dog ears. SEAMS: same slab back with hard rim highlight, same belly-sphere V-notch, same hard-edged shoulder facet. COAT: same flat decal patches over an unrelated ring texture.
rows.fix: Two canids in one batch cannot share a silhouette and a skull. Give the Dog a broader, shorter muzzle with a defined stop and a wider cranium than the Dingo's narrow wedge, and carry the tail as a solid plume arcing ABOVE the back line. Differentiate the body: domestic dog = deeper chest, less leg, softer topline than a dingo.

rows.readsAs: A grey pony with jackrabbit ears — the most legible ungulate here, and a stranger would probably land on 'donkey' or 'mule'.
rows.defect: mustRead 'short upright bristly mane' is ABSENT — the neck crest carries only a slightly paler band and a hairline highlight; no mane geometry, no bristle texture (checked at 3x). Long upright ears read well and the tufted rope tail reads well. LAYERING BUG: the eye is painted ON TOP of the near ear's base, so the ear passes behind and in front of the eye at once. SEAMS: a hard straight edge where the flat neck slab meets the shoulder; the bright back highlight terminates abruptly in a corner at the withers; hard-edged grey shoulder and haunch panels; the mid-belly V-notch between the two spheres. Silhouette is 66% identical to the Eland — the same animal minus horns. COAT: flat, the grey panels read as pasted patches rather than shaded planes of the body.
rows.fix: Add the erect brush mane along the crest — it is the donkey's signature and it also breaks the shared neck-slab. Move the eye forward and below the ear root so the ear can sit behind it. Round the neck-into-shoulder join instead of butting a slab against a facet, and give the donkey the reference's shorter, thicker neck and bigger head relative to the Eland so the two stop sharing an outline.

rows.readsAs: A pale llama or a small sauropod with a bread roll on its back. The hump is the only camel cue and it looks glued on.
rows.defect: TWO of three mustReads fail and the third is executed as a sticker. (1) The hump is a separate dome with its own hard outline and a visible step/notch on both sides where it meets the flat back — pasted, not grown. (2) 'Long curved neck rising from sloped shoulders' FAILS — the neck is a straight parallel-sided tube leaving square shoulders, no S-curve, no slope. (3) 'Long legs with knobbly knee pads and splayed padded feet' FAILS — the legs are plain tapered sticks with a faint ankle band, no knee pads, and the feet are narrow pegs with no splay and no pad. The camel also has NO EARS at all. SEAMS: hump/back join; a hard crease where the head blob meets the neck tube; stair-step pixel jaggies on the left belly-sphere edge; the usual straight-slab topline. COAT: floating flat sand with one hard-edged darker panel at the shoulder.
rows.fix: Make the hump part of the back curve — the topline should rise into it and fall out of it with no closing outline. Rebuild the neck as a curve (up out of a sloped shoulder, then forward) rather than a straight tube. Add the diagnostic camel feet: broad two-toed pads that splay wider than the leg, plus the knee callus. Add small ears. The head needs a camel's convex nose bridge and drooping lower lip, not the batch's shared wedge.

rows.readsAs: A brown goat kid or a young chamois. The small scale and the arched back do land, but the horns say goat.
rows.defect: mustRead 'tiny backswept spike horns' is INVERTED — the render gives two large pale crescents sweeping FORWARD and up over the face, ram/chamois horns pointing the opposite direction from the reference. 'Forehead tuft' is ABSENT. The arched hunched back DOES read (this is the only torso in the batch that is not a flat slab) and the small-antelope scale reads, though the legs are proportionally long rather than short. SEAMS: the mid-belly V-notch between the two spheres is present; the tail is a dark brown CIRCLE stuck on the rump with a hard unblended edge; hard-edged shoulder facet. Head construction is the batch-standard wedge muzzle plus the shared white googly eye. COAT: the best in the batch — the arch is genuinely shaded — but the flank patches are still hard-edged decals.
rows.fix: Turn the horns around: short straight spikes angled BACK along the skull line, roughly one eye-length long, not forward crescents. Add the forehead tuft between them — it and the horns together are the duiker's whole identity. Shorten the legs against the body depth so the crouch reads. Blend the tail into the rump instead of dropping a disc on it.

rows.readsAs: A cream kudu or oryx. The spiral horns are excellent; everything below the neck is the Donkey.
rows.defect: TWO mustReads fail. (1) 'Dewlap of loose skin under the throat' is ABSENT — the throat is a clean straight diagonal from jaw to chest, nothing hanging (checked at 5x). (2) 'Massive ox-like body with a shoulder hump' FAILS — the torso is the same medium straight-topped slab as the Donkey's (66% silhouette IoU) with no bulk and no withers hump; nothing about this body says ox. The tightly spiralled horns DO read and are the strongest single feature in the batch. SEAMS: a hard straight seam where the flat neck slab meets the shoulder; the bright rim highlight along the dead-straight back stops in a sharp corner; the mid-belly V-notch; hard-edged shoulder and haunch panels. COAT: floating flat cream, patches sit on top of the form rather than wrapping it.
rows.fix: Add the dewlap as a hanging fold of body silhouette, not a painted line — it should break the throat outline. Build the withers hump into the topline and thicken the barrel and neck substantially so the Eland outweighs the Donkey at a glance; right now only the horns separate them. Round the neck-to-shoulder join.

rows.readsAs: An elephant — the only unmistakable animal in the batch — but a hooded, mammoth-ish one wearing a large grey sticker on its shoulder.
rows.defect: TWO mustRead details fail. (1) 'Trunk reaching the ground' FAILS — the trunk curls and stops around knee height, clearly above the ground line. (2) 'Two grasping lips' FAILS — the tip is a blunt rounded stub with no finger or lip. The huge fan ear is present at the right SIZE but is rendered as one flat dark teardrop DECAL with a hard crisp outline, no base, no attachment to the skull, and it overlaps the torso — the worst stuck-on part in the batch. 'Pillar legs' is marginal: the columns with toenails read well but taper too much to be pillars. The dipped back is only partly there — the head/withers mass is a tall angular hooded wedge peaking well above the back, which reads mammoth rather than African savanna. Reference calls for SMALL eyes; the render uses the same big white-ringed googly eye as every ungulate in this batch. SEAMS: the ear outline; a hard-edged pale plate across the withers with a straight diagonal boundary; a visible stair-step jaggie where the rump sphere meets the back. COAT: the trunk's ridge banding is genuinely good; the body is flat pale grey with hard plates lying on top instead of wrapping.
rows.fix: Extend the trunk to touch or nearly touch the ground and finish it with the two-lipped tip — that is the silhouette everyone checks. Root the ear: taper it into the skull at the base with a soft edge and a fold, and lift the hard outline. Shrink the eye to a small dark slit and drop the white ring (it is the generic batch eye and it undercuts the one head here that is otherwise its own). Replace the hooded wedge skull with a domed forehead and a defined cheek, thicken the legs into true pillars, and clear the stair-step artifact at the rump.

rows.readsAs: A pale beige jackrabbit-eared whippet or a young donkey — a generic tan quadruped with big ears. Nobody would say 'aardvark'.
rows.defect: TWO mustReads fail. (1) No long tubular pig-like snout: the muzzle is a short tapered triangular wedge ending in a small dark nose bead — the same wedge on the Armadillo and the African Wild Dog. An aardvark snout is a narrow parallel-sided tube nearly as long as the skull; nothing here is tubular. (2) No thick tapering kangaroo tail: the tail is a thin uniform-width whip that curves down and stops, thinner than a hind leg, with no mass at the base. The arched back is the only mustRead that lands. HEAD IS A CLONE: at 4x, the head is pixel-for-pixel the same construction as the Armadillo — same two-tone leaf ear pair, same big white-ringed cartoon eye at the same position, same wedge muzzle, same dark nose dot, same single mouth line. Recolor the Armadillo head and you have this one; nobody would notice a swap. SEAMS: the tail base is a hard-edged tan RECTANGLE pasted onto the rump — crisp vertical and horizontal edges, a visible box against the haunch. There is a stair-step notch in the nape outline where the neck meets the shoulder. COAT: floating. Dead-horizontal hatch lines run straight across the whole barrel and continue unbroken over the shoulder and haunch masses without bending around them; the shoulder and haunch themselves are soft grey airbrushed ellipses smudged on top of the coat, not form emerging under it, and their lower edges scallop the belly into two hanging spheres.
rows.fix: Rebuild the snout as a long narrow tube of constant width, at least 0.45 of head length, with a flat disc nose at the tip and the eye pushed far back near the ear base (aardvark eyes sit almost at the skull rear). Give the tail a base as thick as the thigh, tapering over its length. Replace the rectangular tail-base with a swept blend into the rump mass. Bend the coat hatching to follow the barrel's cross-section and let it break/curve over the shoulder and haunch instead of running through them.

rows.readsAs: An elephant — unmistakably. The only animal in this batch a stranger would name correctly.
rows.defect: All three mustReads are present but the trunk falls short: it curls down and stops around knee height, well clear of the ground, so 'reaching the ground' is not met. The reference NOTE is violated: the topline rises continuously to the skull, making the head the highest point of the animal and the back convex — that is the Asian elephant profile the note explicitly excludes; there is no saddle-shaped concave dip. SEAMS: the ear is a hard-edged dark slab with a razor boundary against both cheek and shoulder — no rim, no fold, no lobe, and it takes no shading from the body it lies on, so it reads as a shield stuck on. The trunk base is a separate rounded knob overlapping the cheek with a visible hard edge rather than growing from the face. The tail base is a hard-edged darker slab pasted on the rump with a stair-step notch. There is an unexplained bright cream patch with a hard border on the upper back. The eye is the same white-ringed cartoon eye used on all seven animals and it sits awkwardly right on the ear's edge. COAT: the best in the batch — the hide hatching curves with the haunch sphere and genuinely wraps the form. The belly is still the batch's twin-sphere sag rather than a barrel.
rows.fix: Extend the trunk so the tip touches or coils on the ground. Lower the skull below the shoulder and cut a concave saddle into the back between shoulder and hip. Soften the ear boundary with a thickened rim and a fold, and shade its lower half by the shoulder behind it. Blend the trunk base into the brow and cheek instead of overlapping it as a disc. Remove the cream back patch or motivate it as a lit plane.

rows.readsAs: A young giraffe or an okapi foal. The reticulated tan-and-brown grid is the single loudest thing in the picture and it says giraffe.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on two of three. (1) The blotches are not irregular patchwork: they are a regular reticulated GRID of near-equal tan polygons separated by uniform brown lines — geometric, evenly spaced, giraffe-pattern, the opposite of the ragged asymmetric splotches the species is named for. (2) There is no BLACK and no WHITE anywhere in the coat; the whole palette is two tans and a brown, so the tri-colour requirement is entirely absent. (3) The ears are tall and POINTED at the tips, not huge and rounded — and at 4x they are the identical ear asset used on the Aardvark and Armadillo. The white brush tail tip does land. HEAD IS A CLONE: side by side with the Aardvark at 4x, same ear pair, same eye ring at the same spot, same wedge muzzle, same nose dot. Swap them and only the colour changes. SEAMS: there is a crisp straight diagonal line at the base of the neck where the neck plate meets the shoulder, and the grid pattern stops dead at it instead of carrying across; a step notch sits in the nape outline. COAT: floating — the grid is a flat overlay at a single scale, it does not compress toward the silhouette edges or wrap the ribs, and the shoulder and haunch show through as separate lighter ovals that the grid runs straight over.
rows.fix: Replace the grid generator with irregular blotch placement: variable-size, variable-shape patches with ragged edges, no connecting web. Force the tri-colour palette — true black patches, tan patches, and white patches on head, legs and tail. Round the ear tips into wide bat cups set low and wide on the skull. Project the blotches onto the body's cross-section so they foreshorten at the flanks and deform over the shoulder and haunch.

rows.readsAs: A weathered white llama-lizard, or a straw-stuffed scarecrow horse. The silhouette says camelid; the surface says wet straw.
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. (1) 'Dense woolly fleece covering the whole body' is rendered as sparse straight BRISTLES sticking OUT past the silhouette — quills fringing the outline like a scrub brush — plus a scatter of random white slash strokes on the flank at conflicting angles. The body surface underneath is smooth and bare. It reads as porcupine or wet straw, never as dense wool, and critically the wool adds no volume to the silhouette: real fleece should fatten the whole animal into a rounded cloud. (2) No topknot fringe at all, and the face is not blunt and short — at 4x it is a long flat wedge with a hooked snout tip that reads reptilian. (3) Ears are the batch's rounded two-tone cups, not short straight spear-shaped ears. HEAD IS A CLONE: strip the neck and it is the Aardvark head with shorter ears — same eye ring, same muzzle wedge, same nose. SEAMS: the tail is a solid grey CIRCLE with a hard crisp edge stuck on the rump — a coin, no taper, no direction. The neck front has a straight crisp edge with a pale stripe running down it, and there is a step at the jaw-to-neck junction. COAT: floating in the worst sense — the fleece strokes ignore the body entirely, and the shoulder and haunch are two big grey airbrushed spheres bulging BELOW the belly line, reading as a pair of hanging sacs rather than muscle inside the form.
rows.fix: Make the fleece a volume, not a texture: inflate the silhouette itself into soft overlapping wool lobes and shade them by the body's light, then add only short curl marks inside. Kill the outward bristles. Shorten and blunt the muzzle to about half its length with a squared-off nose pad, add a topknot lobe above the eyes. Rebuild the ears as short straight spears (banana-shaped, tips inward). Replace the coin tail with a short tapering fleece-covered stub. Pull the shoulder and haunch masses up inside the belly silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A teal alien deer or a mint-green unicorn foal. The colour is the first and loudest read; nobody would call this an earth antelope.
rows.defect: COLOUR IS A BLOCKER: the mustRead calls for a tan flank with a white belly and the render is saturated teal/turquoise head to hoof, including the belly. Nothing on the animal is tan or white except the horns. Second, the horns are smooth featureless pale tubes with no RINGING and no lyre curve — they rise vertically and splay into a plain V, reading as bare bone antennae; and the left horn's base sits on top of a dark teal ear leaf with no join, so it looks planted rather than grown. Third, 'deep chest' fails — the deepest point of the body is not the brisket but two soft grey spheres hanging below the belly line (the shoulder and haunch masses again escaping the silhouette), which scallops the underside into a lumpy double curve. The 'short flicking tail' is a hard-edged dark teal CIRCLE stuck on the rump — the same coin as the Alpaca, no taper, no direction, does not read as a tail at all. The fine legs and cloven hooves are the one thing that lands cleanly. HEAD: the horns do make it non-swappable and it does read as a gazelle, so this passes — but be aware the skull under the horns is the identical shared wedge (same eye ring, same nose, same mouth line) as the Aardvark and Armadillo; only the props differentiate it. The ears are almost invisible behind the horns. SEAMS: a crisp diagonal line runs from the cheek down into the neck, and a pale grey highlight band along the spine ends in a hard-edged wedge at the neck/shoulder junction.
rows.fix: Force the earth palette: tan/fawn flank, hard white belly and rump patch, dark flank stripe. Give the horns transverse rings and an S-curve or lyre sweep, and blend their bases into the brow with a fur collar. Replace the coin tail with a short tapering tail carrying a dark tip. Deepen the brisket and pull the shoulder/haunch spheres back inside the belly line so the chest, not the blobs, is the lowest body point. Add visible ears forward of the horns.

rows.readsAs: A white duck or seabird head on a bleached goat's body — or an albino deer. There is no fox anywhere in this picture.
rows.defect: Every mustRead fails. (1) 'Short rounded ears' — there are NO ears. At 4x, what sits on the skull is a flat pink-grey COIN painted flush on the side of the head with no relief, no pitch and no silhouette; it breaks the outline nowhere and reads as a second eye or an injury. The animal is earless. (2) 'Blunt short muzzle' — the muzzle is the longest and narrowest in the batch: a parallel-sided tube with a squared-off tip, exactly the opposite of the requirement, and it is what makes the head read as a bill. (3) 'Thick fluffy all-white coat and dense round tail' — the coat is flat porcelain white with soft airbrush gradients and zero fur texture, and the tail is a splayed fan of DARK GREY and black bristles, a chimney brush, on an animal that must be all white. Wrong shape and wrong colour on the same feature. FAMILY LIMB FAILURE: the legs are long slender cylinders ending in small dark HOOF caps — this is the ungulate leg used on the Antelope and Alpaca, not a fox's short paw with toes. HEAD: not swappable with another in the batch, but that is not a pass — it is not specific to arctic fox either; the tube muzzle plus coin ear reads as a bird, so the head fails to identify the species. SEAMS: the topline turns a hard angular corner at the shoulder, and the underside has a hard V notch mid-body where the fore and hind masses meet, with the shoulder and haunch showing as dirty grey airbrushed ovals floating on the white.
rows.fix: Halve the muzzle length and blunt the tip into a rounded nose pad. Build real ears: short wide rounded cones that break the head silhouette, with a shaded inner cup. Make the tail a dense round WHITE brush at least as thick as the body is deep, no dark bristles. Swap in the canid foot: short leg, visible paw with toes, no hoof cap. Give the white coat fur texture and a soft irregular silhouette so it reads as thick pelt rather than porcelain, and pull the grey shoulder/haunch smudges out of the white.

rows.readsAs: A small striped cat or a civet — a tabby-marked weasel. It reads as a mammal with stripes painted on, never as an armoured animal. Also rendered far too small in the 440px frame, with a large empty margin.
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS on all three. (1) 'Hinged bands of armour' — the marks are flat dark TRIANGULAR wedges hanging down from the spine and tapering to points at the flank: tiger stripes, not bands. They have no relief, no overlapping lip, no shadow under a leading edge, and crucially the topline silhouette is perfectly smooth where a banded carapace would be scalloped. They also run the whole length of the back rather than being a banded midsection between a solid scapular and pelvic shield. Nothing here reads as armour. (2) 'Long pointed snout with small tubular ears' — the snout is SHORT and blunt with a rounded nose bead, and the ears are the tall two-tone pointed leaf ears used on the Aardvark, not small tubes. (3) 'Tapering armoured tail' — the tail is a smooth bare tapering tube with no rings and no plating. HEAD IS A DIRECT CLONE: at 6x this is the Aardvark's head asset — identical ear pair, identical white-ringed eye, identical wedge muzzle, identical nose dot and mouth line, only the scale and tint differ. It could be swapped with the Aardvark and nobody would see it. SEAMS: the banded strip terminates in a hard straight horizontal edge where it meets the neck, with a step notch in the nape outline; the tail base is the same hard tan slab as the Aardvark's. FAMILY LIMB FAILURE: the legs are plain thin cylinders with rounded dark toe caps — no digging claws, which are the species' second-most identifiable feature after the shell. COAT: flat dot/hatch texture floating over the form; the shoulder and haunch read as separate lighter ovals that the stripes run straight across.
rows.fix: Rebuild the carapace as geometry, not paint: a domed shell that raises the back silhouette above the flesh line, a solid front shield and rear shield with 7-9 hinged transverse bands between them, each band scalloping the topline and casting a shadow on the one behind. Lengthen the snout into a narrow point and shrink the ears to small upright tubes set close together. Ring the tail with plated segments that taper to the tip. Add large curved front digging claws. Scale the whole animal up to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: A generic cartoon deer / mule deer buck in pale sandy tan
rows.defect: mustRead 'dark shaggy neck mane' is ABSENT — the neck is the same flat tan as the torso with the same diagonal hatch, no ruff, no color break, no shag. The antlers are the wrong architecture (two matching upright candelabra with tines pointing straight up, not a sweeping backswept elk rack) and they are rendered as flat, unshaded, untapered cream capsules — the only zero-form elements on an otherwise shaded body, so they read as bleached coral stuck behind the ear. Multiple SEAMS: a ruler-straight vertical line runs top-to-bottom through the rump dividing the pale panel from the darker one, a razor-straight white highlight streak runs the length of the spine, and there is a hard straight facet edge on the cheek. The tail is a flat brown CIRCLE pasted at the rump edge, half hanging outside the silhouette — it reads as a bullet hole, not a tail. The haunch is a soft egg laid over the rump rather than swelling out of it. Coat: the hatch texture is drawn in flat parallel diagonals that ignore the barrel of the ribcage and run straight across the panel boundary — printed on, not lying on. Cream rump patch does read.
rows.fix: Add a real mane: a darker, longer-fibre ruff mass on the ventral neck and throat that breaks the neck silhouette outward. Rebuild the rack as one asymmetric backswept beam per side with taper, a shaded brow tine, and body-lit shading so it is not the only flat object in frame. Kill the straight rump panel edge and the straight spine highlight — feather both. Replace the tail disc with a short tapered tail rooted inside the silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A tiny white donkey or a hare — a blank white body with rabbit ears and a feather duster on the back
rows.defect: The torso is CLIPPED TO PURE WHITE (255) across its whole area — no shading, no form, no coat, no light direction. There is literally no surface for a coat to lie on; the only modeling is two faint circular smudges at shoulder and haunch that read as bruises. The head is effectively MISSING: the near ear occludes the entire skull, leaving a thin white sliver of muzzle, a pinprick eye and a dot nose — no cranium, no cheek, no forehead. Ears are large (size mustRead passes) but they are rounded rabbit OVALS, not the broad triangular flare of a fennec, and their base sits directly on the shoulder with no neck. mustRead 'black-tipped bushy tail' FAILS: the tail is a blown-out solid white disc with straight radiating hair-strokes on one side — a dandelion clock, no taper, no black tip. Legs end in blunt hoof-like tips, not paws. Eye spec says 'prominent'; it is the smallest eye in the batch.
rows.fix: Pull the body value down 30-40% so it has a lit top and shadowed underside — nothing in this render should sit at pure white. Reshape the ears to triangles with a wide base and pointed tip, and shrink/offset the near ear so the skull, brow and cheek are actually visible in front of it. Rebuild the tail as a shaded tapering cylinder of fur with a distinct black terminal third. Enlarge the eye to match the 'prominent' spec.

rows.readsAs: A long-bodied tan greyhound with a dark head and a fern frond for a tail
rows.defect: HARD SEAM at the head/neck: a razor-straight diagonal boundary where the pale cream body meets the dark brown neck-and-head wedge — the head reads as a separate dark part slotted into a light body. Blocker. mustRead 'long LOW mustelid body' fails — the legs are long and straight and the belly clears the ground by more than the body's own depth; the proportions are a leggy dog, not a fisher. mustRead 'dark grizzled coat' fails — the body is pale sandy cream with flat horizontal banding, only the head is dark. mustRead 'blunt muzzle' fails — the muzzle is a sharp pointed wedge. The 'broad rounded ear' is a flat dark CIRCLE painted on the crown, not a projecting pinna. The tail is a leaf/feather with straight bristles on one edge and a glowing WHITE BEAD stuck on the tip — a fisher has no white tail tip, and the bead is an off-body artifact. There is a jagged faceted step in the outline at the back of the jaw. Coat sits as flat horizontal stripes that do not wrap the barrel.
rows.fix: Grade the dark head colour down the neck into the shoulder over 15-20px so there is no straight boundary. Halve the leg length and lengthen/lower the torso until the body reads longer than it is tall by 3:1. Push the grizzled dark colour across the whole coat, not just the head. Blunt the muzzle and build the ear as a projecting rounded pinna with an inner cup. Delete the white tail bead and rebuild the tail as a shaded tapering cylinder.

rows.readsAs: A spotted goat or a fallow deer fawn — anything but a cat
rows.defect: This is the Fisher's head RECOLOURED: identical wedge skull, identical flat disc ear on the crown, identical white-ringed cartoon eye, identical downturned mouth line, identical oval nose. Swap the two and nobody would notice — this is exactly the owner's complaint, made literal. Nothing cat about it: no short face, no broad cheeks, no whisker pads, no upright triangular ears, no forward-set binocular eyes. mustRead 'short thick tail' is ABSENT — there is no tail, only a flat grey CIRCLE pasted at the rump edge and half outside the silhouette (the same disc primitive as the Elk's). mustRead 'stocky heavy-boned cat body' fails — the body is a light, long-legged ungulate frame. mustRead 'rows of solid spots and neck stripes' fails — spots are randomly scattered hard-edged blobs with no rows and no neck striping. The spots are clipped dead by a ruler-straight vertical panel line at the rump and do not continue onto the pale panel: the coat is printed on a flat map, not lying on the form. Also a razor-straight white line streaks across the shoulder and along the spine.
rows.fix: Give it a cat skull: short muzzle, high domed cranium, wide cheeks, forward-facing eyes, and real triangular pinnae — it must not share geometry with the Fisher. Rebuild the body low, deep-chested and heavy-boned on short thick legs with paws. Add an actual short thick tail rooted inside the silhouette. Re-lay the spots in longitudinal rows that follow the barrel and continue across the rump panel, and add 4-5 dark neck stripes. Remove the straight panel edge and the straight spine highlight.

rows.readsAs: An elephant — the only immediately identifiable animal in the batch
rows.defect: The ear is a huge dark slab with a RULER-STRAIGHT top edge and a straight vertical leading edge meeting in a hard 90-degree corner — a cut-out plate pasted over the head and shoulder, the worst seam in the batch. It is also the wrong size and shape: it should be a rounded OVAL SMALLER than a savanna elephant's, and it is instead larger than the head and covers a third of the body. The EYE is painted ON the dark ear slab, behind the ear's leading edge — anatomically impossible; the eye must sit forward of the ear on the cheek. mustRead 'trunk reaching the ground' FAILS: the trunk terminates around knee height, well clear of the feet. The trunk's ring texture is a stack of hard-edged floating grey dashes that sit on top of the tube rather than wrapping it. Legs are slender tapering columns — deer legs, not the pillar legs an elephant needs. The tail is nearly as thick as the trunk and reads as a second trunk on the wrong end. A hard-edged pale wedge sits on the rump. Tusks are acceptable — white, forward and downward, reasonably straight.
rows.fix: Redraw the ear as a soft-edged rounded oval about 60% of its current area, with a feathered lower/rear margin, and move the eye forward onto the cheek clear of it. Extend the trunk so its tip touches or curls at ground level. Curve the trunk rings so they follow the tube's cross-section instead of sitting as straight bars. Thicken all four legs into columns and slim the tail to a thin rope with a terminal tuft.

rows.readsAs: An orange long-legged dog or a small pony with a plume on its back
rows.defect: Head is the Fisher's and the Fishing Cat's skull again — same wedge, same eye, same mouth line, same nose oval; only the ears differ (upright triangles here, which is the one correct fox trait). HARD SEAM: a straight diagonal boundary where the pale cream chest meets the orange neck, plus a straight hard edge across the front of the chest. mustRead 'huge bushy white-tipped tail nearly body-length' FAILS on size and form — the tail is roughly a third of body length, held up as a stiff plume, and it is the SAME shared primitive as the Fisher's (a feather/frond with straight radiating bristles) with a glowing white BEAD at the tip rather than a white-furred brush end. mustRead 'low slender body on black stockings' FAILS: the body is high off the ground on long straight legs, and the legs are pale orange for their whole length with only a small dark hoof-like foot — no black stockings. Coat is flat horizontal banding that reads as printed stripes on a flat shape; it does not wrap the ribcage or darken under the belly.
