rows.fix: Lower the body: shorten the legs by about a third and deepen/lengthen the torso. Rebuild the tail at 80-100% body length as a thick shaded cylinder of fur that sweeps out and down, with a genuinely white furred terminal third instead of a glowing bead. Run true black up all four legs from foot to elbow/hock. Feather the neck-to-chest colour change. Give the skull a distinct fox profile — a narrower, straighter muzzle and a wider triangular cheek — so it cannot be swapped with the Fisher's.

rows.readsAs: A pale bovine with a glowing horseshoe or an energy hoop clamped over its face
rows.defect: The horns render as a near-CLOSED GLOWING WHITE RING that curls over the front of the face, plus a second white crescent over the muzzle. It reads as a hoop, a magnet or a nose ring — not upcurving bovine horns — and it is the only element in the batch with a bloom halo, so it looks like an attached energy device. It fully OCCLUDES THE EYE: no eye reads at all. Blocker. mustRead 'pale grey forehead patch between upcurving horns' FAILS — there is no distinguishable forehead patch, and the horns are not upcurving. HARD SEAM: a ruler-straight diagonal line runs from the top of the rump down through the haunch separating the dark brown rump patch from the pale body, and a razor-straight white highlight streaks the spine. The head shape itself, stripped of the ring, is the same generic wedge muzzle as the Fisher/Fox family with two hard-edged brown teardrop ears pasted on the crown. Shoulder ridge does read, modestly. White stockings do read against the darker upper body. Coat is horizontal contour lines that curve with the form — the best coat in the batch, but it still reads as topographic contours or wood grain rather than short bovine hair.
rows.fix: Rebuild the horns as two separate thick tapering cones that sweep out sideways and then UP, terminating clear of the face — they must never cross the eye line, and remove the glow/bloom entirely so they read as horn keratin. Expose the eye. Add a distinct pale grey boss between the horn bases. Feather the rump-patch boundary and the spine highlight so neither is a straight line. Widen and square the muzzle into a bovine box so the head cannot pass for the Fisher's.

rows.readsAs: A cream-coloured baby giraffe or a plucked alpaca-shaped balloon animal; the long neck and tiny head read as giraffe/ostrich long before camelid.
rows.defect: HEAD: identical template to Lynx and Maned Wolf — same tapering wedge muzzle, same hard-scored straight mouth line running back into the cheek, same single dark nose tick, same oversized white cartoon eyeball set high beside the ear base. The only per-species variable is ear size/hue. Swap this head onto the Lynx and nobody would notice. The 'long banana-curved ears' do not read: they are two short heart/leaf shapes about as tall as the skull is deep, i.e. deer ears. LEGS: only TWO legs are drawn — the far pair is entirely absent on a quadruped. TORSO: the dorsal line is a perfectly straight ruled horizontal edge capped with a thin hard rim highlight; the 'shoulder and haunch solid' renders as two grey radial-gradient discs hanging off the ventral line with visibly detached edges — they read as an udder, not as bone and muscle inside the body. SEAMS: hard diagonal crease at the shoulder where the neck column meets the torso, and a hard notch step in the silhouette at the back of the jaw. COAT: flat horizontal corduroy banding stamped straight across the barrel, ignoring its curvature — floating, not lying on the form. TAIL: a flat mid-brown circle pasted on the rump with a hard unshaded edge and no taper (the same disc appears on the Lynx). Aspect measures 0.84 against a spec of 1.1.
rows.fix: Draw the far leg pair at reduced value behind the body. Kill the two ventral gradient discs and instead build the shoulder and haunch as bulges in the torso OUTLINE with the shading following that silhouette. Break the ruled dorsal line into a withers-dip-croup curve. Replace the tail disc with a short tapered tassel that starts inside the rump mass. Give the llama its own skull: blunt split-lipped muzzle with a rounded chin, no scored mouth line, small dark eye set low and far forward on the side of the face, and true banana ears — narrow, at least 1.5x skull depth, curving inward at the tips. Warp the coat bands along the barrel's cross-section instead of stamping them horizontally.

rows.readsAs: A spotted fawn or a young giraffe. There is nothing feline in this picture at all — it stands on hooves with an upright neck.
rows.defect: This is the Llama recoloured. Same skull, same heart-leaf ear pair, same wedge muzzle with the same scored mouth line and nose tick, same white cartoon eye in the same socket, same ruled dorsal line, same two hanging gradient sacs, same flat brown disc for a tail. ALL THREE mustReads fail: no black ear tufts (the ears are broad leaves with zero tuft); no flared facial ruff (the cheek line is bare); no snowshoe paws — the feet are chopped cylinders with dark oval caps that read unambiguously as HOOVES, and the hind legs are the same length as the fore. Aspect measures 1.10 against a spec of 1.85, so the long low cat is rendered as a short tall ungulate. SEAMS: hard vertical step in the silhouette at the nape and a hard diagonal where the neck meets the shoulder. COAT: the black spots are hard-edged blobs on a top layer — they do not dim in the belly shadow, they do not compress toward the silhouette edge, and they spill across the boundary onto the haunch disc unchanged. Pure decal.
rows.fix: This needs a cat body, not a recolour of the camelid. Drop the neck to horizontal, shorten it, lengthen the body to a 1.85 aspect, raise the hind leg over the fore so the rump sits higher than the shoulder. Replace the hoof caps with broad splayed paws wider than the leg is thick. Add real black tufts: two hard spikes rising off the ear tips, at least half the ear's height, in near-black. Add the ruff as a fringe of downward hair silhouetted off the cheek line so it breaks the jaw outline. Rebuild the skull short and round — flat forehead, blunt short muzzle, forward-facing eye. Project the spots through the body's shading so they darken under the belly and foreshorten near the edges.

rows.readsAs: An orange foal or spring lamb with rabbit ears and a bottle brush stuck to its rear.
rows.defect: HEAD: the third instance of the same skull — identical wedge muzzle, identical scored mouth line, identical nose tick, identical white cartoon eye. Only the ear scale changed, and ear scale is a parameter on the shared template, not a canid skull. There is no canid stop at the brow, no black nose pad, no dark facial mask. mustReads: the very large erect ears DO read (the one thing that lands). Black stockings DO NOT — the legs are plain uniform orange with only a small dark cap at the very tip of the foot; a stocking must run up the cannon to the knee. The dark mane DOES NOT read — there is a slightly browner saddle on the mid-back and a faint darker patch behind the ears, but no erectile black crest along the neck and shoulders. LEGS: only TWO legs drawn. Leg length reads roughly right but the legs are featureless straight tubes with no hock, no pastern, no visible paw. TORSO: same two ventral gradient sacs, same ruled dorsal line. COAT: the pale tan patches on the rump and shoulder are hard-edged wedges clipped flat by the silhouette — flat polygons floating on top, not fur following a surface. TAIL: a comb of straight bristle strokes with a white bead at the tip, joined to the rump at a hard elliptical seam; it reads as a paintbrush, not hair. SEAMS: hard outline where each ear meets the skull, hard crease at the neck/shoulder.
rows.fix: Paint the black stockings as a value ramp from the foot up past the knee on all four legs — they are 40% of this animal's identity. Build the mane as a raised crest of separated dark hair strokes running the nape to the shoulder blade, silhouetted ABOVE the neck outline so it breaks the profile. Draw the far leg pair. Replace the hard tan patch wedges with soft-edged colour that darkens where the body turns away. Rebuild the tail from the rump outward as tapering strands with the base buried under the hip fur, no hard join, no white bead unless it fades in. Give the head a canid profile: domed brow with a defined stop, narrow snout, black nose pad, dark eye rim.

rows.readsAs: A short tan dog, or a very smooth otter. Nothing about it says rodent.
rows.defect: Head is the mustelid template shared verbatim with Marten, Mink and Meerkat: the same brown dome cap, the same small round ear disc placed high on the crown, the same short pointed muzzle with the same scored mouth line and dark nose tick, the same small ringed eye. Four heads, one skull. All three mustReads fail: NO large orange incisors — the mouth is a scored line with no teeth of any kind, and the incisors are this animal's single identifying feature; NO scaly rope-like tail — the tail is a smooth featureless tapering tube with no scale texture and no ring pattern; NO webbing on the hind feet — the feet are chopped cylinders with plain dark oval caps identical to the Marten's. The 'blunt rounded head' also fails: the muzzle comes to a point. SEAMS: a hard straight diagonal where the dark head/neck colour meets the pale torso, a hard vertical notch in the silhouette at the nape, and a hard elliptical join where the tail meets the hip. The eye ring physically overlaps and touches the ear disc, which reads as a placement bug. TORSO: ruled straight dorsal line, hard-edged flank decal bounded by straight diagonals, two detached radial-gradient discs for shoulder and haunch. COAT: flat horizontal corduroy banding across the whole barrel ignoring its curvature. Aspect 1.95 against a spec of 2.4.
rows.fix: Put the incisors in — two bright orange chisel teeth protruding below the upper lip, visible in silhouette, sized so they read at thumbnail. Blunt the muzzle: cut the taper and square the front of the face. Re-texture the tail with visible ring scaling and thicken its base so it emerges from inside the hip mass instead of butting against it. Widen and flare the hind foot with visible webbing between splayed toes. Feather the head-to-torso colour transition across at least 10px instead of a hard diagonal. Move the eye clear of the ear.

rows.readsAs: A tan dachshund with a bottle brush for a tail. Not a mustelid — the body is a rigid slab, not a supple tube.
rows.defect: Head is the same skull as Marsh Rodent, Mink and Meerkat, differing only in hue. mustReads: the pale orange throat bib is ABSENT — the throat is the same brown as the head with no bib of any kind. 'Large rounded ears' FAILS — the ear is a tiny round nub roughly one-sixth of the skull's height, not large. 'Foxy face' FAILS — the face is a snub dome with a stubby muzzle and no vulpine wedge. The bushy full-length tail is present in intent only: it is a comb of straight bristle strokes with a white bead at the tip, attached at a hard elliptical seam at the rump, and it reads as a paintbrush rather than fur. TORSO: the dorsal line is a perfectly straight machined horizontal edge from tail base to shoulder, capped with a thin pale rim — a mammal's back is never a ruled line, and this reads as a plank. The flank 'coat' is a flat trapezoid decal with straight diagonal sides at the shoulder and hip; it floats completely free of the body's volume. Horizontal corduroy banding stamped over the whole torso. Two detached radial-gradient smudges for shoulder and haunch. FEET: all four are chopped tubes with flat oval caps — no toes, no pads, no paw. SEAMS: hard diagonal at the neck/torso colour break, hard vertical notch at the nape, hard join at the tail base. IDENTICAL TO MINK in every construction detail. Aspect 2.29 against a spec of 3.
rows.fix: Add the bib as a distinct pale orange field filling the throat and upper chest, with a soft lower boundary. Triple the ear size and set it as a rounded cup with a visible inner hollow. Lengthen and narrow the muzzle into a foxy wedge with a defined brow stop. Curve the dorsal line into an arched mustelid back — the arch is the whole read of the family. Delete the trapezoid flank decal and replace it with countershading that darkens continuously toward the belly. Bury the tail base under a fringe of rump fur so there is no visible join, and drop the white tip bead. Build actual paws with three or four visible toes. Then differentiate this from the Mink by more than hue — see the Mink entry.

rows.readsAs: A pale hairless lamb or a small goat standing broadside. Nobody would guess meerkat.
rows.defect: POSTURE IS COMPLETELY WRONG — the single most important mustRead. It is standing on all fours in profile, not bolt upright on hind legs and tail. Measured aspect is 1.09, i.e. WIDER than tall, against a spec of 0.5; the render is off by more than a factor of two in exactly the dimension that defines the species. The other two mustReads also fail: NO dark rings around the eyes (there is a brown ear disc that happens to abut the eye and reads as a bruise, not a mask); the tail has NO black tip — it is a plain uniform tan hook. HEAD: the fourth copy of the mustelid skull template, unchanged from Marsh Rodent, Marten and Mink. The ear is also wrong per the row's own note: it sits high on the crown rather than small and low on the side. LEGS: only TWO legs drawn. TORSO: two hanging radial-gradient sacs on the ventral line with detached edges, ruled straight dorsal line, corduroy banding across the barrel, hard-edged pale patches at the shoulder and hip. SEAMS: hard step in the silhouette where the tail meets the rump, hard crease at the neck/shoulder.
rows.fix: Re-pose entirely: rotate the body to vertical, plant the hind feet and prop the tail as a third point of contact, tuck the forelimbs against the chest, and let the head sit on top of a straight upright torso. Target a 0.5 aspect. Paint the eye mask as a solid dark ring extending past the eye toward the ear. Black the last third of the tail. Move the ears down onto the sides of the skull and shrink them. Give the skull its own shape — short pointed face with a broad forehead — instead of the shared mustelid dome. Draw all four limbs.

rows.readsAs: The Marten again with the saturation pulled down. On its own, a low tan dog with a bottle brush tail.
rows.defect: This is a palette swap of the Marten and it is the clearest failure in the batch — same ruled straight dorsal line, same flat trapezoid flank decal with the same straight diagonal boundaries, same two detached shoulder/haunch gradient smudges, same corduroy banding, same brush tail with the same white bead at the tip and the same hard elliptical join at the rump, same chopped-tube feet with oval caps, same head down to the eye ring position. mustReads: 'glossy dark chocolate fur' FAILS on both counts — the coat is mid-brown over a large pale tan flank, several values too light, and there is no specular gloss anywhere on the body. 'White chin patch' is ABSENT — the chin is plain brown. 'Elongate low body' is the one that lands, though the measured aspect is 2.62 against a spec of 3.6, so it is not as long or as low as it should be. HEAD: the same mustelid template as Marsh Rodent, Marten and Meerkat; swappable with any of them. SEAMS: hard diagonal at the neck/torso colour break, hard vertical notch at the nape, hard join at the tail base.
rows.fix: Drop the whole coat to a dark chocolate value and remove the pale flank decal entirely — a mink is near-uniform dark, and that uniformity is what separates it from the marten. Add a specular run along the top of the back and the top of the haunch to read as wet gloss. Paint a small clean white patch on the chin and lower lip only. Lengthen the body toward a 3.6 aspect and lower the belly closer to the ground. Slim the tail into a tapered cylinder rather than a bristle brush, and lose the white tip bead. Give the skull a flatter, narrower profile than the marten's so the two are distinguishable head-only.

rows.readsAs: A cream-and-tan sheep wearing a horseshoe-shaped sticker on its cheek, with straw glued around its outline
rows.defect: HORNS FAIL as a mustRead: they are not a pair of horns growing from the skull but a single flat cream ANNULUS (a closed ring) laid over the face — it crosses in front of the muzzle and clips the eye socket, reading as a decal, not as short thick horns curving back and down. MANE FAILS: instead of a hanging mane over neck and shoulders there is a halo of straight straw spikes radiating outward from the silhouette edge only (top of spine, brisket, belly, rump) — they float off the body against the background and none of them lie over the neck. SEAM: a 1px pale hairline runs the entire topline from withers to rump, a hard graphic line where the back cap meets the barrel. OFF-BODY ARTIFACT: a dark brown disc with bristles is pasted on the rump reading as a burn hole. COAT FLOATS: the fur is a flat crosshatch of straight tan strokes that ignore the barrel's curvature, and two soft airbrush ovals sit on the shoulder and haunch with the strokes running straight under them — shading applied over the coat, not the coat shaded by form. HEAD is the same mesh as the Takin: identical dome, identical high dark eye, identical ring horn.
rows.fix: Replace the annulus horn with two tapered, separately-drawn horn solids rooted behind the eye and sweeping back-and-down clear of the muzzle, shaded to the light. Redraw the mane as an overlapping fur mass drawn INSIDE the neck/shoulder silhouette that widens the neck, not as radial spikes on the outline. Delete the topline hairline (blend the back cap into the barrel). Replace the rump disc with a short tail solid rooted in the haunch. Curve the fur strokes to follow the barrel's cross-section so the shading is the form, not an overlay. Give the tahr its own skull: shorter, blunter, deeper jaw than the Takin's.

rows.readsAs: A pale cream sheep with a long straight face and straw stuck around it — no horns visible at all at thumbnail size
rows.defect: HORNS FAIL as a mustRead. There IS a ring on the face, but it is the identical flat annulus used on the Tahr, tinted the same beige as the coat, so it disappears against the cheek — at full size it reads as a smudge and at thumbnail it reads as no horns at all. Nothing sweeps outward then back. HUMPED SHOULDERS FAIL: the topline is essentially flat, the withers no taller than the rump; nothing about this silhouette is bison-like or stockier than a goat — it is dimensionally the Tahr's body with a different tint. Legs are thin, not short and thick. The Roman-nosed arched muzzle is the one mustRead that does read. SAME SEAM as the Tahr: a pale hairline along the whole topline. SAME ARTIFACT: dark bristled disc pasted on the rump. Coat is the same flat straight-stroke crosshatch with airbrush ovals floating over it, plus the same outline-only straw halo.
rows.fix: Draw the horns as two solid boss-rooted horns in a contrasting dark keratin tone, thick at the base on top of the skull, out to the side then hooking back — they must be legible in silhouette. Raise and mass the withers into a real hump so the back slopes down to the rump, and thicken/shorten all four legs. Differentiate the barrel from the Tahr's outright (deeper chest, heavier belly). Remove the topline hairline and the rump disc.

rows.readsAs: A grey lamb or a grey shorthaired dog with a hole burned in its hip
rows.defect: PROBOSCIS FAILS as a mustRead: the muzzle is a plain tapering snout with a small downward hook and a nostril crease at the tip — there is no short mobile trunk, no overhang past the lower lip, nothing that reads as prehensile. ROUNDED HIGH RUMP WITH SLOPING BACK FAILS and is in fact inverted: the topline is dead flat and the rump sits LOWER than the shoulder. STUBBY TAIL FAILS: in its place is a near-black flat CIRCLE pasted onto the hip — it reads as a hole in the animal, not a nub. SEAMS: a hard vertical step and notch is cut into the lower rear of the skull where the head block meets the body; the dark head/neck grey ends against the pale body along a hard diagonal collar edge; a hard-edged darker wedge cuts across the rear quarter; the same pale hairline runs the topline. The ear is a flat dark ellipse stamped on the skull with no base. HEAD is not tapir-specific at all — it is the identical dome-skull + ear-disc + ring-eye + hooked muzzle used on the Tasmanian Devil, the Tiger and the Warthog, only recoloured.
rows.fix: Build the proboscis as an actual mass: a thickened, drooping upper lip that overhangs the mouth and hangs below the jawline, with the nostrils on its underside. Raise the pelvis above the withers and round the croup so the back slopes forward. Replace the black hip circle with a small tapered tail rooted in the rump. Dissolve the head/neck colour boundary into a gradient and remove the notch so the skull grows out of the neck. Give the tapir skull a straight heavy forehead and a very small eye set far back — nothing like the devil's.

rows.readsAs: A small light-grey dog or lamb with a dark head and a thin curling tail
rows.defect: THREE of three mustReads fail. OVERSIZED BLOCKY HEAD AND GAPING JAWS: the head is small relative to the body (smaller in proportion than the Tapir's in the same batch), egg-shaped, not blocky, and the jaws are shut — a single thin mouth line, no gape, no teeth. BLACK FUR WITH A WHITE CHEST BAND: the body is pale silver-grey over its whole length; only the head and neck are dark. There is no white chest band because there is no dark field for it to sit on — the value scheme is exactly inverted from the animal. The tapering tail is the one thing that reads. SEAM: hard step-notch at the rear of the skull and a hard tonal edge where the dark neck meets the pale shoulder — the head is stuck on. HEAD IS A DIRECT COPY of the Tapir's: same dome, same big flat ear disc, same white ring eye, same hooked tapering muzzle at the same angle. Swap the two heads and nobody could tell.
rows.fix: Make the body black and the head genuinely oversized (roughly a quarter of body length), with a broad flat cranium, wide zygomatic arches and a short deep jaw. Open the jaws and show the canines — the gape IS the species. Put a single white crescent across the chest and optionally the rump against black fur. Rebuild the skull from scratch so it cannot be confused with the Tapir's; drop the ear disc for small round marsupial ears with pink inner colour.

rows.readsAs: A striped hyena or a thylacine — a striped hoofed-looking animal with a long plain tail; not a big cat
rows.defect: WHITE CHEEK RUFF AND WHITE EYEBROW SPOTS FAIL — entirely absent; the face is flat orange with black bars, and one of those bars runs horizontally straight through the eye. LONG RINGED TAIL FAILS: the tail is plain unringed orange, and its root is a hard-edged rectangular slab pasted onto the rump — a visible seam. The stripes only half-satisfy: on the flank they DO run vertically, but they are all bunched into a single fan radiating from one point over the shoulder, the entire hindquarter and rump are bare orange, none continue onto the legs, and on the head they are HORIZONTAL bars. Worst, a long dead-straight black bar runs the whole length of the flank at mid-height — that is a graphic line, not fur, and it crosses the fanned stripes at a hard angle. COAT FLOATS: the stripe fan sits on a flat plane and does not wrap the barrel's curvature. SEAM at the neck: hard step-notch behind the skull plus a hard vertical boundary where a paler orange collar meets the striped body. HEAD IS NOT A CAT — it is the same dome-skull, ear-disc, ring-eye and long hooked muzzle as the Tapir, Devil and Warthog, recoloured orange and painted with stripes.
rows.fix: Delete the straight horizontal flank bar. Distribute the stripes as separate vertical bands wrapping the whole barrel, curving with the body's cross-section, continuing over the rump, down the legs and around the tail as rings ending in a black tip. Build a cat skull: short broad muzzle, wide cheek mass, small rounded ears set wide on a domed cranium, forward-set eyes with the pale eyebrow spots above them and a white ruff flaring off the cheeks. Root the tail in the rump as a continuous taper instead of a slab.

rows.readsAs: A pink dachshund with two ivory pegs hanging off its chin
rows.defect: SEAM — the clearest one in the batch: the head is a separate box stuck onto the body. There is a hard rectangular STEP where the head's top plane meets the body's top plane at a different height, a straight vertical cut edge beneath it, and a notch chopped out of the lower rear of the skull. A second hard vertical line crosses the barrel near the front of the ribcage. DENSE BRISTLE MOUSTACHE FAILS: the muzzle is smooth pink with a thin brown mouth line and a small brown curve — not one bristle, and the moustache is the species' signature. VAST WRINKLED BLUBBERY BODY FAILS: the body is a slim even-diameter sausage no deeper than the Tapir's, with only faint horizontal contour bands and no fold or roll anywhere. The tusks read, and the paddle feet with digit marks are credibly flipper-like, but the animal stands on four short legs like a terrestrial quadruped rather than sprawling on the fore-flippers. Two dark discs sit on the forehead above the eye reading as misplaced nostrils. The head skull IS distinctive — but only because of the boxy seam artifact and the pasted-on tusks; the eye and mouth stamps are the batch's shared ones.
rows.fix: Merge the head into the neck — no step in the topline, no vertical cut, one continuous mass from brow to shoulder. Add the moustache as a dense bristle pad filling the whole squared muzzle, tusks emerging from behind and below it. Balloon the body: massive chest and neck tapering to the hips, with two or three heavy skin folds at the neck and shoulder and a wrinkled surface. Lower the whole animal so the belly sits near the ground and the fore-flippers prop it up. Move the two dark discs off the forehead — the nostrils belong at the top of the muzzle.

rows.readsAs: A grey-brown dog or small deer with two straight horns growing off the bridge of its nose
rows.defect: TUSKS FAIL in placement and shape: two straight cream spikes rise off the TOP of the snout, side by side like a rhino's twin horns, and they do not curve — a warthog's tusks come out of the sides of the mouth and sweep up and outward. As drawn they read as horns on a deer. FACIAL WARTS FAIL — none. ERECT BRISTLY MANE FAILS — the neck and spine are completely smooth; what runs along the topline instead is the batch's pale 1px hairline SEAM where the back cap meets the barrel. TAIL FAILS on carriage: it hangs down and back with a dark tuft rather than being carried straight up (the tuft itself reads). The head is not flat-fronted or wedge-like and the body is not notably leggy. The pink nose disc at the muzzle tip is the only pig cue in the picture. HEAD is the shared batch skull again — same dome, same big ear/eye-patch disc, same ring eye, same long hooked muzzle as the Tapir, Devil and Tiger.
rows.fix: Re-root the tusks at the corners of the mouth, below and behind the nose, and curve them up and out in a crescent; add the smaller lower pair. Add the two paired fleshy wart lobes on the cheek and below the eye. Add the mane as a stiff erect crest of bristles standing UP off the neck and spine and breaking the silhouette — that also lets you delete the hairline seam it should be covering. Flip the tail to vertical with the tuft at the top. Flatten and square the front of the skull into a wedge so it stops sharing a profile with the Tapir.

rows.readsAs: A cream-white cartoon okapi or llama with two airbrushed palm-frond sunbursts sprayed on its ribs. Only the flank pattern gestures at 'zebra'; from the neck up and the knees down a stranger would not say zebra.
rows.defect:
MUSTREAD 1 FAILED (blocker) — stripes do not continue onto the legs or belly. All four legs are bare white tubes from shoulder/thigh to hoof, and the entire lower barrel is unmarked. Worse, what is on the flanks are not stripes: they are two radial starbursts of tapered feathery spikes converging on a point over the shoulder and a point over the haunch, clipped off at a curved boundary above the belly. It reads as spray-paint / palm fronds, not bold bands wrapping a barrel.
MUSTREAD 2 FAILED (blocker) — there is no mane at all. The dorsal line of the neck is a bare cream edge from poll to withers; not an erect brush, not even a flowing one. Nothing is there.
MUSTREAD 3 PARTIAL (major) — the tail silhouette is right (bare tube + terminal tuft) but the tuft is a flat mid-grey hard-edged ellipse stuck on the tube end like a lollipop paddle. Wrong value (should be black), no hair, and a visible hard seam at the join. The tube itself is nearly leg-thick and the same cream as the coat, so 'bare' does not read.
HEAD (blocker) — the head is 100% blank white: no facial striping, no dark muzzle, no cheek marking. The two ears are fused into a single dark heart-shaped mass sitting on top of the skull, and the eye is placed INSIDE the right lobe of that heart, at the crown of the skull, instead of on the cheek below and forward of the ears. The eye itself is a googly white disc with a dark ring — cartoon, not an ungulate's dark almond. The muzzle is a long featureless faceted wedge with a hard polygonal crease running its whole length along the lower jaw. Delete the heart-ears and this exact skull could be swapped onto a llama, guanaco, okapi or deer and nobody would notice — it carries zero equid mass (no jowl, no cheekbone, no wide nasal bridge, no rounded dark-tipped ears).
SEAMS (blocker) — a hard angular step/notch at the poll where the back of the skull meets the top of the neck, reading as a stuck-on head; a straight facet line along the back from withers to croup; a sharp V crease under the belly where the shoulder sphere and the haunch sphere meet, exposing the two-ball torso construction; a hard edge at the tail-tuft join. Leg-to-body junctions are the one clean part — those blend properly.
COAT — floating, not lying on the body. Form shading exists (undersides darken), but the pattern ignores it: the sprays radiate from two arbitrary point sources rather than following the ribcage, terminate at a clipped patch boundary, and stop dead at the limb roots, so the markings read as decals applied to two spheres.
ANATOMY — the hind leg is the same straight tube as the foreleg, with no hock angle; hooves are tiny two-block caps that read as socks.
rows.fix:
1) Replace the two radial spray fans with true banding: vertical bands generated along the body's longitudinal axis, wrapping perpendicular to the spine, continuing over the shoulder and haunch, down the full length of all four legs to the hoof, and meeting under the belly (thin/converge there rather than stopping at a patch edge). Kill the point-source emitter entirely — nothing about a zebra radiates.
2) Add the erect brush mane as a hard-edged crest standing off the dorsal neck line from poll to withers, banded black/white in register with the neck stripes, and let it break the silhouette.
3) Stripe the head: banded muzzle bridge and cheek, and a solid black/dark-grey muzzle tip and nostril patch. This alone removes most of the 'generic wedge' problem.
4) Split the ears into two separate rounded upright ovals set well back on the skull with dark inner cups and dark tips, and move the eye down and forward to the cheek, roughly a third back from the muzzle tip and below the ear line. It must not overlap the ear geometry.
5) Rebuild the equid skull: deepen the jowl/cheek mass, widen the nasal bridge, and remove the straight facet crease along the lower jaw so the muzzle is a rounded taper, not a folded plane.
6) Blend the poll: no angular step where the skull meets the neck — carry the neck volume up into the base of the skull.
7) Smooth the back facet line and the belly V so the shoulder and haunch read as one barrel, not two spheres.
8) Recolour the tail tuft to near-black, give it hair-strand edges instead of an ellipse, taper it into the tail tube (no hard join), and thin the bare upper tail so it reads as skin, not a fifth limb.
9) Give the hind limb a hock angle and enlarge the hooves into a single solid dark cup per foot.

rows.readsAs: A long-legged orange dog — closer to a pony-proportioned mutt than a fox. A stranger would say 'orange dog with a feather-duster tail'.
rows.defect: MISSING mustRead: black stockings. The legs are plain orange for their whole length with only a ~10px dark cap on the toe stub — no stocking reads at all. The brush tail is present with a white tip, but it is built as a fan of separate straw-like bristle spikes with an orange lobe laid over them; it reads as a broom/wheat sheaf, not a volume of fur, and the bristles poke out past the silhouette. Feet are flat-cut dark cylinder stubs (hoof/boot), not paws. SEAMS: a hard diagonal facet crease where the tail lobe meets the rump; the back is a dead-straight plank with a crisp aliased rim stroke; a notch/step at the occiput where the head blob sits on the neck. Coat: the flank striations do follow the barrel, but shoulder and haunch are soft airbrushed grey ovals floating on the surface rather than muscle under fur. Twins with Red Panda (identical torso, limbs, ear shape and head kit) and with Sand Cat (identical torso and limb set).
rows.fix: Run the dark leg colour from the elbow/hock down to the toe so the stocking reads at silhouette scale, not a toe cap. Rebuild the tail as one tapered fur mass with the bristle detail INSIDE the silhouette and the white tip as the terminal third, not a ball. Give the canid family a paw terminal (toes/pad) instead of the cut cylinder. Blend the tail root into the rump instead of a facet edge, and break the straight back line with a scapula rise and a lumbar dip. Differentiate the head from Red Panda's: longer, thinner snout, sharper triangular ears with black backs, white cheek/throat.

rows.readsAs: A rust-coloured dog or dingo with a ringed tail. Nothing says red panda; it also reads at dog/coyote size, not raccoon size.
rows.defect: TWO missing mustReads. (1) No white face mask and no rust tear-stripes — the face is a flat unbroken rust field, the single most identifying feature of the animal is absent. (2) Legs and belly are NOT jet-black; they are the same rust as the torso with tiny dark toe caps, so the two-tone body that defines the species is gone. The ringed tail IS there and is the best thing in the picture (rust with dark bands) — the reference row is wrong to ask for 'pale rings'; dark-on-rust is correct, keep it. SEAM: a hard step where the neck tube crosses the shoulder panel — you can trace the neck cylinder's outline over the torso. Head is the Red Fox head with a shorter snout: same ovoid cranium, same rod-and-ball nose, same dark leaf ears, same white-ring eye decal.
rows.fix: Paint the white mask (white brows, cheeks, muzzle) with rust tear-stripes running from the inner eye to the jaw — this alone rescues the species. Take the legs and the whole underside to near-black. Shorten the legs and deepen the chest so it reads raccoon-sized. Give it round white-fringed ears set wide on a broad low skull instead of the fox's tall dark leaf ears.

rows.readsAs: A generic cream deer or young elk. It reads deer, but not specifically reindeer.
rows.defect: THREE missing mustReads. (1) No brow shovel — the antlers are symmetric back-swept branched beams with no forward palm over the face, which is the one antler shape that distinguishes reindeer from every other deer. (2) No thick pale neck mane — the throat is a slightly lighter cream but there is no fringe, no silhouette bulge, no hair edge. (3) Hooves are small dark two-tone stubs, narrow and pointed, not the broad splayed crescents called for. SEAM/STUCK-ON PART: the tail is a flat hard-edged dark brown disc pasted on the rump — a perfect circle with an aliased boundary, reads as a hole or a sticker. Also a straight bright rim stroke along the back. Coat does follow the volume here (contour striations wrap the barrel and haunch correctly) — the torso solid is working. Head is the same wedge muzzle, same dark eye-blob and same mouth line as Saiga; only the headgear differs.
rows.fix: Rebuild the antler as a reindeer antler: main beams sweeping back then up, with a flattened brow tine palmated FORWARD over the nose. Add a real mane — a pale hair mass hanging below the throat that changes the neck silhouette. Widen and split the hoof into two splayed toes. Replace the disc tail with a short tapered tail growing out of the rump contour. Differentiate the skull from Saiga's: shorter, blockier muzzle with a broad rhinarium and a visible ear pair.

rows.readsAs: A rhinoceros — the only picture in the batch a stranger would name correctly and immediately.
rows.defect: One mustRead only partly delivered: 'thick plated hide with deep folds' is not there. The hide is smooth grey with faint contour striping; the lighter grey areas over the shoulder and rump are flat hard-edged panels, i.e. stickers with a visible boundary, not folds with a shadowed crease. Horn placement is correct (two pale horns rising off the nose, not the forehead), the body is correctly low and barrel-shaped, and the three-toed feet with pale nails read well. SEAMS: the tail is a flat grey slab with a square corner attached to the rump — it reads like a cut-out trunk stuck on the back end; there is a facet edge running vertically across the muzzle; a hard vertical line at the top of the front leg. The dark round blotch at the eye is oversized and ambiguous (it reads as a second eye or a bruise). Coat/hide otherwise lies ON the form correctly — the contour lines genuinely wrap the barrel and haunch domes; this is the best surface in the batch.
rows.fix: Convert the flat shoulder/rump panels into real plates: a dark crease line with a lit lip above it and a shadow below, following the body contour. Regrow the tail from the rump as a thin tapering rope with a tuft. Kill the facet line across the muzzle and soften the leg-to-belly junction. Shrink the eye blotch to a small deep-set eye placed far back on the side of the skull as the note requires.

rows.readsAs: A long low weasel or ferret on hollow pipe legs. The body length reads mustelid, but the legs look unfinished.
rows.defect: TWO missing mustReads plus a rendering defect. (1) The tail is a thin constant-width rope curving off the rump — no muscular base, no taper; the reference asks for a thick muscular tail tapering to a point and this is the opposite. (2) No webbed feet: every leg terminates in an OPEN-ENDED CYLINDER — you can see the darker elliptical interior of the tube, like cut pipe. There is no foot at all on any of the four limbs. (3) The face is blunt with a small round ear, which is right, but there are no whiskers. SEAMS: a hard brown cap block where the tail meets the rump; an abrupt colour boundary at the throat where the dark brown head meets the pale tan neck with no transition. Head is the shared kit again — same ovoid cranium, same rod-and-ball nose, same white-ring eye — with a small round ear substituted for the fox's leaf ear.
rows.fix: Close the leg tubes and give the family a webbed foot terminal: a splayed flat pad with visible toe webbing, drawn wider than the leg. Rebuild the tail thick at the base (as wide as the hindquarter) tapering to a point over its length. Feather the head/neck colour change into a gradient. Add whiskers and a broad flat rhinarium so the face reads otter rather than generic small carnivore.

rows.readsAs: A pale goat or antelope with straight ringed horns — an oryx-lite. The one feature everyone knows the saiga for is absent.
rows.defect: MISSING mustRead: the bulbous drooping trunk-like nose. The muzzle is a plain tapered wedge ending in a rounded tip — it is the SAME muzzle geometry as the Reindeer in this batch, down to the mouth line and the dark blob at the eye. Without the proboscis this is not a saiga. The ringed horns are good: straight, rising vertically, with clear ring banding, and pale enough to read translucent. Slim legs are correct. SEAMS: a hard-edged lighter panel over the shoulder with a straight boundary; a straight bright rim stroke along the back; the same flat dark disc tail pasted on the rump as the Reindeer. Coat sits on the form acceptably on the barrel, but the haunch and shoulder are soft airbrushed grey ovals rather than shaded volumes.
rows.fix: Build the nose as a distinct swollen down-hanging proboscis overhanging the mouth, with downward-facing nostrils and a visible bridge hump — it must change the head silhouette, not just the shading. Once that lands the head can no longer be confused with the Reindeer's. Replace the disc tail, dissolve the hard shoulder panel edge into the coat, and relieve the straight back line.

rows.readsAs: A fennec fox, or a sandy jackrabbit-eared kit fox. Nobody would say cat.
rows.defect: TWO missing mustReads and a wrong family read. (1) The head is small and narrow with a pointed snout, and the ears are two enormous TALL UPRIGHT dark ears set high and close together — the exact opposite of the required broad flattened skull with low wide-set ears. (2) The legs are long slim cylinders ending in small two-tone hoof-like tips; the reference asks for short stocky legs with furred feet, and there is no fur on the foot and no stockiness. The banded tail is partly there — three dark blotches and a dark tip — but the bands read as blobs sitting on top of the tail rather than fur bands wrapping it. WORST SEAM IN THE BATCH: the neck is a separate lighter tube drawn over the shoulder and its outline is fully traceable as a step across the chest, with a notch cut out behind the skull; the top of the back is a ruler-straight line carrying a hard aliased bright rim stroke, so the torso reads as a plank. Body, limb set and tail geometry are the same asset as Red Panda, recoloured.
rows.fix: Rebuild the skull wide and flat-topped with the ears set LOW on the sides, short and rounded, so the head reads feline in silhouette; add the pale muzzle and cheek ruff. Shorten and thicken all four legs and give the felid family a rounded furred paw. Wrap the tail bands around the cylinder with shading. Dissolve the neck-tube outline into the shoulder mass and put a scapula rise and a lumbar dip into the back line so it stops being straight.

rows.readsAs: A shaggy pale pig, or a badly-shorn sheep, standing square on four legs. Nothing about it says otter, water, or marine mammal.
rows.defect: Every mustRead fails. (1) Posture: it is a standing quadruped, not floating belly-up; there is no rock on the chest and no water context at all. (2) Hind feet are not webbed flippers — all four legs end in the same tapered cylinder with a flat elliptical end-cap (see the foot crop: the leg is literally a tube cut off with a disc, no toes, no webbing). (3) No pale whiskers — the only hairs near the face are the same generic straw spikes used over the whole body. HEAD: it is the shared batch skull — round dome, one tiny dark ear pip at the crown, one big white-ringed cartoon eye, a tapering muzzle with a dot nose. Recolour it and it is the Sloth's head exactly; swap the two and nobody would notice. SEAMS: the dark brown head/neck mass stops dead against the pale body along a hard curved colour boundary at the shoulder; a crisp bright 1px rim stroke runs the length of the spine and reads as an outline, not a highlight; the leg tops are sliced off by a straight line where they meet the belly; a hard-edged dark disc is pasted on the rump. COAT: floating, not lying on the body — a flat burlap crosshatch runs in straight rows over the whole flank without wrapping the shoulder or haunch lobes, and hundreds of straight straw spikes project outside the silhouette in all directions like a hedgehog.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a mustelid on its back: horizontal floating body, belly up, forepaws holding a rock on the chest, head lifted at the near end. Give the hind limbs real webbed flippers (broad, flattened, splayed toes) — not the shared cylinder. Replace the shared dome skull with a short blunt otter head: broad flat muzzle, wide pale whisker pad with actual radiating whiskers, small round ears set low and far back, small dark eyes with no white sclera ring. Kill the rim stroke on the spine, blend the head colour into the neck across a gradient rather than a hard edge, and let the coat hatch curve around the shoulder/haunch masses instead of running in flat rows. Clip the fur spikes to the silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A shaggy grey mountain goat — this is the closest read in the batch, and broadly the right animal.
rows.defect: MustRead miss: 'large donkey-like ears' are absent. At head zoom there are only the two pale horns and a dark forelock mass between them — no large ear shape reads anywhere on the skull. The horns are also wrong in form: they curve up and inward in a lyre, rather than the short straight backswept spikes specified. SEAMS: a crisp bright white stroke runs the entire length of the back, terminating at the neck — a hard line, not a form highlight; the darker head/neck mass meets the pale body along an abrupt vertical boundary at the shoulder with no transition; both front legs are cut off by a straight edge where they enter the chest; a hard-edged dark disc sits on the rump. The shoulder and haunch are two flat ellipse lobes whose edges are visible and which meet in a sharp V under the belly. COAT: floating — the crosshatch runs in flat horizontal rows across the flank and does not bend over the shoulder or haunch lobes, and the mane is a fringe of straight straws sticking outside the outline rather than hair growing from the neck.
rows.fix: Add the big donkey ears — wide, low-set, projecting sideways from behind the horn bases; they are the serow's single most recognisable feature. Straighten the horns into short backswept cones. Remove the spine rim stroke. Feather the head/neck colour into the body. Let the coat hatch follow the barrel of the ribcage and curve over the shoulder and haunch so the fur is shaded by the form. Keep the cloven dark hooves — those are correct.

rows.readsAs: A spotted fawn or young deer — Bambi with oversized ears. Nobody would call this a cat.
rows.defect: The three mustReads are technically present (very long legs, large upright oval ears on a small head, short tail and boldly spotted coat) but the family reads wrong at every joint. FEET: this cat has no paws — the foot crop shows four bare cylinder ends with flat elliptical caps, identical to the Snow Leopard's and the Sea Otter's. The 'each family has its own limb and foot type' rebuild did not reach the cats. HEAD: the ears are large and correct, but the skull under them is the shared taper — a pointed dog/deer snout with a dark dot nose at the tip, a long straight mouth slit running back, and a round cartoon eye with a full white sclera ring. A cat's face is short, wide and flat-fronted with almond eyes; this is a fennec-fox muzzle. The ears are flat hard-edged shapes pasted on the crown with a visible outline. SEAMS: the neck is a faceted polygon meeting the shoulder along a hard diagonal edge; a bright rim stroke runs the spine; the front leg's top is a straight cut across the chest. COAT: partly floating — the spots stop at the shoulder and haunch lobe boundaries in several places instead of continuing across the form, and the lobe edges themselves are hard.
rows.fix: Give it cat feet: compact rounded paws with visible toes, not cylinder caps. Shorten and broaden the muzzle into a feline face — flat front, small nose pad set high, whisker pads, almond eyes without the white sclera ring. Blend the ears into the skull so they grow from it. Dissolve the neck facet and the spine rim stroke. Run the spot field continuously over the shoulder and haunch so the coat is one skin, and shade the spots by the underlying form. Tail should be short and thick, not a fat tapered curl.

rows.readsAs: A pale hippopotamus-headed pony, or a Muppet cow. The face is genuinely unreadable as any real animal.
rows.defect: The head is malformed. At zoom there is a bulbous downturned snout, a large dark brown oval sitting where the eye should be (it reads as an ear that has slid onto the face), and a big pale crescent ring overlapping the cheek that corresponds to nothing anatomical. There is no locatable eye. This is not a sheep face and not a specific face at all — it is a broken blob, so it is not head-unique in the sense of being species-specific. MustReads: 'thick woolly fleece blurring the body outline' FAILS — the silhouette is smooth and hard-edged everywhere, and the surface is a wood-grain contour hatch, not wool; 'narrow bare face' FAILS, the face is wide and bulbous; 'short drooping tail' FAILS — the only thing at the rear is a hard-edged flat brown disc pasted on the hip, which reads as a paint blot. SEAMS: a crisp bright stroke runs the top of the back and up the neck; the shoulder and haunch are two flat overlapping ellipses whose edges are plainly visible and which meet in a sharp V under the belly; all four legs are separate tapered tubes overlapping the body with a hard edge at the top.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head from scratch: narrow bare wedge face, small dark eye placed high and to the side of a long muzzle, small ears angled back — and delete the crescent artefact and the misplaced oval. Make the fleece actually fleecy: break the silhouette with a soft lumpy crenellated outline and replace the wood-grain hatch with clumped curled wool that thins to bare skin at the face and lower legs. Replace the rump disc with a real short drooping tail. Remove the spine rim stroke, and soften the shoulder/haunch lobe edges so they are volumes under the fleece rather than two pasted ellipses.

rows.readsAs: A small khaki sheep or goat standing on four legs.
rows.defect: MustReads fail. (1) 'Long hooked scythe claws' are entirely absent — the limbs end in short stubby hoof-like tips, the same tube-and-cap construction as the rest of the batch. This is the single defining feature of a sloth and it is not in the picture. (2) The face is not small, round and flat with a faint smile — it is the shared batch skull with a projecting tapered muzzle, a dot nose at the tip, two round ear pips on the crown, and one large white-ringed cartoon eye. Sloths have no visible ears, a flat disc face, and tiny dark eyes in a dark mask. (3) The fur is pale khaki, not greenish, and it is not shaggy over most of the body — only a small comb of straws on the shoulder. Posture is a standing quadruped rather than suspended under a branch. HEAD: this is the Sea Otter's head in a lighter colour; the two are directly swappable. SEAMS: hard colour boundary where the darker head mass meets the pale body at the neck; visible hard-edged shoulder and haunch ellipses meeting in a V at the belly; hard-edged dark disc on the rump; leg tops cut by straight lines. COAT: floating — a flat contour hatch over the flank plus straws that project outside the silhouette.
rows.fix: Give it the claws — three long curved hooks per limb, longer than the foot, as the read-at-a-glance silhouette feature. Hang it: limbs above the body gripping a branch, body slung beneath. Replace the head with a flat round face — no muzzle projection, no ear pips, small dark eyes inside a darker facial mask, faint upturned mouth line. Make the fur long, coarse, downward-hanging and green-tinged over the whole body, following gravity, and blend the neck into the shoulder instead of butting two colours together.

rows.readsAs: A grey shaggy warthog or a scruffy donkey. It does not read as a bear of any kind.
rows.defect: MustReads fail. (1) The coat is NOT black — the body renders pale grey-beige with only the head dark, so the animal reads two-tone and washed out. (2) There is no pale U or Y chest blaze anywhere; the chest is undifferentiated. (3) 'Huge curved claws' are represented by a single tiny flat white rectangular tick projecting horizontally from each front toe — at zoom it reads as a rendering artefact or a highlight glitch, not a claw. (4) The snout is long-ish, which is right, but it is the same dark colour as the rest of the head, so the 'long PALE mobile snout' that distinguishes this bear from every other bear does not read. HEAD: the shared batch template again — dome skull, ringed cartoon eye, tapering muzzle with a dot nose; the only differentiator is that the ears are bigger and the whole thing is darker. Recolour the Sloth's head and enlarge its ear pips and you have this head. SEAMS: the dark head/neck mass stops abruptly against the pale body along a hard curved boundary at the shoulder — the most visible seam in the batch; a bright crisp stroke runs the whole spine; hard-edged shoulder and haunch ellipses; hard-edged dark disc on the rump. COAT: floating — straight straw spikes scattered over and outside the body at all angles with no direction or form logic, over a flat hatch.
rows.fix: Make the body genuinely black and shaggy so it is one dark mass, then put a clean pale U/Y blaze on the chest as the read feature. Replace the white tick marks with real claws — long, curved, ivory, clearly longer than the toes. Recolour the muzzle pale grey against the black head and give it loose protrusible lips so it reads as a termite-sucking snout rather than a generic taper. Remove the head/body colour seam and the spine stroke. Make the shag hang downward in clumps that follow the barrel and the shoulder mane, not radiate outward as straws.

rows.readsAs: A white Dalmatian-spotted pony or goat with a bottle-brush horse tail.
rows.defect: MustReads fail on all three. (1) The tail is long, but it is rendered as a stiff spiky black-and-white brush angled up and away from the rump, joined at a hard edge — it reads as a horse's tail or a chimney brush, not a thick ropy furred cat tail. (2) The coat carries small dense scattered dots, not large open rosettes — and the dots are clumped in the middle of the back and absent over most of the shoulder and haunch. (3) 'Short stout legs and big paws' FAILS twice: the legs are long and thin, and the foot crop shows the leg is a plain cylinder terminated by a flat grey elliptical cap — there is no paw at all, no toes, nothing. HEAD: not feline and not unique. A large flat grey DISC sits on top of the skull where an ear should be (it reads as a lens or a bald patch), the eye is the same white-ringed cartoon dot used across the batch, and the muzzle is a long pointed taper with a dot nose — the opposite of the short blunt muzzle and domed skull the reference calls for. It is the Serval's skull in white. SEAMS: the neck meets the shoulder along a hard straight edge with a visible notch/step on the upper side; a bright rim stroke runs the spine; the shoulder and haunch are two flat pale-grey ellipses with hard edges floating on top of the coat — the spots visibly stop at their borders instead of continuing across. COAT: floating — the lobes sit over the spot field rather than the spots being shaded by the lobes.
rows.fix: Give it paws — big, broad, snowshoe-like, with toes — and shorten and thicken the legs so the body sits low and heavy. Redraw the tail as a single thick tube of fur, as long as head-and-body, carried in a low curve, growing continuously out of the rump. Replace the dot field with large open rosettes — broken rings with a paler centre — distributed evenly and warped over the shoulder and haunch. Rebuild the head as a big cat's: domed forehead, short blunt muzzle, small rounded ears (two of them, integrated into the skull, not one grey disc), pale green almond eyes without the white sclera ring, thick cheek ruff. Remove the neck step, the spine stroke, and the hard lobe edges.

rows.readsAs: a grey shaggy sheep or musk-ox calf with a dark head — nobody would say 'bear'
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS 3/3: no pale cream spectacle rings or patches (the only light thing on the face is a 4px white eye-ring that reads as an eyeball highlight, not a marking); the coat is pale grey-tan burlap, not a shaggy BLACKISH coat; the face is not short-and-heavy — it is the same tapered wedge muzzle with a thin drawn mouth-line used on the hyenas. HEAD is the batch's stock kit: rounded skull + one hard-edged dark CIRCLE pasted flat on the side for an ear (crisp rim, no attachment) + white-ring eye + oval nose nub. Swap it with the Sun Bear head and nothing changes but hue. SEAMS: a crisp bright white rim-line runs the full length of the topline like a drawn outline; the legs are smooth untextured pale tubes that change colour at a hard boundary where they meet the dark torso; a flat dark disc is stuck on the rump. COAT FLOATS: the fur is a uniform criss-cross hatch mesh laid flat across the barrel with no regard to its curvature, and dozens of shaggy strokes detach from the silhouette entirely — free-floating dark spikes under the belly and off the chest, touching nothing. FEET: two-toed dark hooves with white nubs. A bear has plantigrade clawed paws.
rows.fix: Give it a bear chassis: plantigrade paws with visible claws (no hooves), a short deep skull with the muzzle no longer than the skull is deep, and a small rounded ear set BACK on the skull built as a form with a lit near-face and shaded inner bowl — not a flat disc. Paint the cream spectacles as two soft-edged pale masses ringing the eye and running down the cheek toward the chest. Recolour the coat to near-black with warm brown breakup. Kill the white topline rim entirely. Clip every fur stroke to the body mask so nothing floats, and drive stroke direction and length off the surface normal so the hatch wraps the barrel instead of tiling it.

rows.readsAs: an Appaloosa pony, or a spotted deer — a hoofed grazer, not a carnivore
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS 2/3. The topline does NOT slope down to low hips — the back is level and the croup is actually HIGHER than mid-back, a horse's profile; the defining hyena read is absent. There is no massive neck and no heavy jaw: the muzzle is a long shallow duck-bill wedge with a straight ruled mouth-line, the weakest jaw in the batch. Spots and one rounded ear do read. HEAD is the same kit as the bears and the Stoat — the identical hard-rimmed circular ear disc, the identical white-ring eye, the same wedge muzzle; only the spots and the muzzle length differ. SEAMS: a hard bright ridge-line runs straight from withers to rump along the spine, and directly below it a crisp boundary marks where the spotted panel starts — the pattern is a saddle-blanket with an edge. The tail is a pale flat oval clapped over the haunch with a hard rim, with a bristle brush behind it. FEET: dark two-toed hooves on all four legs — fatal on a hyena. COAT: spots are flat black stickers that keep their size and roundness across the belly curve and clump into one amorphous blob at the shoulder; they sit above the surface, not on it.
rows.fix: Rebuild the topline so the withers are the highest point and the hips sit clearly below them, and thicken the neck into the shoulder as one continuous mass. Replace the hooves with four blunt-clawed digitigrade paws. Deepen and shorten the muzzle into a heavy bone-cracking jaw with a defined masseter bulge and a real lower jaw line, not a ruled stroke. Delete the spine highlight and the spotted-panel boundary — distribute spots over the whole flank with size falling off and shape squashing toward the silhouette edge so they read as being on a cylinder. Make the tail grow from the rump instead of overlapping it with an oval.

rows.readsAs: a generic pale antelope or a pronghorn — plausible as an antelope, unidentifiable as a springbok
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS 2/3. There is NO dark chocolate side stripe and no white flank below it — the whole animal is one flat tan; the single most identifying springbok mark is missing. The face is NOT white and has NO dark eye stripe — it is the same tan as the body, unmarked. Horns half-read: two pale prongs that do curve in, but they are smooth and unringed and they sprout from a brown lump between them that reads as a topknot rather than ears. HEAD is generic: identical white-ring eye and identical duck-bill muzzle with the ruled mouth-line as both hyenas; without the horns this head is interchangeable with the Spotted Hyena's. SEAMS — the worst in the batch: the torso is built from visibly straight-edged POLYGONAL panels. A hard trapezoid sits over the shoulder in a darker tan, and a ruled straight line runs from the withers down the back. The body reads as flat cut paper, not a solid. A flat dark circle is pasted on the rump. COAT: no coat at all — the surface is bare gradient fill with faint horizontal banding that ignores the form.
rows.fix: Paint the three marks that make the species: a hard dark chocolate band along the flank from elbow to hip, crisp white below it and on the rump, and a white face with a dark stripe from each eye down to the muzzle corner. Ring the horns with transverse ridges and set them on a skull with real ears BELOW and outside them. Rebuild the torso as one lofted solid — no straight panel edges anywhere on a mammal's body — and derive shading from the surface normal instead of from stacked flat shapes. Remove the pasted rump disc.

rows.readsAs: a dachshund, or a stretched golden retriever — a small dog, not a weasel
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS 1/3, half-reads another. Long tubular body and long neck are the one clear success. The tail is NOT black-tipped: the tip is medium brown, only a shade or two darker than the tail itself, invisible at thumbnail size — the species' name-feature does not register. Legs are acceptably short. HEAD is the stock kit again — the same hard-rimmed circular ear disc, the same white-ring eye, the same tapered muzzle as the bears and hyenas; there is nothing mustelid about it (no blunt triangular head, no rounded low-set ears, no dark nose button). SEAMS: the tail base is a distinctly darker orange wedge that meets the pale body at a hard vertical colour boundary — the tail is stuck on, not grown. The rump is cut off as a straight-edged wedge and the belly line is an angular polyline of straight facets. The shoulder and haunch are two airbrushed brown blur-discs sitting on top of the surface rather than masses inside it. FEET: dark two-toed hooves. On a mustelid that alone kills the read.
rows.fix: Make the tail tip genuinely BLACK and give it a hard boundary at the tip, not at the base — then blend the base into the rump colour so it grows out. Replace hooves with five-toed pink-brown paws. Rebuild the head as a flat wedge skull with small low rounded ears set wide, a dark nose pad, and eyes as small dark beads without the white ring. Smooth the belly and rump silhouette into continuous curves — no facets on a weasel. Replace the blur-disc shoulder and haunch with lit-and-shaded volumes that read through the coat.

rows.readsAs: a zebra foal or a small striped pony, crossed with a rabbit — the ears and the hooves both point away from hyena
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS 3/3. The back does NOT slope steeply down — the topline is level to slightly rump-high, and the front legs are not longer than the hind. There is NO erect crest of mane along the spine; the spine is bare, the only bristles in the picture are on the tail. The ears are large but ROUNDED teardrops, not pointed, and the muzzle is a long shallow duck-bill, not a heavy blunt one. HEAD is the batch's worst construction: two identical leaf-shaped ears overlap in a Mickey-Mouse/heart cluster floating above the skull with their own outline, and the stripes on the face are a hard-edged axis-aligned dark RECTANGLE laid across the skull and muzzle with ruled straight top and bottom edges and comb teeth hanging off it — a flat decal, visibly clipped to a rectangle. The same twin-teardrop ear pair is used verbatim on the Sugar Glider in this batch. SEAMS/ARTIFACTS: a second hard-edged dark RECTANGLE sits in the mid-flank with straight sides. The tail base is the same pale flat oval clapped over the haunch. FEET: dark two-toed hooves. COAT FLOATS: the flank 'stripes' are a radiating spray of tapered strokes fanning from one point — they read as a fern frond or palm leaf pinned to the side of the animal, not as vertical bands wrapping a ribcage.
rows.fix: Fix the topline first — it is the stated defining read: raise the withers, drop the hips, lengthen the forelegs relative to the hind. Add the dorsal crest as erect hair standing off the spine from nape to rump. Clip the stripe generator to the body mask and stop it producing rectangles — draw stripes as roughly vertical bands that follow the ribcage's curvature and bend with it, not as a radial fan. Separate the two ears, point their tips, set them at different depths with the far ear darker. Deepen the muzzle into a heavy blunt jaw. Replace hooves with clawed paws.

rows.readsAs: a tiny white goat or pony standing on the ground — it is not identifiable as an arboreal marsupial at any size
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS 2/3 and the posture spec fails outright. The reference says posture 'flying'; this is a four-square standing quadruped with hooves. There is NO patagium — no membrane between wrist and ankle, nothing gliding, the defining anatomy of the species is entirely absent. The eyes are NOT huge black orbs — they are the same small white-ring dots used on every other animal in the batch, set in a dark face patch. The tail is NOT as long as the body and NOT bushy fur: it is roughly half body length and rendered as a hard-edged fan of straight spikes that reads as a bottle brush or a shell. The dark facial stripe is the only mustRead element that lands. HEAD is not unique: the twin-teardrop ear pair is pixel-for-pixel the same construct as the Striped Hyena's, and the muzzle is the same wedge. SEAMS: a hard straight edge runs along the top of the back where the pale grey panel meets the neck; the tail base is a pale flat disc stuck over the rump with a bright white blob artifact at its tip; the shoulder and haunch are two grey blur-discs floating on the surface. FEET: dark hooves — on an animal whose whole identity is gripping hands.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pose as a glide: limbs splayed to the four corners, body flattened toward the viewer, and the patagium as a continuous taut membrane spanning wrist to ankle on both sides with the limb bones showing through it. Blow the eyes up to occupy a large fraction of the face and make them solid black with one specular dot — no white ring. Replace hooves with small five-fingered grasping hands with visible digits. Rebuild the tail at full body length as soft layered fur with a broken silhouette, not radial spikes, and blend its base into the rump instead of capping it with a disc.

rows.readsAs: a dark grey sheep or a hornless ram — the last thing a stranger would say is 'the smallest bear'
rows.defect: mustRead FAILS 3/3. There is NO golden-cream crescent on the chest — the chest is plain dark grey, nothing there at all. The coat is not short, sleek and jet-black: it is mid-grey with a uniform horizontal wavy hatch that reads as corduroy or knitwear. There are no long curved climbing claws — the feet are dark hoof caps with a tiny white nub. The blunt short muzzle half-reads but the skull is generic. HEAD is a straight recolour of the Spectacled Bear's in this same batch — same rounded skull, same hard-rimmed circular ear disc in the same position, same white-ring eye, same nose nub, same thin curved mouth-line. Cover the bodies and no one could tell them apart. SEAMS: the pale grey coat is a cut-out BLANKET with a crisp continuous outline visible running from the withers, down behind the shoulder, along the belly and around the haunch — the coat is stuck on top of the torso rather than being its surface. The dark neck meets that panel at a hard edge at the shoulder. A bright white rim-line runs along the topline. A flat dark circle is pasted on the rump. COAT FLOATS: the hatch runs in uniform horizontal bands ignoring the barrel's curvature and the haunch's mass entirely.
rows.fix: Paint the chest crescent — a bold golden-cream U high on the chest is the single feature that names this species, and it is worth more than everything else on the list. Recolour to genuine jet-black with sheen highlights rather than grey hatch, and let loose skin folds break the silhouette at the neck and shoulder. Give it long pale curved claws extending past the toes on all four feet. Differentiate the skull from the Spectacled Bear: shorter, wider, with a broader muzzle and small ears set low and wide. Dissolve the blanket boundary so coat colour transitions are soft and driven by the form, delete the white topline rim and the rump disc.

rows.readsAs: A grey pig-tapir with two pale bicycle handlebars pasted across its face
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL — 'enormous swept-back crescent horns' is not in the pixels: the horns are two cream tubes that spring from mid-face and curl FORWARD and DOWN into near-closed rings over the cheek and muzzle, occluding the entire face. The face carries NO eye at all (verified at 8x). 'Broad flat wet muzzle' also fails — the snout ends in a plain rounded lump with no nose disc or nostrils. Ears are dark upright deer-almonds. SEAMS: an untextured pale plank runs along the top of the back with a hard edge and stops abruptly at the withers; the shoulder and haunch are flat untextured dark discs sitting on an otherwise contour-hatched coat, so the shading floats while the coat is mapped; the tail root is a polygon cut into the rump with a straight edge. Body reads mid-weight, not massive — the belly scallops into two lobes and the legs are thin sticks.
rows.fix: Rebuild the horns from the top of the skull: a heavy triangular base at the poll, sweeping out and BACK in a flat crescent that stays behind the eye line and never crosses the muzzle. Add the eye (buffalo eye sits low and wide on the skull, forward of the ear). Terminate the muzzle in a broad flat wet nose plate with visible nostrils, wider than the jaw. Drop the ears to horizontal droop below the horn base. Delete the spine plank and let the dorsal highlight be a soft gradient; make the shoulder/haunch masses carry the same hatch as the flank so they read as form, not decals.

rows.readsAs: A small tan short-coated dog, or a ferret-dachshund toy
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL — 'very short legs': the legs are long, the belly clears the ground by more than a full leg width, and the animal stands like a terrier. mustRead PARTIAL — 'extremely long tube-like body': the torso plank is roughly 4:1 but the creature overall measures 183x97 px in a 440 box (1.9:1) and is rendered undersized in frame, so it never reads long; the note's arch is absent, the back is dead straight. mustRead WEAK — 'small flat rounded ears': one flat brown disc on the crown that reads as a patch or a hole, and only one is drawn. SEAMS: a pale hard-edged spine strip runs the full back; the torso is a straight-sided slab with no shoulder or haunch swelling (the haunches are faint airbrush smudges, not solids); the feet are open-ended tubes showing an elliptical pipe mouth. The tail is a dark nub with no length.
rows.fix: Halve the leg length so the belly nearly grazes the ground and drop the chest between the elbows. Arch the spine into a low hump and extend the body ~40% so the silhouette reads 4:1 including head. Give it a real tail: at least a third of body length, tapering, dark-tipped. Model both ears as small rounded flaps with a rim and inner shadow set low on the skull. Close the foot tubes with a pad and toes. Kill the spine strip and build the shoulder/haunch as actual swellings in the torso solid.

rows.readsAs: A pale gazelle or a donkey-deer hybrid with rabbit ears
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL — 'erect short mane': verified at 6x, the neck crest is completely bare and smooth, no mane of any kind. Ears and the bare-topped tufted tail do read. HEAD: this is the same skull as Wild Horse, Wild Pig and Wild Pony — same long taper, same hairline mouth stroke running halfway back the jaw, same tiny comma nostril, same white-ring eye — only the ear length differs, so it is fully swappable within the batch. The eye is also drawn ON TOP of the ear fill instead of on the skull, a z-order error. SEAMS: the neck is a separate tube plugged into the withers with a visible notch at its base; the back plank ends in a sharp straight diagonal; the head lump's silhouette crosses the neck as an overlap contour; the shoulder and haunch are two radial-gradient domes that bulge BELOW the belly line as separate lobes rather than swelling within the barrel.
rows.fix: Add the erect brush mane: short stiff hairs standing straight up along the whole crest from poll to withers, no fall. Move the eye onto the skull, forward of and below the ear root, and draw the ears behind the eye. Differentiate the skull from the horse: give the ass a straighter, narrower nasal bone, a heavier lower jaw angle, and a distinctly grey/white muzzle ring. Fair the neck cylinder into the chest with a continuous contour instead of a plugged tube, and pull the haunch/shoulder domes back inside the belly silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A shaggy brown pig with a dinner fork stuck in its nose
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL — 'upward-curving tusks from the lower jaw': the tusks are two straight vertical white blades planted on TOP of the snout behind the nose disc, pointing dead up, with no curve and no jaw origin. mustRead FAIL — 'high shoulder hump sloping down to a low rump': the topline is essentially level, and the rump carries a dark round disc rather than dropping away. mustRead PARTIAL — 'bristly mane along the spine': bristles exist but are sprayed around the ENTIRE outline including belly, chest and rump, reading as straw stuck to the animal rather than a dorsal crest. No ear reads at all; the dark round disc on the cheek with the tiny eye at its rim reads as an eye socket. SEAMS: a hard-edged pale quadrilateral panel with straight sides covers the whole flank like a saddle blanket; a bright white hairline runs the spine; a hard straight break at the neck/shoulder. Coat floats — bristles cross over the flank panel in random directions ignoring the body's curve.
rows.fix: Re-root the tusks at the lower jaw corner, emerging below the mouth line and curving up and back outside the muzzle; add the smaller upper tusk behind them. Rebuild the topline as a genuine wedge: withers well above the rump with a continuous downward slope. Confine the bristle crest to a band along the spine and shoulders only, and delete the belly/rump halo. Add upright triangular ears with tufted rims. Remove the flank panel and the spine hairline entirely; let the flank read as one continuous solid with the hatch following its curvature.

rows.readsAs: A slim tan foal or a young deer
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL — 'stiff upright brush mane with no forelock': the neck crest is smooth and bare; the only brush in the picture is on the tail. mustRead FAIL — 'stocky barrel body on short legs': the legs are long and thin and the barrel is shallow — this is exactly the slender riding-horse build the note forbids. mustRead FAIL — 'large heavy head': the head is small and delicate. The dun coat is there but the dark dorsal stripe is not. HEAD: identical construction to Wild Ass — same skull outline, same mouth hairline, same nostril tick, same white-ring eye placed on top of the ear — with only ear length changed. Fully swappable. SEAMS: hard-edged pale plank along the spine; a hard vertical panel boundary at the shoulder; the shoulder and haunch are two radial-gradient domes that hang below the belly line as separate balls, giving the underside an udder-like double-lobe silhouette.
rows.fix: Add the erect Przewalski mane: a short stiff black brush standing up the whole crest, no forelock, and paint the dark dorsal stripe from withers to tail. Shorten the legs by ~25% and deepen the barrel so the body depth exceeds the leg length. Enlarge the head and thicken the jaw and muzzle. Merge the shoulder/haunch domes into the torso solid so the belly reads as one continuous curve, and delete the spine plank and shoulder panel edge.

rows.readsAs: A grey-brown pony wearing a pig's nose
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL — 'short upward-curving tusks': absent entirely, verified at 5x. mustRead FAIL — 'long wedge snout ending in a flat disc nose': the dark nose oval sits on the SIDE of the muzzle, mid-face, and the muzzle continues past it — the snout does not terminate in the disc. mustRead FAIL — 'high shoulder hump with a bristly crest mane': the topline is level and the bristles ring the entire silhouette (belly, chest, rump) instead of forming a dorsal crest. HEAD: this is the equid head — the same heart-shaped dark ear pair, the same white-ring eye, the same tapered muzzle as Wild Horse and Wild Pony, only recoloured. Nothing suid about it. SEAMS: clear stair-step right-angle notches where the neck meets the shoulder (two visible square steps); a hard-edged flank panel; a pale spine strip.
rows.fix: Put the nose disc flat on the END of the snout, facing forward, and lengthen the snout into a true wedge with a straight dorsal profile. Add short upward-curving tusks at the lower jaw corner. Replace the heart ears with small upright triangular pig ears set wide and low. Build the shoulder hump so the topline drops to the rump. Restrict bristles to a spine crest. Fix the neck-to-shoulder join — the stair-step notches must be faired into one continuous contour.

rows.readsAs: The Wild Horse in a straw coat
rows.defect: mustRead FAIL — 'thick shaggy mane and forelock over the eyes': there is no forelock at all, the eye is fully exposed, and the neck crest itself is bare; the shag is scattered over the whole outline — jaw, throat, chest, belly, rump — so it reads as straw stuck to the animal, not a mane. mustRead PASS-ish — the deep barrel on shorter legs roughly reads. mustRead WEAK — the head is small but the forehead is not broad. HEAD: same heart ears, same white-ring eye, same nose oval on the side of a tapered muzzle as Wild Horse and Wild Pig; swap them and no one would notice. SEAMS: a bright white hard hairline runs the length of the spine; a visible notch/corner where the neck meets the shoulder; the haunches are radial domes bulging below the belly line. COAT FLOATS — the fur is drawn as opaque straight sticks laid across the flank in random directions, not wrapping or shading with the form, and they cross over the flank's own boundary.
rows.fix: Give it the actual pony read: a thick mane falling down ONE side of the neck and a heavy forelock hanging over and partly covering the eye. Confine the shag to mane, tail, jaw-line and belly fringe; delete the rump and chest spray. Re-draw fur strokes so they follow the surface flow — curving over the barrel and haunch, darkening in the shadowed lower half — instead of straight sticks at random angles. Broaden the forehead and shorten the muzzle so the head differs from Wild Horse's at a glance. Remove the white spine hairline and fair the neck-shoulder notch.

rows.readsAs: A pale straw-stuffed llama or shorn alpaca with a beige hoop laid across its face — the hoop reads as a bit/bridle, not a horn.
rows.defect: MUSTREAD FAIL - horns. There are no massive spiralling horns beside the head.
