What is drawn is a single flat ribbon in a U/C shape, in almost exactly the head's own body tone (low contrast, nearly invisible), painted ACROSS the cheek and muzzle in front of the eye, plus a small hooked stub in front of the nose. It reads as a mouth-hoop. MUSTREAD FAIL - coat: 'short coarse hair' is rendered as long straw spikes that radiate well past the silhouette along the neck, back, chest and belly, and they cross over the legs. The coat is floating, not lying on the form. MUSTREAD partial - body: not blocky/muscular; it is a soft sack with two airbrushed ellipses (shoulder, haunch) sitting on top of it as gradient discs, on thin pale sticks. SEAM: a hard pale line runs the full length of the spine, separating the back from the body silhouette. A dark round disc with drip artifacts is stuck on the rump where the tail should be. HEAD: the head is the same stamp as Yak and Wildebeest - one huge featureless dark-brown ellipse eye (no iris, no pupil, just a blob) high on a rounded skull, with a pale ribbon hoop laid over the top. Swap it with the Yak's and nobody would notice.
rows.fix: Build the horn as a real 3D spiral: two segmented tapering cones rooted at the top-back of the skull, sweeping down BEHIND and BESIDE the cheek and forward past the jaw, keratin-ringed, in a tone 25-35% darker than the face so they read against it. Never draw horn across the muzzle. Replace the straw-spike coat with short directional hair strokes clipped INSIDE the body silhouette and shaded by the torso solid. Kill the spine highlight line. Give the sheep a Roman-nosed convex muzzle and a small almond eye with a horizontal pupil - that alone would separate it from the Yak.

rows.readsAs: A thylacine, or a young striped deer — long-legged, tuck-waisted, walking on cloven hooves.
rows.defect: MUSTREAD FAIL - tail. The tail is a fat club with three irregular brown BLOTCHES down one side, not rings, and the tip is pale, not black. MUSTREAD FAIL - head: it is not broad. It is a narrow tapering wedge with a long pointed dark-tipped muzzle; the tabby stripes are on the torso only, the face is unstriped. MUSTREAD FAIL - build: this reads lighter and leggier than a house cat, not heavier. The legs are long, straight, thin dowels and the feet are cut cylinders with two ellipse toe-caps - a cloven hoof, not a padded paw with a soft toe spread. FOOT TYPE IS WRONG FOR THE FAMILY. SEAM: a hard dark line runs along the top of the back and continues into the neck. COAT: the stripes are flat black spikes radiating from the spine, drawn on top of the barrel with no wrap - they do not compress toward the belly or bend around the shoulder, so the pattern floats. HEAD: the dark round ear-patch + tiny white cartoon eye with a black dot pupil + tapering muzzle with a bead nose is IDENTICAL to Wolverine and Wombat in this same batch.
rows.fix: Shorten the legs by ~35% and drop the chest so the body sits low; a cat's elbow is near the bottom of the ribcage. Replace the cut-cylinder foot with a rounded paw: broad pad ellipse with 3-4 short toe bumps and no visible cylinder end. Rebuild the tail as an even-thickness cylinder with 4-5 CLEAN full-width dark bands and a solid black terminal third. Widen the skull across the cheeks, shorten the muzzle to about a third of head length, add the two tabby cheek streaks and an M on the forehead, and move the eye forward and up so it is large and forward-facing - that is what makes a cat head.

rows.readsAs: A grey donkey-zebra hybrid wearing two beige door handles on its face, with a fern leaf pasted on its shoulder.
rows.defect: MUSTREAD FAIL - no shaggy chin beard and no neck mane anywhere; the throat is bare grey. MUSTREAD FAIL - head is not heavy or boxy or cow-like; it is a rounded flat oval blob with no distinguishable muzzle, plane change, or jaw. The horns are two flat closed-ish pale RINGS laid over the front of the face; one of them passes directly over the top of the eye. That is a decal, not a horn. Wildebeest horns hook out sideways then up from the crown - nothing here goes sideways. ARTIFACT: the flank marking is literally a FERN FROND - a central rachis with paired pinnae angling off it - plus a hard-edged dark triangular shard at the point of the shoulder. That is plant geometry on a mammal. COAT: the frond is drawn flat with straight cut edges that ignore the barrel; it does not wrap. SEAMS: a hard straight-edged wedge where the hind leg meets the rump, and a flat grey block break at the hip. Feet are two-toe cut cylinders. HEAD: same stamp as Yak and Wild Sheep - one big featureless dark ellipse eye plus the pale ribbon hoop; the only difference is a few dark bars across the skull.
rows.fix: Delete the fern generator from this coat entirely and replace with vertical brindle bars that curve down and forward over the ribs and fade at the belly. Add the two features that ARE the animal: a black hanging chin beard from the jaw to the throat, and an upright bristle mane along the crest of the neck. Rebuild the head as a long deep box - flat frontal plane, square muzzle, eye set high and far back near the horn base. Rebuild horns as solid tapering cones emerging from a boss on the crown, out to the side then hooking up; nothing may cross the eye. Blend the hind-leg root into the haunch mass instead of butting a wedge against it.

rows.readsAs: A grey fox-anteater on hooves — long thin snout, rounded rabbit ears, and a spiky white-tipped zebra tail held up in the air.
rows.defect: MUSTREAD FAIL - head. It is the opposite of broad and blocky: a narrow tapering wedge with a very long, thin, downward-angled snout that reads anteater/opossum. The ears are two rounded ovals set side by side and slightly splayed, not erect triangles. MUSTREAD FAIL - tail. This is a thin spiky black brush with a WHITE BALL at the tip, carried angled UP and back. It is not bushy, it is not straight, it is not level or low - and it is the exact same tail asset as Wildebeest, Yak and Wolverine in this batch. MUSTREAD partial - the legs are long but the chest is shallow and flat-sided, not narrow-and-deep. SEAM (blocker): at 6x, a hard straight diagonal crease runs from the withers down across the shoulder where the neck wedge meets the torso, and a hard horizontal line runs along the top of the back into it. The scapula is a crisp-edged grey polygon with an arc boundary. Feet are blunt cut cylinders with visible elliptical end caps - pipe ends, not paws. COAT: there is no fur at all; the body is flat grey with two soft airbrushed radial ellipses (shoulder and haunch) floating on the surface as gradient discs. The head IS distinguishable from the others in this batch, but it is distinguishable as the wrong animal.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail: a single thick tapered mass, widest at mid-length, hanging down and back below the level of the spine, with fur silhouette bumps on the outline instead of stuck-on bristles - and give the wolf its OWN tail, not the shared bovid brush with a white ball. Widen the skull across the zygomatics, cut the snout length by a third and give it depth (a jaw line, not a spike), and make the ears tall isoceles triangles with a forward-facing opening. Fix the shoulder seam by extending the torso solid up into the neck and shading across the join, rather than overlaying a neck wedge. Replace the pipe feet with four-toed paws. Add short guard-hair texture that follows the body curvature and darkens over the back.

rows.readsAs: A mangy brown dog or a young hyena on stilts, coated in loose straw, with a white-tipped tail held out behind it.
rows.defect: MUSTREAD FAIL - no pale flank stripe. There is no light band sweeping along either side to the tail; the flank is uniform tan with random dark flecks. That is the wolverine's single most recognisable mark and it is absent. MUSTREAD FAIL - build. There is no humped shoulder and no bear mass. The body is a slim tube on four long thin dowels; note also the reference itself asks for SHORT stout legs and these are the same long legs the Wolf and Wildcat got. MUSTREAD FAIL - tail and paws: the tail is a bare tapered cylinder with a WHITE BALL tip and a sparse bristle fringe (again the shared brush asset), not bushy; the feet are cut cylinders with two ellipse toe caps and no claws at all. COAT: straw spikes radiate past the silhouette on the back, belly and legs and cross over the limbs - floating, not on the body. SEAM: a hard white line along the whole spine, and visible flat cut ends at the top of the leg tubes. HEAD: identical template to Wombat and Wildcat - dark round ear patch, small white cartoon eye with a dot pupil, tapering muzzle, bead nose. Recolour it and it IS the Wombat's head.
rows.fix: Paint the flank stripe as an actual light band that starts behind the shoulder, arcs up over the hip and meets its opposite number at the tail root - it must be a shape, not a shade. Halve the leg length and double their thickness; raise the withers into a real hump so the topline peaks at the shoulder and falls to the hips. Give it plantigrade paws: wide, flat, five short toes with visible curved claws. Rebuild the tail as a dense short cone whose FUR forms the outline. Clip all fur strokes inside the silhouette and shade them by the torso. The head needs a mustelid signature: small round ears set low and wide on a broad flat skull, a short blunt muzzle, and a dark facial mask against the pale forehead.

rows.readsAs: A meerkat's head stuck onto a small tan pig, or a capybara.
rows.defect: MUSTREAD PASS - stout barrel body with no tail, that one is right. MUSTREAD FAIL - snout. The muzzle is a pointed tapering wedge ending in a tiny dark nose bead, with a thin drawn mouth line. A wombat's snout is a broad, blunt, squared-off bare pad nearly as wide as the skull. This is a rodent muzzle. MUSTREAD FAIL - legs: short, yes, but they are straight thin smooth tubes with two-toe cut ends, not bowed, not thick, and with no digging claws. SEAM (blocker): at 6x the head is a distinctly DARKER tan shape whose contour cuts a clean hard-edged step across the shoulder and down the throat, plus a notch step at the back of the skull. The head is unmistakably pasted on top of the body rather than growing out of it. There is also a grey-blue hard line along the top of the back. COAT: there is no coat - the body is a flat tan fill with faint horizontal hatching and one soft airbrushed ellipse on the shoulder. Nothing reads as fur. HEAD: this is the batch's clearest case of the owner's complaint - the same dark round ear patch, the same white cartoon eye with a dot pupil, the same tapering muzzle with a bead nose as Wolverine and Wildcat.
rows.fix: Match the head fill to the body fill and blend the join across the neck with the same shading ramp as the torso, so no contour step survives. Rebuild the skull: wide and low, ears as two small rounded tabs on the corners, and a broad flat rectangular naked rhinarium the width of the muzzle with the eye set small and close beside it. Bow the forelegs outward at the elbow, thicken them to roughly the depth of the body, and give each foot a spread of long flat digging claws. Add a coarse short-fur texture that darkens under the belly and over the haunch so the barrel reads as a solid.

rows.readsAs: A shaggy brown ram or musk-ox with two beige hoops on its face — the closest to right in this batch, but still ram-shaped.
rows.defect: MUSTREAD partial - the hair curtain is there in intent but it renders as separate loose straw spikes that stick out well past the silhouette and stop around mid-leg; it never becomes a continuous skirt reaching the ground, and it crosses over the legs, so it floats rather than hanging from the flank. MUSTREAD PASS - the shoulder hump is present. Head is carried level, not low. MUSTREAD FAIL - tail. It is a fat grey-brown cylinder terminating in a WHITE BALL with a thin bristle fringe - the same shared asset as Wolf, Wolverine and Wildebeest - and it reads as a shaved club, not a long horse-like plume. HORNS: two flat pale ribbon hoops laid over the front of the face; the upper one passes directly OVER the top of the eye, and a stub sprouts from the middle of the cheek. They are surface decals, not structures on the skull. EYE: one huge featureless dark-brown ellipse with a single white glint - no iris, no pupil, and far too large. SEAM: a hard white line along the entire spine, and the tail root is a hard-edged wedge butted against the rump. HEAD: same stamp as Wild Sheep and Wildebeest.
rows.fix: Make the flank hair a single continuous silhouette skirt - extend the body outline itself downward in a ragged hem to just above the hooves, with strand detail INSIDE that shape, and let it occlude the upper leg rather than crossing it. Replace the tail with a thin bare base and a long dense hanging plume of hair reaching the hock; drop the white ball. Rebuild the horns as solid tapering cones rooted at the crown, sweeping out and forward then curving up, never crossing the eye or the muzzle. Shrink the eye to a small dark almond with a visible lid and set it high on the side of a long deep bovid skull. Kill the spine highlight and blend the tail root into the haunch.
